labels.abilities_header: What you can do, and how often:
labels.abilities_ambiguous: More than one of those. Be more specific:
labels.memos_header: MEMOS  -  {count} read off the walls so far
labels.memos_none: You have not stopped to read anything yet. The walls are covered in it.

01.name: Clause 1: Acceptance of Terms
01.clause: By proceeding beyond this point you acknowledge that you have read and understood the following, which you have not.

02.name: Clause 2: Fees and Charges
02.clause: Reasonable administrative costs may be applied at our discretion. Reasonable is defined in Clause 2, which is this one, and defines it as whatever we apply.

03.name: Clause 3: Limitation of Liability
03.clause: Our total liability shall not exceed the amount you have paid us, which is nothing, which is the point of the clause.

04.name: Clause 4: Acceptable Use
04.clause: You agree to conduct yourself acceptably. Acceptable conduct is determined locally, by consensus, by people who have lived here longer than you.

05.name: Clause 5: Data Retention
05.clause: We retain your data for as long as is necessary. Necessity is assessed by us, continuously, and has never yet concluded.

06.name: Clause 6: Intellectual Property
06.clause: All material generated in the course of the arbitration, including your likeness, remains our property in perpetuity throughout the universe.

07.name: Clause 7: Force Majeure
07.clause: Neither party shall be liable for failure to perform due to circumstances beyond reasonable control. Reasonable control has never been defined and will not be.

08.name: Clause 8: Indemnification
08.clause: You agree to indemnify and hold us harmless against all loss arising from your dispute, including loss arising from our conduct of it.

09.name: Clause 9: Severability
09.clause: If any provision is found invalid, the remainder shall continue in full force. Nothing here is load-bearing. That is the point of it.

10.name: Clause 10: Governing Law
10.clause: This agreement is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it is enforced, which is here, and which is us.

11.name: Clause 11: Modification of Terms
11.clause: We may amend these terms at any time. Continued use constitutes acceptance. There is no way to stop using it from where you are standing.

12.name: Clause 12: Termination
12.clause: We may terminate this agreement at any time, for any reason or none, with immediate effect. You may not.

13.name: Clause 13: Entire Agreement
13.clause: This document constitutes the entire agreement between the parties and supersedes all prior understandings. There is nothing else. There was never anything else.

vanguard.name: Vanguard
vanguard.desc: You were a warehouse supervisor. Fourteen years of standing between other people and a forklift has left you structurally sound and slightly deaf. High HP, high armour, and the only person here who can take a hit meant for someone else.
vanguard.style: You absorb. Your job is to be the thing that gets hit, and to still be standing afterwards. Highest health and armour of the four, abilities that pull attacks onto you and halve what lands, and the only class that can take a blow meant for your companion. Slow, heavy, and very hard to finish.

skirmisher.name: Skirmisher
skirmisher.desc: You delivered parcels for a living, which means you have never once been where someone expected you to be. Crits on 19 and 20. Can guarantee an escape from one stalker per floor, which will matter more than you currently think.
skirmisher.style: You reposition. Your job is to be somewhere the fight is not, and to arrive at the moment it is worst for whatever you are hitting. Crits on 19 as well as 20, so you land big hits twice as often as anyone, and you are the only class that can guarantee an escape when a fight turns. Fragile if you stand still.

hexwright.name: Hexwright
hexwright.desc: You read the terms. All of them. Something in Clause 11 read you back. You now spend your own health as a casting resource, which is either genius or the single worst arrangement in this building.
hexwright.style: You convert. Your job is to turn your own health into damage, deliberately, at a rate nobody sensible would accept. The hardest hitter in the building and the easiest to kill: lowest health, no armour bonus, and half your best abilities cost HP to use. Every fight is a bet on ending it first.

advocate.name: Advocate
advocate.desc: You are not a lawyer. You are, however, the kind of person who asks to speak to a manager and then keeps speaking. Debuffs through sheer rhetoric, and can Object once per fight to cancel something a boss was very much counting on.
advocate.style: You argue. Your job is to make the thing in front of you worse at its own job. Debuffs, vulnerabilities and cancellations rather than raw damage, and one ability that shuts down a boss move entirely. Middling numbers, and the only class that wins several encounters in this building without swinging at all.

chest_jammed: "That's seized. You'll have to put your back into it."
chest_rigged: "Wait. Wait. Look at the corner. See it?"
chest_mimic: "That is not a chest. That is a mouth with hinges."
"It's breathing. Chests do not breathe. Step back."
pip.name: Pip
pip.desc: A small tidy thing with too many eyes and a clipboard it does not need. Was a quality inspector. Still is, really.
pip.passive: Inspects chests before you open them.
stabilise: "Up. Up. You are not signed off for this."

grunk.name: Grunk
grunk.desc: A zombie. Deeply apologetic about the whole situation. Was a shift manager, once, and has not fully let go of it.
grunk.passive: Absorbs the first pounce on each floor.
stabilise: Grunk hauls you up, apologising the entire time.

cube.name: The Cube
cube.desc: A small hovering cube. It will not explain itself. It has been asked.
cube.passive: Improves your odds in minigames. Method unclear.
stabilise: The Cube hums. You are standing again. No further information is offered.

bartleby.name: Bartleby
bartleby.desc: A very small dragon with a large opinion of his own wingspan. Fireproof, and quietly furious that nobody has noticed.
bartleby.passive: Fire resistance, and a breath weapon he insists is full-sized.
stabilise: "Get UP. I am not carrying you, I am extremely small."
"Not like this. Not on a Tuesday."

interpose.name: Interpose
interpose.desc: Halve incoming damage for two rounds. Standing in front of things is a skill.

brace.name: Brace
brace.desc: +2 AC for two rounds and heal 1d6.

hostile_takeover.name: Hostile Takeover
hostile_takeover.desc: 2d8 damage plus your Strength, and the target loses its next turn.

slip.name: Slip
slip.desc: Your next escape attempt automatically succeeds.

flurry.name: Flurry
flurry.desc: 3d4 damage plus Dexterity. Fast, messy, effective.

expedite.name: Expedite
expedite.desc: Advantage on your attacks for two rounds.

writeoff.name: Write-Off
writeoff.desc: Spend 2 HP to deal 2d6 plus Intelligence.
flavour: This will hurt us both. Mostly you.

audit.name: Audit
audit.desc: All enemies become vulnerable for three rounds. They take 2 extra damage from everything.

compound_interest.name: Compound Interest
compound_interest.desc: Spend 4 HP. 2d8 damage to every enemy.

objection.name: Objection
objection.desc: Cancel the target's next special ability and weaken it for three rounds.
flavour: I'm going to stop you there.

cross_examine.name: Cross-Examine
cross_examine.desc: 1d8 damage plus Charisma, and the target becomes vulnerable.
flavour: Let's go back to what you said earlier.

class_action.name: Class Action
class_action.desc: 1d10 to every enemy and weakens all of them.
flavour: You're not the only one I've spoken to.
There are twelve of us now.

immovable.name: Immovable
immovable.desc: +2 AC for three rounds and every enemy has to come at you rather than your companion.
flavour: I'm not moving. You'll have to come here.

load_bearing.name: Load Bearing
load_bearing.desc: Halve incoming damage for three rounds and heal 3d6. You are structural now.
flavour: I've had worse off a pallet truck.

redundancy_notice.name: Redundancy Notice
redundancy_notice.desc: 4d10 plus Strength, and the target loses its next turn.

blindside.name: Blindside
blindside.desc: 3d8 plus Dexterity, and advantage on your next two rounds.

cut_and_run.name: Cut and Run
cut_and_run.desc: 2d6 to every enemy, and your next escape is guaranteed.
flavour: Everyone gets one. Then I'm gone.

recorded_delivery.name: Recorded Delivery
recorded_delivery.desc: 5d8 plus Dexterity, and the target takes extra damage from everything for three rounds.

depreciate.name: Depreciate
depreciate.desc: Spend 3 HP. Every enemy becomes vulnerable for four rounds and takes 1d8 now.
flavour: Written down over the useful life.
You are worth less than you were a moment ago.

bad_debt.name: Bad Debt
bad_debt.desc: Spend 6 HP for 4d8 plus Intelligence. The worst exchange rate in the building and worth it.
flavour: I am not expecting to get this back.

total_loss.name: Total Loss
total_loss.desc: Spend 10 HP. 4d8 to every enemy and all of them weakened.
flavour: Nothing here is worth repairing. Including me.

leading_question.name: Leading Question
leading_question.desc: 2d8 plus Charisma, and the target is weakened for three rounds.
flavour: You'd agree with that, wouldn't you.
Isn't it true that you already knew?

discovery.name: Discovery
discovery.desc: Every enemy becomes vulnerable for three rounds, and you heal 3d6 out of sheer momentum.
flavour: I'll take the whole file, thank you.

summary_judgment.name: Summary Judgment
summary_judgment.desc: 5d6 plus Charisma, the target loses its next turn, and its next special ability is cancelled.
flavour: There is no case to answer.
We are not doing the rest of this.

last_line.name: Last Line
last_line.desc: Halve incoming damage and +2 AC for four rounds, and heal 4d8. You are the only thing still between them and everyone else.
flavour: Nobody gets past. Nobody has yet.

structural.name: Structural
structural.desc: Every enemy must come at you for three rounds, +2 AC, and 2d8 to all of them for the trouble.
flavour: I'm the load-bearing one. Come on.

full_stop.name: Full Stop
full_stop.desc: 6d10 plus Strength, and the target loses two turns.

blur.name: Blur
blur.desc: Advantage for four rounds and +2 AC for two. Nobody is quite sure where you are.

hit_and_run.name: Hit and Run
hit_and_run.desc: 4d8 plus Dexterity, and your next escape is guaranteed.
flavour: Sign for it. I'll wait outside.

signed_for.name: Signed For
signed_for.desc: 7d8 plus Dexterity, and the target takes extra damage from everything for four rounds.

liquidate.name: Liquidate
liquidate.desc: Spend 6 HP. 3d8 to everything, and everything vulnerable for three rounds.

short_position.name: Short Position
short_position.desc: Spend 10 HP for 6d8 plus Intelligence. You are betting against yourself and winning.
flavour: This settles badly for both of us. Sooner for you.

write_down_all.name: Write Down
write_down_all.desc: Spend 16 HP. 5d10 to every enemy and all of them weakened. The largest single loss in the building.
flavour: Nothing here is worth carrying forward.

no_case.name: No Case to Answer
no_case.desc: Every enemy weakened for four rounds and vulnerable for three. There is nothing for them to argue.
flavour: On what basis? On what basis exactly?

without_prejudice.name: Without Prejudice
without_prejudice.desc: 4d8 plus Charisma, heal 4d6, and cancel the target's next special.

final_submission.name: Final Submission
final_submission.desc: 6d8 plus Charisma, the target loses two turns, and 2d8 to everything else.
flavour: That is the whole of my case and I am finished.

fire_axe.name: fire axe
fire_axe.desc: Break glass in emergency. You did. 1d10, Strength.

letter_opener.name: letter opener
letter_opener.desc: Absurdly sharp for what it is. 1d6+1, Dexterity.

stylus.name: signing stylus
stylus.desc: It signed you up. It can sign things out. 1d6, Intelligence.

mop.name: janitor's mop
mop.desc: Heavier than it should be. Somebody kept it in very good condition. 1d8, Strength.
mop.found: Somebody looked after this. That is somehow the sad part.

stapler.name: industrial stapler
stapler.desc: Rated for eighty sheets. It has been used for other things. 2d4, Dexterity.
stapler.found: It is still loaded. That is not reassuring.

hi_vis.name: hi-vis vest
hi_vis.desc: +2 AC. Nothing in this building will hit a man in a hi-vis vest without checking first.

courier_jacket.name: courier jacket
courier_jacket.desc: +1 AC. Waterproof, pocketed, faintly smells of somebody else's dinner.

lanyard.name: visitor lanyard
lanyard.desc: +0 AC. Purely psychological. Surprisingly effective anyway.

good_suit.name: the good suit
good_suit.desc: +1 AC. You wore this to a funeral and an interview. It has seen you at your most persuasive.

ppe_vest.name: management-grade PPE
ppe_vest.desc: +3 AC. Reinforced, fitted, and clearly never worn on an actual floor.
ppe_vest.found: Still has the tag on it.

ration.name: meal-kit bar
ration.desc: From the subscription that started all this. Heals 2d4+2.
found: The exact product that ruined your life. It is fine. It is genuinely fine.
Chalky. Nutritionally complete. Deeply upsetting in context.

vending_coffee.name: vending machine coffee
vending_coffee.found: It is somehow still hot. Nobody has been here in years.

smoke_canister.name: smoke canister
smoke_canister.desc: +2 AC for three rounds and a lot of coughing.

chargeback_scroll.name: notice of chargeback
chargeback_scroll.desc: Advantage on attacks for two rounds. Legally intimidating.

adrenaline.name: emergency adrenaline
adrenaline.found: There were six brackets on that wall. One auto-injector.

audit_trail.name: The Audit Trail
audit_trail.desc: A cracked handheld unit that logs where you have been. Type MAP to read it.
audit_trail.found: It powers up immediately and displays the last ten rooms you walked through. It has been recording since you arrived. Nobody asked it to.
audit_trail.use: The screen flickers and catches up with itself.

settlement_chit.name: settlement chit
settlement_chit.desc: Redeemable against a claim you have not yet made. Keep it.
settlement_chit.offer:
You still have the settlement chit. Redeemable against a claim you have not yet made — and you have just made one.

Spend it and sit down again? [yes/no]
settlement_chit.spent:
You put the chit on the table. It is taken without comment, the way a thing is taken when it was always going to be.

Again, then.

business_card.name: your own business card
business_card.desc: Your old job. Your old name for yourself. Weightless and heavy.

pressed_card.name: the card, pressed
pressed_card.desc: Carried so long it has taken the shape of you. The old job is worn off it and the edge is not. You hold it the way you hold something you have decided about.

own_merch.name: official arbitration merchandise
own_merch.desc: A mug with your face on it. Takes a slot. Worth nothing. You are keeping it.
found: Your face, printed slightly wrong, on a mug. The licensing is airtight.
A keyring. Of you. Mid-scream. It is selling well.

greeter_badge.name: The Greeter's name badge
greeter_badge.desc: HELLO MY NAME IS and then thirty years of scratched-out attempts.
greeter_badge.found: Under all the scratching there is one name written very carefully, once.

laminate.name: laminated notice
laminate.desc: Unreadable. Indestructible. You cannot bring yourself to drop it.
found: The text has faded to nothing under the plastic. The plastic is immaculate.
You cannot read it and you cannot destroy it, so you keep it.

cut_laminate.name: the laminate, cut
cut_laminate.desc: The machine took the unreadable notice and gave it an edge. Still unreadable. Still indestructible. Now it is shaped like something you swing.

toll_token.name: toll token
toll_token.desc: Brass, heavy, stamped PAID IN FULL. The Coin Diver would not say what it is good for.
toll_token.found: "You'll know when," he says, which is what people say when they don't know either.

crowbar.name: crowbar
crowbar.desc: Somebody breached a wall with this. 1d12, Strength.
crowbar.found: There is brick dust in the claw. It has been used recently, and hard.

coin_gauntlet.name: coin gauntlet
coin_gauntlet.desc: Forty thousand coins fused into the shape of a fist. 2d6, Strength.
coin_gauntlet.found: It is exactly as heavy as it looks and considerably more satisfying.

waders.name: chest waders
waders.desc: +3 AC. Dry legs, for the first time in hours.
waders.found: Your size. Everything down here is your size.

receipt_coat.name: coat of receipts
receipt_coat.desc: +2 AC. Layered, laminated, and weirdly effective.
receipt_coat.found: Every receipt is yours. Some are for things you have not bought yet.

grease.name: channel grease
grease.desc: Advantage on attacks for three rounds. Do not ask what it is.

sump_water.name: bottled sump water
sump_water.found: Clear. Cold. Labelled in handwriting: IT'S FINE, I CHECKED.

ledger_page.name: a page from the ledger
ledger_page.desc: One page, torn from something enormous. It lists eleven names and then a twelfth, added later, in different ink. The twelfth is yours.
ledger_page.found: The other ten are crossed out. Not scored through. Crossed out neatly, one line, the way you mark something completed.

extended_log.name: The Extended Log
extended_log.desc: A second unit, cabled to the first. Doubles how far back your path is recorded. Type MAP.
extended_log.found: He hands it over without ceremony. "Found it in a bag on floor nine. Nobody claimed it. Nobody was going to."
extended_log.use: The two units sync. The trail runs back twice as far as it did.

excess_clause.name: the excess clause
excess_clause.desc: One paragraph, torn out clean. It is the paragraph that says the limit does not apply.
excess_clause.found: "It was always there," she says. "It's just at the back. Everything that helps you is at the back."

actuary_pen.name: actuary's pen
actuary_pen.desc: Heavier than a pen has cause to be. 2d6+2, Intelligence.
actuary_pen.found: It has been used to write one number, many thousands of times.

loss_ledger.name: loss ledger
loss_ledger.desc: +4 AC. Held across the chest, it stops most things. It has stopped things before.
loss_ledger.found: Something went into this ledger about two inches and stopped.

secateurs.name: secateurs
secateurs.found: Cleaned after every use. Every single use.

gardening_gloves.name: gardening gloves
gardening_gloves.desc: +4 AC. Reinforced far past what gardening requires.
gardening_gloves.found: Your size, of course. There is a name inked inside the cuff and it has been crossed out and replaced four times.

casserole.name: a casserole
casserole.desc: Still warm, in a dish with a name taped to the bottom. Heals 5d4+5.
casserole.found: Somebody left this on a doorstep for somebody. The tape says a name and a date, and the date is tomorrow.

cold_tea.name: cold tea
cold_tea.found: Somebody made this the way you would make it for a person you liked, and then was called away, and never came back for it.

policy_wording.name: policy wording
policy_wording.desc: +2 AC for four rounds. Reading it aloud slows almost anything down.

hensley_keys.name: the keys to number 14
hensley_keys.desc: House keys on a ring with a plastic tag. The tag says WELCOME.
hensley_keys.found: There is a fifth key on the ring that does not fit any door on this floor.

parity_disk.name: the parity disk
parity_disk.desc: One disk out of six, warm, still spinning. Without it RAID-6 cannot rebuild.
parity_disk.found: The Backup was not guarding this. It was carrying it, which is different, and you think it may have wanted somebody to have it.

tape_flail.name: tape flail
tape_flail.desc: Two thousand feet of LTO on a reel handle. 2d8+2, Strength.
tape_flail.found: Somebody made this. Deliberately. In their own time.

rack_plate.name: rack blanking plate
rack_plate.desc: +5 AC. Steel, one rack unit, with a handle riveted on at some point after manufacture.
rack_plate.found: There is a dent in it that is exactly the shape of a rack rail swung hard.

cold_backup.name: cold backup
cold_backup.desc: Heals 6d4+6. A sealed pouch from deep storage, retrieval time forty years.
cold_backup.found: The label has a use-by date on it that has not arrived yet.

root_token.name: root token
root_token.desc: Advantage on attacks for four rounds. Nobody down here should still have one of these.

raid_head.name: a head from RAID-6
raid_head.desc: One array, spun down, still faintly warm. It contains everything the arbitration knew about you, and it is unreadable now.
raid_head.found: You do not know why you are keeping it. You keep it.

signature_pen.name: signature pen
signature_pen.desc: The pen from the model release. 3d6+2, Charisma.
signature_pen.found: It is the pen. It is genuinely the pen.

brand_shield.name: brand shield
brand_shield.desc: +6 AC. A display board bearing an approved version of your face.
brand_shield.found: You are holding your own head in front of you as armour, and it works, and you are going to think about that later.

royalty_cheque.name: royalty cheque
royalty_cheque.desc: Heals 5d6. Made out to you, for an amount, at last.
royalty_cheque.found: The amount is not large. It is not zero either, and zero is what you were expecting.

likeness_rights.name: your likeness rights
likeness_rights.desc: One page, signed back over. Your face is yours again.
likeness_rights.found: Signed and dated by somebody with your handwriting who was not you.

barometer.name: the barometer
barometer.desc: Glass, brass, and permanently falling. 3d8, Intelligence.
barometer.found: The needle is hard against STORMY and the glass is cracked from the inside.

storm_coat.name: storm coat
storm_coat.desc: +7 AC. Oilskin, weighted hem, hood that actually works.
storm_coat.found: Dry inside. It has been through worse than this and it is still dry inside.

eye_of_the_storm.name: the eye
eye_of_the_storm.desc: A minute of nothing at all, bottled. Heals 7d6.
eye_of_the_storm.found: It is completely still and completely quiet and holding it makes your ears pop.

prism.name: the prism
prism.desc: A small heavy wedge of glass. It is where the colour comes from. It is not going to explain itself and neither is anyone else.
prism.found: It catches light that is not in the room and throws it on the wall in a band, and you look at the band for longer than you can account for.

crucible_hammer.name: crucible hammer
crucible_hammer.desc: Foundry-grade, long-handled, head still warm. 4d6+3, Strength.
crucible_hammer.found: The handle has been rewrapped eleven times by eleven different pairs of hands.

slag_plate.name: slag plate
slag_plate.desc: +8 AC. Cooled slag beaten flat and strapped. Ugly and unarguable.
slag_plate.found: It weighs what a debt weighs, which is the joke the foundry has been making for forty years.

quench.name: quench
quench.desc: Heals 8d6. Cold, clean, and the first genuinely good thing in the foundry.
quench.found: Somebody bottled this from the trough and left it where the crews could reach it, and did not put their name on it.

full_disclosure.name: Full Disclosure
full_disclosure.desc: A hand-drawn survey of the whole floor, and every floor after. Type MAP.
full_disclosure.found: Every room, drawn by hand, to scale. Whoever has been ahead of you since Clause 1 stopped long enough to do this properly, and then left it where you would find it.
full_disclosure.use: The survey unfolds. The whole floor is on it, including the parts you have not walked.

indemnity_waiver.name: the indemnity waiver
indemnity_waiver.desc: One page. It says nobody else pays for you from here on.
indemnity_waiver.found: Signed by The Guarantor, in its own hand, at the end, which nobody asked it to do.

severed_half.name: a severed half
severed_half.desc: Half of something that was one thing. Warm on the cut face.
severed_half.found: The cut is perfectly clean and the face of it is warm, and you do not want to think about how recently.

blue_pencil_item.name: the blue pencil
blue_pencil_item.desc: Strikes out the offending part and leaves the rest standing. 4d6+4, Intelligence.
blue_pencil_item.found: Worn down to four inches by forty years of striking things out.

severance_plate.name: severance plate
severance_plate.desc: +9 AC. A wall section with one clean edge and one ragged one.
severance_plate.found: It was load-bearing until this floor decided nothing was.

whole_thing.name: a whole one
whole_thing.desc: Heals 9d6. Complete, uncut, all of it.
whole_thing.found: Nothing on this floor is whole. This is, and that is worth more here than what is in it.

gavel.name: the gavel
gavel.found: The head is worn flat on one side from forty years of the same motion.

court_dress.name: court dress
court_dress.desc: +10 AC. Heavier than it looks and it looks heavy.
court_dress.found: It fits. Nobody has measured you and it fits.

stay_of_execution.name: stay of execution
stay_of_execution.desc: Heals 10d6. A signed order that this does not happen yet.
stay_of_execution.found: Signed, sealed, undated. Somebody left the date blank on purpose.

vorn_seal.name: Vorn's seal
vorn_seal.desc: The court's seal, pressed into wax, on nothing at all. There is no document under it.
vorn_seal.found: A seal with no judgment attached to it. Vorn pressed it and then had nothing to press it onto.

red_pen.name: the red pen
red_pen.found: It has been used on every document in this building including, at least once, on a person.

original_copy.name: the original copy
original_copy.desc: +11 AC. Unamended, and therefore harder than anything derived from it.
original_copy.found: There is one of these. Somebody hid it before the first revision and then never came back.

clean_draft.name: a clean draft
clean_draft.desc: Heals 11d6. No changes marked. Nothing in the margin.
clean_draft.found: No tracked changes, no comments, no queries. Reading it is a physical relief.

unamended_term.name: the unamended term
unamended_term.desc: One clause, in its first wording, before anyone got to it. It says something quite reasonable.
unamended_term.found:
It reads: 'either party may withdraw at any time, without penalty.'

That was Clause 1, once. Before the first amendment. Four billion people accepted the current version.

persistence.name: Persistence
persistence.desc: A length of pipe with tape on the handle. It does 4d8 and it scales off CON, because it does not require skill. 4d8, Constitution.
persistence.found:
There is a note wrapped round the handle in the same careful biro as the walls of every safe room in this building.

It says: I FOUND THIS ROOM THE SAME WAY YOU DID. TOOK ME NINE GOES. YOU MUST BE ANGRIER THAN I WAS.

ash_blade.name: ash blade
ash_blade.desc: Forged from the last pour before shutdown. 6d6+4, Strength.
ash_blade.found: Still warm. It has been still warm for eleven years.

shutter_plate.name: shutter plate
shutter_plate.desc: +12 AC. A security shutter, cut down and strapped.
shutter_plate.found: It came off a door that somebody very badly wanted to keep closed.

last_kettle.name: the last kettle
last_kettle.desc: Heals 12d6. Somebody kept one working. Somebody always keeps one working.
last_kettle.found: Filled, boiled, and left. It is still hot and this floor has been cold for years.

reaper_scale.name: a scale from the Reaper
reaper_scale.desc: Grey, the size of a dinner plate, and covered in text too small to read. Every record it ever ate is written on it.
reaper_scale.found: You hold it to the light. Somewhere on it, in type a fraction of a millimetre high, is your name and the date you clicked Accept.

blank_page.name: a blank page
blank_page.desc: Nothing is written on it. On this floor that makes it the most powerful object available. 7d6+4, Charisma.
blank_page.found: It supersedes all prior understandings, and it says nothing at all, and those two facts turn out to be the same fact.

entire_plate.name: the entire agreement
entire_plate.desc: +13 AC. The whole document, bound flat and worn on the chest. Nothing gets past the whole document.
entire_plate.found: It is not heavy. That is what surprises you.

good_tea.name: a proper cup of tea
good_tea.desc: Heals 13d6. Made by somebody who cared how it came out.
good_tea.found: Two sugars. Nobody has ever asked you how you take it and this is correct.

notice_of_withdrawal.name: a notice of withdrawal
notice_of_withdrawal.desc: Thirteen refusals, one per clause, logged and filed by something that was not supposed to be listening.
notice_of_withdrawal.found: It is stamped. You do not know what stamped it and there is nothing in the room that could have.

harmony.name: the building's harmony
harmony.desc: Nine seconds of every machine in the building agreeing with you. It has not happened before.
harmony.found: You cannot carry a sound. You are carrying it anyway.

the_photograph.name: the photograph
the_photograph.desc: Two people on a mediocre beach. On the back, in biro: I PUT THESE UP SO WHOEVER COMES NEXT KNOWS SOMEBODY GOT THIS FAR.
the_photograph.found: You take this one down and put it in your coat, which is the first thing you have taken from this building that anybody would miss.

the_last_word.name: the last word
the_last_word.desc: Nine seconds of commentary, cut off mid-sentence. It is the only recording of the narrator that exists outside the building.
the_last_word.found: You have no idea how you are carrying this. You are carrying it.

royalty_statement.name: a royalty statement
royalty_statement.desc: Five pieces of merchandise bearing your face, and a statement showing what you are owed for them. The figure is not zero.
royalty_statement.found:
UNITS SOLD: 41,900,112. RATE PAYABLE TO LIKENESS: 0.00%. AMOUNT DUE: 0.00.

Somebody has written underneath, in biro: this is the bit that made me start walking.

the_franchise.name: the franchise
the_franchise.desc: The right to license your own face back to yourself. Use it and everything you sell from here on is worth half again.
the_franchise.found: It is a folder. It is very heavy for a folder.

silent_partner.name: a silent partner
silent_partner.desc: Somebody agrees to be on your side and to never once say anything about it. +1 to every stat, permanently.
silent_partner.found: No name on the paperwork. There is a space for one and it has been deliberately left.

the_deed.name: the deed
the_deed.desc: The deed to one floor of this building. Not a specific one. Use it to restore yourself completely, once.
the_deed.found: You now own a floor of the building you are trying to escape, which is either leverage or a joke at your expense.

second_opinion.name: a second opinion
second_opinion.desc: A written second opinion on your case. Use it to get one more chance if you go down.
second_opinion.found: Signed by somebody who never saw the file and was paid anyway.

hazard_wrap.name: hazard wrap
hazard_wrap.desc: +4 AC. Orange, adhesive, and applied directly to you.
hazard_wrap.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

ledger_binding.name: ledger binding
ledger_binding.desc: +5 AC. Two hundred years of accounts, worn as a chestplate.
ledger_binding.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

dust_sheet.name: dust sheet
dust_sheet.desc: +6 AC. It has covered something valuable for a long time.
dust_sheet.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

mesh_liner.name: mesh liner
mesh_liner.desc: +7 AC. Rated for splash. Not rated for this.
mesh_liner.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

counterweight.name: counterweight
counterweight.desc: +8 AC. It slows you down and stops you going over.
counterweight.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

padded_ledger.name: padded ledger
padded_ledger.desc: +9 AC. Somebody padded a ledger literally, for once.
padded_ledger.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

interleaf.name: interleaf
interleaf.desc: +10 AC. The blank pages between clauses, layered and pressed.
interleaf.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

mirror_backing.name: mirror backing
mirror_backing.desc: +11 AC. Whatever hits you sees itself doing it.
mirror_backing.found: It fits well enough and it is not the same as the last one.

injunction.name: an injunction
injunction.desc: A stop order, granted, sealed and never served. Guarded for 6 rounds.
injunction.found: Somebody won this and then did not use it, which is the saddest document in the building.

without_prejudice.name: a without prejudice letter
without_prejudice.desc: Everything in it can be said and none of it can be held against you. Advantage for 6 rounds.
without_prejudice.found: Marked in red across the top, twice, by somebody who wanted no confusion about it.

standing_order.name: a standing order
standing_order.desc: It keeps happening whether anybody attends to it or not. Guarded for 8 rounds.
standing_order.found: Still in force. Still being honoured. Nobody has been able to find who set it up.

material_change.name: a material change
material_change.desc: The circumstances are different now and everybody has to account for it. Advantage for 8 rounds.
material_change.found: The paper is warm, which paper is not.

costs_order.name: an order as to costs
costs_order.desc: Somebody else is paying. Everything pays 35% more from here.
costs_order.found: The figure has been left blank, which you suspect is the point.

signage.name: Animate Signage
taunt: PLEASE WAIT HERE.
THIS AREA IS MONITORED.
YOUR PATIENCE IS APPRECIATED.
death: {name} delaminates. Thirty years of protective plastic peel back in one long curl, and the notice underneath is finally, briefly readable. It says PLEASE WAIT HERE. Then it isn't readable at all.
{name} folds along a crease that was not there a second ago, and keeps folding, down and down, until what is left could fit in a pocket. You do not put it in your pocket.
You take it corner-first. {name} comes apart into forty smaller signs, each one insisting on something different, all of them wrong.
The board splits down the middle. Both halves land face up. Both still say PLEASE WAIT.

intern.name: Perpetual Intern
taunt: "Is this going to count toward anything?"
"I was told there'd be a review."
"I've been here since the acquisition."
death: {name} sits down. Not dramatically. Just sits down, on the floor, mid-sentence, and does not get up. The lanyard settles last.
You put {name} through a lever-arch file and out the other side. Paper everywhere. Forms nobody will ever process, from a department that no longer exists.
{name} looks at the wound, then at you, then says "is this going to count toward anything" and stops before you can answer.
The clipboard goes one way, {name} goes the other. Somewhere a review meeting is quietly cancelled.

clipboards.name: Clipboard Swarm
taunt: They circle at head height, clicking their clips.
Somewhere in the swarm, a pen is still attached by a chain.
death: The swarm loses cohesion. {name} clatters to the floor in a heap, forty-odd boards and one pen still attached by its chain, swinging.
You catch {name} at the centre of its own spiral. The whole formation snaps outward, embeds itself in four walls, and stops clicking all at once. The silence is worse.
One board at a time, {name} comes apart, and each one lands face down, which somehow feels deliberate.

mascot.name: Vantablack Mascot Suit
taunt: The head is on backwards. It is still watching you.
It waves. It keeps waving. It is closer than it was.
death: The suit deflates. {name} sags, sits, and settles into a shape that is unmistakably empty. It was empty the whole time. The head, still on backwards, rolls to a stop facing you.
You take the head off. There is nothing inside. There has never been anything inside. The arms keep waving for four more seconds.
It goes down in a heap of foam and enthusiasm. The hand is still raised. You have to look away from the hand.
The zip goes. {name} comes apart at the seams, and what comes out is warm air and the smell of a costume worn by nobody for a very long time.

queue.name: The Queue
taunt: It is not moving. It is arriving.
There is no front of it. You have checked.
death: {name} loses its order. The barriers go slack, the rope drops, and half a mile of implied patience unwinds all at once into nothing.
You break {name} somewhere near the middle. It does not have a front, so it does not have anything to fall back on. It simply stops arriving.
The grooves in the floor fill back in. {name} was never people. {name} was the wearing-down.

middle_management.name: Middle Management
taunt: "Have you got a minute?"
"I'm not angry. I just want to understand the process."
"Let's take this offline."
death: {name} circles back one last time, gets halfway through "let's take this", and does not reach the word offline.
You put {name} through the nameplate. It was facing the visitor's chair anyway. Both halves land in the leather seat, which is, on reflection, exactly where it always wanted to be.
{name} asks for a minute. You do not give it one.
The escalation ends. {name} goes down still gesturing at a whiteboard that is not in this room and never was.

the_greeter.name: The Greeter
taunt: "WELCOME! Have you signed in?"
"You'll want to fill this out. Both sides."
"Everyone finds the first day hard."
death:
{name} goes down slowly, the way someone sits after a very long shift.

The welcome pack drops first. Then the badge. Then him, folding onto the blue committee carpet in the bright, bright room, still holding the last biscuit out toward you.

"Everyone finds the first day hard," he says. "You did well."

And then Clause 1 is disputed, and the room is just a room.

You take {name} across the flipchart and both go over together.

He lands amongst forty name badges laid out for forty people who never arrived, and he is still, somehow, pleased. Pleased that someone came. Pleased that someone got this far.

"Sign in on your way down," he says. "It helps with the numbers."

The projector keeps running. It has one slide left.

The handshake ends.

{name} lets go, steps back, straightens the badge that has thirty years of scratched-out names on it, and sits down in the front row like an attendee.

"Twelve more," he says, and sounds sorry about it, and means it. "They won't all be like me."

coin_slick.name: Coin Slick
taunt: It moves like water and lands like money.
Somewhere under it, something metal shifts and settles.
death: The slick loses its shape and becomes what it always was: forty thousand coins and a sewer floor, no longer in agreement about which is which.
It goes flat, all at once, with a sound like a till emptying into a drain. Which is close enough.
You break the surface tension. {name} sluices away down the channel, still trying to add up.

surcharge.name: Surcharge
taunt: "This was always going to be applied."
"It's in the summary. There's a summary."
It is smaller than you expected and it is already behind you.
death: {name} is itemised, disputed, and removed. It comes off the total with a small, satisfying click.
You get it in writing. {name} cannot survive being in writing.
It shrinks. Keeps shrinking. Rounds down to nothing and is gone.

collections.name: Collections
taunt: "We've written to you three times."
"This is not a threat. This is a courtesy."
"We can do this at your convenience or ours."
death: {name} goes down mid-sentence and the sentence keeps going for a second without it, which is the worst part.
You settle the account in full. {name} accepts the settlement and stops, professionally, like a man clocking off.
The last notice falls out of its hand, face up. It is addressed to you. It is dated next Tuesday.

meter.name: The Meter
taunt: The dial has not stopped since you entered the room.
It has already charged you for reading it.
death: The dial spins backwards, fast, all the way past zero, and keeps going into a negative you are pretty sure they will find a way to bill you for.
{name} stops ticking. The silence has a price on it. Everything down here does.
Glass, then springs, then a long unwinding whirr, then nothing.

drowned_customer.name: Drowned Customer
drowned_customer.atk2: the weight of what they carried
taunt: "I only wanted to cancel."
"I did read some of it."
Their pockets are full of coins. Their pockets have always been full of coins.
death:
{name} stops fighting the weight and goes down easily, gratefully, pockets first.

You could empty the pockets. You do not.
The coins go one way and {name} goes the other, and for a second, unburdened, they almost float.
"Thanks," says {name}, which is the only word any of them has managed, and then the channel takes them.

auditor.name: The Auditor
taunt: "I'm not here to catch you out. I'm here to be thorough."
"Walk me through this one again."
"You've kept very poor records of yourself."
death:
{name} closes the folder. Slowly. Puts the pen down beside it, squared to the edge, because even now it will not leave a desk untidy.

Then it falls forward across the count table and does not get up.
You get through {name}'s guard on the third pass and it says, with what sounds like genuine professional respect, "that's the right answer," and stops.
The findings scatter. Two hundred pages, every one of them about you, every one of them accurate. It takes {name} a long time to go down, and it goes down still reading.

the_deductible.name: The Deductible
taunt: "A part of everything. Not all of it. That would be unreasonable."
"You will hardly notice."
It has already taken something. You cannot work out what.
death:
{name} splits along its own excess and both halves take a portion of the other, and that continues, smaller and smaller, until there is nothing left worth taking.

It will re-form. That is what a deductible is. But not today, and not for you.
You pay it in one lump. All of it, at once, more than it can process. {name} chokes on the full amount and comes apart at the toll gate.
The gate arm drops. {name} is under it. For the first time in this building, something has been charged the whole thing.

ledgermaw.name: Ledgermaw
taunt: "NEARLY."
"SO CLOSE."
"ONE MORE."
The reels stop on three different things. It counts that as a win. For itself.
death:
The reels stop.

All three land on the same symbol for the first time in the machine's life, and {name} pays out.

Every fee this building has ever levied comes out of it at once, a solid column of coin roaring across the count room floor, and somewhere in the middle of it the machine's light goes out looking, if anything, relieved.

You do not take any of it. There is nowhere down here to spend it, and you know exactly what it cost.

You get the crowbar into the coin door and open {name} the wrong way.

It makes a noise no machine should make. Then it makes the correct noise, the one it was built for, the one it has never made: a payout. Forty years of it. It goes on for a long time.

When it finishes there is silence and knee-deep money and a way through to the stairs.

actuarial_table.name: Actuarial Table
taunt: It finds your row without looking.
"You are cheaper than you think."
death: The columns collapse into each other and {name} resolves, finally, to a single number. It is lower than you would like.
You tear it along the fold. Both halves disagree about your life expectancy and neither is now in a position to argue.
{name} balances. For one second, every column adds up, and the relief of it destroys the thing entirely.

exclusion.name: Exclusion
taunt: "Not that. Never that."
"Read the second schedule."
death: You find the thing it excludes and hold it up, and {name} cannot be in the same room as its own exception.
It shrinks to a footnote, then to a superscript, then to nothing. Very tidy.
{name} is excluded from the list of things that are covered, which now includes itself, which it does not survive.

small_print.name: Small Print
taunt: It is too small to see and it is already inside your sleeve.
There is more of it than there is of the document.
death: You get it under a light. {name} cannot survive being legible.
Enlarged past six point, it simply stops being binding, and falls apart mid-sentence.
The swarm resolves into one line of text, and the line says something reasonable, and that is the end of it.

claimant.name: The Claimant
taunt: "I have the letters. I kept all of them."
"It was going to be settled last spring."
death:
{name} sets the folder down, carefully, squared to the shelf edge, and then goes down beside it.

The claim is still open. It will be open long after both of you.
The correspondence scatters across the flooded floor and floats, and {name} watches it go with something almost like relief.
"Fine," says {name}, and it is the first time anyone has said that word down here and meant it.

act_of_god.name: Act of God
taunt: The shelving moves. Nobody moved it.
It is not aimed at you. It is simply happening at you.
death: It stops. No reason. Acts of God do not need one to start and they do not need one to stop.
{name} exhausts itself against the archive wall and becomes, retroactively, foreseeable, which finishes it.
The water goes flat. Whatever was moving through it has moved on somewhere else, or into somewhere else, and the difference matters less than you would like.

loss_adjuster.name: The Loss Adjuster
taunt: "I'm here to establish what actually happened."
"You've overstated this. People do. It's not an accusation."
"My figure is my figure."
death: {name} revises the figure one last time, downward, out of habit, and goes down beside its own assessment.
You get past the clipboard on the third exchange. {name} says "that's a fair sum" with what sounds like professional respect, and settles.
The final position turns out to be the floor.

the_cap.name: The Cap
the_cap.atk2: the most this can be worth
taunt: "Whatever you do to me, only so much of it counts."
"You may continue. It will not accumulate."
"This is the maximum. There is always a maximum."
death:
The ceiling comes off.

Everything you have already done to {name} arrives at once, all of it, uncapped and backdated, forty minutes of ignored damage landing in a single second.

It has time to say "that isn't" and does not finish, and Clause 3 goes with it.

{name} exceeds its own limit.

There is a sound like a very large number rolling over, and the archive water drops six inches all at once, and what is left of the aggregate limit settles on the shelves like dust.

Their liability to you is now, formally and in writing, unlimited.

net_curtain.name: Net Curtain
taunt: It moved. You did not see it move.
Somebody was at that window and is not now.
death: {name} comes down off its rail in a heap, and the window behind it is just a window, with nobody at it, which is what it always was.
You get it off the wall. It goes limp immediately, and is only fabric, and was probably only ever fabric.

wheelie_bin.name: Wheelie Bin
wheelie_bin.atk2: put out on the wrong day
taunt: It is out on a day that is not collection day.
The lid is not quite closed.
death: {name} goes over on its side and everything in it comes out, and it is all correctly separated by material, and that is the most frightening thing on this floor.
The wheels give. {name} rolls to the kerb, settles at the exact regulation distance from the wall, and stops.

lawn.name: The Lawn
taunt: Nothing on it is longer than anything else on it.
The stripes go the wrong way and you cannot say why you know that.
death: {name} loses its level. One corner sinks, and the whole thing gives up at once, and by tomorrow it will be a meadow and by Thursday somebody will have complained.
You take it back to the soil. Whatever was under it does not reappear.

caroller.name: Caroller
taunt: They are singing the correct number of verses.
It is not the season. It has not been the season for years.
death: {name} reaches the end of the verse before stopping, because you do not stop mid-verse, and then goes down neatly on the doorstep.
The harmony drops out. The rest of the street keeps going for two more bars without noticing, which is worse.

ice_cream_van.name: The Ice Cream Van
taunt: The chimes are the right tune played at the wrong speed.
It has been on this street since before the houses.
death:
The chimes wind down through four wrong notes and stop.

The hatch is open. There is nobody inside {name}, and there is a scoop resting in a tub of something that has been perfect for forty years.
{name} rolls to a halt against the kerb, and the freezer clicks off, and the whole street goes quiet in a way that suggests it had been listening the entire time.

neighbourhood_watch.name: Neighbourhood Watch
taunt: "We're not accusing anybody of anything."
"We just like to know who's about."
"You're not from Willowmead, are you."
death: The torch goes out. {name} goes down on the verge, and the logbook falls open at today's date, and your description is already in it, timed to the minute you arrived.
You get past the torch. {name} says "I was only" and does not finish, and the sticker in the window behind you peels at one corner.

the_committee.name: The Committee
taunt: "We did circulate this."
"It was minuted. You'd have had a copy if you were on the list."
"Any other business?"
death:
{name} moves to adjourn. There is a seconder. The motion carries, and the hall lights go off in sequence from the back, and nobody is left in the room to stack the chairs.

Somebody stacks the chairs.
You break quorum. Without quorum {name} cannot resolve to do anything at all, including continue existing, and it goes down still trying to establish whether that was in order.

mrs_hensley.name: Mrs Hensley
mrs_hensley.atk1: a quiet word on the step
mrs_hensley.atk2: the full weight of the street
taunt: "I've called Brian. He's just up the road."
"Nobody's angry with you, love. We're only concerned."
"You'll find we're very close here."
death:
The phone goes down in its cradle.

{name} sits on the second step of her own front door, hands in her lap, and the street behind you stops coming.

"That's that then," she says, and she is not being brave about it, she simply thinks it is true. "You'll want the keys. Number 14's been empty since before any of us."

And Clause 4 is disputed, and every curtain on the estate is perfectly still.

You end it in the hallway, under the good light, on the carpet she hoovers on Tuesdays.

{name} goes down between the hall table and the stairs, and the last thing she does is straighten the runner with one hand, because somebody will be coming.

Nobody comes. The street outside is bins out, hedges level, and forty front windows with nobody at any of them.
call: "Brian? It's me. Yes. Now, if you would."
"Sandra, could you pop round. Bring the other two."
"They're still here. No, still. Yes please."

neighbour.name: A Neighbour
taunt: "Ann said you were causing bother."
"I'm not stopping."
death: {name} goes back up the path without being asked, which is somehow the most unsettling exit available.
"Right," says {name}, and sits down on the low wall, and does not get up.

tape_ghoul.name: Tape Ghoul
taunt: It is wearing a lanyard from a company that no longer exists.
"Restore request," it says. "Restore request. Restore request."
death: {name} unspools. Two thousand feet of tape goes across the aisle and settles, and every inch of it is somebody's data, and none of it will ever be read.
You get it at the reel. {name} collapses inward with a noise like a filing cabinet apologising.

orphan_process.name: Orphan Process
taunt: It is still doing a job for a system that was decommissioned.
"Parent?" it asks. "Parent? Parent?"
death:
{name} finds no parent to report to, and having nothing to report to, stops.

It takes a moment. It has been trying for a long time.
You kill the process. It exits cleanly, which after everything is the least it deserved.

retention_policy.name: Retention Policy
taunt: "Necessity is assessed continuously."
"There is no second half of the schedule."
death: {name} concludes. First time in the building's history that anything has concluded, and it takes the whole rack down with it.
The hold is released. Everything {name} was keeping goes at once, and the aisle is suddenly, enormously empty.

cold_storage.name: Cold Storage
taunt: The air off it hurts.
"Retrieval time: forty to sixty years."
death: {name} thaws, all at once, and what comes out of it is water and paper and one very old smell.
You get it open. There is nothing inside {name} but temperature.

undead_sysadmin.name: Undead Sysadmin
taunt: "I'm not on call. I'm not on call. Check the rota."
"Who paged me. Who paged me."
The lanyard says CONTRACTOR and a date.
death: {name} goes down beside the rack it has been maintaining since the acquisition, and the pager on its belt goes off one more time, and nobody answers it.
"Handover," says {name}, and hands you nothing, and stops.

the_backup.name: The Backup
taunt: "Anything you do, I have a copy of me from before you did it."
"This is not a fight. This is a scheduled task."
death:
You do it faster than {name} can rebuild.

The repair falls behind, then further behind, and then there is nothing left to restore from, and the last light on the array goes out on the word COMPLETE.

It drops the parity disk. That was always what it was really guarding.

sysadmin.name: Senior Sysadmin
taunt: "I built this floor. I'm not letting you walk it."
"Twenty-two years. Twenty-two."
"Nobody down here is meant to be awake."
death: {name} performs a clean shutdown of itself, in order, service by service, because it was never going to go out any other way.
You take {name} at the rack door and it says "fair", which is the first honest word on this floor.

raid_six.name: RAID-6
taunt: "DEGRADED. REBUILDING. DEGRADED. REBUILDING."
"YOU CANNOT TAKE ENOUGH OF ME AT ONCE."
"I HAVE SURVIVED WORSE THAN YOU. I HAVE SURVIVED EVERYTHING."
death:
You break parity.

The sixth head goes and there is nothing left to rebuild it from, and RAID-6 works that out at the same moment you do.

"DEGRADED," it says, and then, much more quietly, in a voice that is almost a person's: "unrecoverable."

Every drive in the catacomb spins down together. It takes about forty seconds. It is the quietest the building has ever been, and every record it ever held of you goes with it.

The array fails past its own tolerance.

Six heads is two more than it needs and one fewer than it has, and you have finally taken enough at once that the arithmetic stops working.

RAID-6 spends its last cycle doing the only thing it knows how to do, which is trying to rebuild, from nothing, forever, and then not.

licensing.name: Licensing
taunt: "In perpetuity. Throughout the universe. Standard wording."
"You signed the model release. It was clause six."
death: {name} runs out of territory to enforce in, which takes a while, and then folds.
The licence lapses. Nobody renews it. {name} was only ever the renewal.

plush_you.name: Plush You
taunt: It is you, badly, in fleece.
It squeaks when it moves. It is moving a lot.
death: {name} splits at the seam and what comes out is stuffing and about four hundred paperclips, which raises a question you set down immediately.
You knock the head off. The embroidered face keeps the same expression it had, which was yours, which was never that.

trademark.name: Trademark
taunt: It is a symbol and it is load-bearing.
"Do not use without permission."
death: {name} enters the public domain, seventy years early, and stops being enforceable in the middle of the aisle.
You use it without permission. Repeatedly. {name} cannot survive that.

derivative_work.name: Derivative Work
taunt: It is nearly you. The proportions are off in a way you can feel.
"Based on a true dispute."
death: {name} is found to be substantially similar and comes apart on that basis alone.
The adaptation fails. {name} reverts toward the original, gets most of the way, and stops there, which is the part you will think about later.

cease_and_desist.name: Cease and Desist
taunt: "You are hereby required to stop."
"This letter is not a negotiation."
death: You do not cease. You do not desist. {name} has no second paragraph and goes down on the strength of that.
The demand is refused. {name} had never once been refused and does not have a procedure for it.

the_focus_group.name: The Focus Group
the_focus_group.atk2: a note from the back of the room
taunt: "We didn't warm to them."
"Would you say you're rooting for this person? Be honest."
"Can we get more participants in? Engagement's dropping."
death:
The session overruns. One by one {name} remembers they have to be somewhere, and there is no session without participants, and the glass goes dark.

The last one out leaves the clipboard behind. You read the top sheet. It says, in the box marked GENERAL IMPRESSION: they kept going.
call: "Can we get another one in? Engagement's dropping."

brand_guardian.name: Brand Guardian
taunt: "That is not the approved version of you."
"You are off-brand. You have been off-brand since Clause 1."
"There is a document. There is always a document."
death: {name} goes down defending a version of you that never existed, and defends it right to the end, which is either loyalty or the absence of anything else.
You go decisively off-brand. {name} cannot process the inconsistency and comes apart along the style guide's own fold lines.

the_likeness.name: The Likeness
the_likeness.atk2: the thing you always do third
taunt: "I've seen every fight you've had. All of them. Including the ones you lost."
"You lead with the same thing every time. You know that, don't you."
"I'm not you. I'm the footage."
death:
It runs out of your moves.

That is the whole trick, in the end: it only has what you have already done, and somewhere in the last six floors you started doing something else.

{name} tries the opening move one final time, the one from Intake, the one you have not used since Clause 2, and you are not standing where you used to stand.

"Oh," it says, in your voice, with something that is almost pride in it. "You changed."

And the hall of merchandise goes dark, rack by rack, all the way back to the stairs.

You beat it by being worse than it expected.

{name} has your file, your armour, your best six floors, and no idea what you are going to do next, because neither do you, and that turns out to be the only advantage anyone has ever had down here.

It goes down in your armour, wearing your face, and the face is not angry. It looks, if anything, relieved to stop performing you.

Your likeness reverts. It is a small thing. It is yours.

unforeseen.name: The Unforeseen
taunt: Nobody drafted for this.
It was not in the risk register. Nothing is.
death: {name} becomes, retroactively, foreseeable, and cannot survive that.
You see it coming. That is all it took.

act_of_weather.name: Act of Weather
taunt: The pressure drops and your ears go.
It is weather. Indoors. Fully committed to it.
death: {name} blows itself out against the far wall, the way weather does, having achieved nothing and ruined the afternoon.
The front passes. That is the only way any of these ever end.

beyond_control.name: Beyond Reasonable Control
taunt: "This is not attributable to anyone."
"There is no party at fault here."
death: You attribute it. Specifically, in writing, to a named party. {name} cannot exist inside an attribution.
Somebody turns out to be responsible after all, and {name} goes down under the weight of that.

contingency_plan.name: Contingency Plan
contingency_plan.atk2: the plan for this exact thing
taunt: "We planned for you."
"There is a document. Of course there is a document."
death: The plan does not survive contact. {name} has never had contact before and it does not take it well.
You do the thing the plan did not account for. {name} has no page for it and stops on the spot.

the_forecast.name: The Forecast
taunt: "Eighty percent chance of you not making it."
"Outlook: unchanged. Outlook: unchanged."
death: {name} is wrong. It has never been wrong. It takes it very badly and then it takes it permanently.
The forecast is revised. {name} does not survive the revision, which is the first honest thing it has done.

the_exception.name: The Exception
the_exception.atk2: what the clause does not cover
taunt: "I am the part that makes the rest of it legal."
"Without me, Clause 7 is unenforceable. With me, it is unanswerable."
death:
You take out the exception, and Clause 7 goes from unanswerable to merely enormous.

{name} drops something small and heavy on its way down, and it catches the light in a way nothing else on any floor has, and you pick it up before you have decided to.

contingency.name: Senior Contingency
taunt: "There is always another plan."
"You cannot get underneath this. There is no underneath."
"I have a version of this conversation for every thing you might do."
death: You get underneath it. There was an underneath. {name} finds that out at the same moment you do.
{name} exhausts its escalation path, arrives at the bottom of it, and finds nothing there, which is what everyone finds.

kaleidon.name: Kaleidon, the Unforeseeable
kaleidon.atk1: a shape you have not seen before
taunt: "NOTHING ABOUT ME IS SETTLED."
"YOU CANNOT LEARN ME. I AM NOT FINISHED BEING MADE."
"ASK YOURSELF WHY THE LIGHT CAME BACK. ASK ME. I WILL NOT TELL YOU EITHER."
death:
It runs out of configurations.

That should not be possible and Kaleidon clearly agrees, because it stops halfway through becoming something and simply stays there, a shape with no name, and the shape is beautiful and it is the last new thing this floor will ever produce.

The colour does not go when it dies. You wait for it. It does not go.

Somewhere above you, in a building of grey rooms and grey carpet and grey people, a floor stays in colour, and nobody who authorised any of this is left to file the exception.

You stop trying to predict it and simply keep going until it stops.

That turns out to be the answer. Not cleverness. Persistence. Kaleidon reconfigures forty times and every one of them is remarkable and none of them is enough, and the fortieth is smaller than the first.

"Oh," it says, in a voice made of about nine voices. "You were never going to work me out. You were just going to outlast me."

And the light stays.

debtor.name: Debtor
taunt: Their tally board has too many digits on it.
"I'm nearly clear. I'm nearly clear."
death: {name} sets the barrow down, straightens up for the first time in a very long time, and does not pick it back up.
The debt goes with them. That is the only way anyone leaves this floor and everyone here knows it.

pour_crew.name: Pour Crew
taunt: "Mind your feet. That's all the warning you get."
"Stand clear of the pour."
death: {name} goes into the sand mould it was filling, which is not the worst end available on this floor.
You get inside the swing of the ladle. There is nothing {name} can do at that distance and it knows it immediately.

held_harmless.name: Held Harmless
taunt: "It has to go somewhere. It does not have to go to us."
"Held harmless. Somebody is held. It is not harmless."
death: The harm comes back to it, all of it, everything it ever passed on, and there is nobody left downstream to take it.
{name} runs out of people to hold it for.

joint_and_several.name: Joint and Several
joint_and_several.atk1: all of it, from any of them
taunt: "Any one of us is liable for all of it."
"You only have to catch one."
death: You catch one. Under joint and several liability that is sufficient, and {name} goes down carrying the entire amount alone, exactly as it always said it would.
The others do not help. That was always the arrangement.

the_smelt.name: The Smelt
taunt: The heat off it is a physical wall.
"Everything is the same once it is molten."
death: {name} goes cold. It takes a long time and it takes the whole aisle's heat with it, and by the end you can hear the foundry properly for the first time.
You get the furnace door shut. {name} is on the wrong side of it.

the_surety.name: The Surety
taunt: "I stand behind every obligation on this floor."
"When they cannot pay, I pay. Then I collect. Ask them how the collecting goes."
death:
{name} stands behind one obligation too many.

The whole structure it was propping up comes down onto it, which is precisely what a surety is for, and it does not complain, and that is somehow the worst part.

the_bond.name: The Bond
taunt: "You are covered. You are extensively covered."
"Every good thing that happens to you down here is on my paper."
"I would like to discuss the premium."
death: The bond is discharged. {name} has never been discharged before and turns out to have nothing underneath the obligation at all.
You default. Spectacularly, deliberately, in front of witnesses. {name} cannot enforce against somebody with nothing, and finds that out standing up.

the_guarantor.name: The Guarantor
taunt: "Everything you do to me, someone you brought pays for."
"That is the clause. I did not write it. I only enforce it, and I enforce it completely."
"Look at them. Look at what you are doing to them."
death:
You break the indemnity.

It takes the whole fight to work out how, and the answer turns out to be simple and horrible: you have to be willing to keep going while it costs somebody else, right up until the moment it stops.

{name} goes down and the redirection goes with it, and your companion, battered, still standing, looks at you with an expression you are going to be carrying for a while.

"Sorry," you say.

They shrug it off, because they always do, and that does not help at all.

The last of it lands on it rather than on them.

{name} spends the entire fight moving your damage onto somebody who did not sign anything, and then, at the end, has nobody left to move it onto, and takes the whole amount itself.

"Ah," it says. "Yes. That is what it feels like."

It sounds genuinely surprised. It has been doing this for forty years and has never once been on this end of it.

offcut.name: Offcut
offcut.atk1: the edge where it was cut
taunt: It is the part of something that was not needed.
It has a clean edge and a ragged one.
death: {name} is trimmed the rest of the way and there is nothing left to be an offcut of.
You take the ragged end. {name} comes apart along the clean one, which is where it always wanted to go.

partial_term.name: Partial Term
taunt: "...and the remainder shall continue in full force."
It only has the second half of its own sentence.
death: {name} loses its remainder and there is nothing left to continue in force.
You strike out the surviving portion. It does not survive.

blue_pencil.name: Blue Pencil
taunt: It removes the offending part and leaves the rest standing. Usually.
"Hold still. This will be neater if you hold still."
death: {name} runs a line through itself, which is either an accident or the most professional thing on this floor.
You catch the pencil. Without it {name} is just a rule with nothing to enforce.

void_clause.name: Void Clause
void_clause.atk1: the absence where a term should be
taunt: There is a shape here and the shape is what is missing.
It was struck out years ago and has not noticed.
death: {name} is void, and this time somebody tells it so, and it goes.
The gap closes. There was never anything there. There is now less than that.

unenforceable.name: Unenforceable
unenforceable.atk1: a demand with nothing behind it
taunt: "You will comply."
"There are consequences. I am not going to specify them."
death: You decline to comply. {name} has no second move and has never needed one until now.
{name} turns out to be exactly as enforceable as it always was, which is not at all.

the_remainder.name: The Remainder
taunt: "I am what continues after the invalid parts are removed."
"You have removed eight clauses. I am still here. Consider what that means."
"There is always a remainder."
death: {name} is reduced past the point where anything remains, which nobody has ever managed and which it plainly did not think possible.
You take the balance. {name} goes down and, for the first time in this building, the phrase 'in full force' stops being true.

hemikin_left.name: Hemikin (Left)
taunt: "We are not severable."
"Kill this one and the other gets no easier." It is lying. Slightly.
death:
The left half stops.

Somewhere on this floor, through however many walls, the right half feels it, and you hear it, and it is not a good sound.

Whatever waits at the bottom of Clause 9 is now half of what it was, and it knows exactly whose fault that is.

hemikin_right.name: Hemikin
hemikin_right.atk2: the half that was always stronger
hemikin_right.atk3: both halves, if you were slow
taunt: "WE ARE NOT SEVERABLE."
"YOU TOOK THE OTHER ONE. THERE IS NO OTHER ONE. THERE WAS NEVER AN OTHER ONE."
"IF ANY PROVISION IS FOUND INVALID, THE REMAINDER SHALL CONTINUE."
death:
It cannot continue.

That is the whole of it: Hemikin is a clause about surviving the loss of your own parts, and it has now lost enough of them to find out that the clause was never true, and it works this out at exactly the moment you do.

"The remainder," it says, and stops, because there is not one.

The floor settles. Somewhere above you, in twelve other clauses, something that had been holding on lets go a little.

precedent.name: Precedent
taunt: "This was settled in 1974 and you were not consulted."
"It binds. That is what it is for."
death: You distinguish it on the facts. {name} is no longer binding and no longer anything.
Overruled. {name} goes down and takes a hundred years of it with it.

jurisdiction.name: Jurisdiction
taunt: "You are inside. That is all jurisdiction is."
"There is nowhere this does not reach. There is only nowhere you have got to."
death: You step outside it, briefly, and in that step {name} has no power at all and you use the step.
{name} loses its reach. It is only a boundary, and boundaries are lines, and lines can be crossed.

the_gallery.name: The Public Gallery
taunt: They are all facing you and none of them is looking at you.
The murmur goes up when you enter and does not go down.
death: {name} disperses the way a gallery does: not at once, in ones and twos, muttering, and the room is much larger afterwards.
The murmur stops. Forty faces turn away together and there is nobody in any of the seats.

obiter.name: Obiter Dicta
taunt: "This does not bind you. I am saying it anyway."
"By the way. And this is not part of the judgment."
death: {name} was never necessary to the decision and is now not necessary to anything.
You ignore it, which is legally correct and personally satisfying, and {name} cannot survive being correctly ignored.

contempt.name: Contempt
taunt: "You will address the court properly."
"That was your warning. There is one warning."
death: {name} requires a court to be in contempt of, and you have been steadily removing the court all afternoon.
You are held in contempt, punished for it, and still standing, which turns out to be the end of {name} rather than of you.

the_clerk.name: The Clerk of the Court
the_clerk.atk1: the file that was never passed up
taunt: "I decide what reaches the bench. I have decided about you several times."
"Your file came through me in the second week. All of it did."
"There is a correct way to do this and you are not doing it."
death:
{name} goes down among four decades of paper it decided nobody needed to see.

The last thing it does is square the stack. It cannot help it. Forty years of squaring stacks.

Underneath the stack is your file, complete, with every excluded page still in it, and a note clipped to the front in careful handwriting: SHOULD HAVE GONE UP. MY ERROR.

the_bailiff.name: The Bailiff
taunt: "You're coming with me."
"Nothing personal. It's the job. It has always been the job."
"Everyone comes with me eventually."
death: {name} lets go of your arm and sits down on the bench outside the court like somebody at the end of a very long shift.
You are not removed. {name} has removed everyone, for forty years, without exception, and the exception undoes it.

justice_vorn.name: Justice Vorn
taunt: "You are here because you disputed. Nobody disputes."
"I have presided over four billion acceptances and eleven disputes."
"I am not against you. I am the venue. It amounts to the same thing."
death:
Vorn gives judgment against itself.

It takes a while to work out that that is what has happened. You beat it, and it stands, and it looks at the empty gallery and the unlit bench and the court with no jurisdiction left in it, and it says, quite formally:

"The court finds for the disputant. The court further finds that it has no power to make that finding, the governing law having been disputed at Clause 10. The court notes the irregularity.

The court is adjourned. The court is not going to reconvene."

And it sits down on the steps of its own bench, and stops being a judge, and is only a very old thing in a robe.

The judgment goes the other way.

"So noted," says Vorn, and it is not bitter, and that is somehow worse. "Eleven disputes and one of them landed. I would like the record to show that I heard it properly."

The record shows nothing. There is no record. You disputed the clause that made records binding two floors ago and everything since has been off the books, and Vorn knows, and gave you the hearing anyway.

tracked_change.name: Tracked Change
taunt: Everything it does is in a different colour and attributed to nobody.
"Accept? Reject? Accept all?"
death: You reject the change. {name} reverts, and there is nothing underneath a change but the thing it was changing.
Accepted. {name} is merged into the body text and stops being a separate thing at all.

schedule_two.name: Schedule Two
taunt: "I am attached to the main body and I am longer than it."
"See schedule two. Everyone forgets to see schedule two."
death: {name} is detached from the main agreement, and a schedule with nothing to be a schedule to is just paper.
You read it. All of it. {name} has never been read to the end and does not survive the experience.

the_variation.name: The Variation
taunt: "That was true when you started swinging."
It has been three different things this round.
death: {name} varies itself one time too many and lands on a version that cannot stand up.
You hit the version that is actually there rather than the one you were aiming at, and it turns out that was the whole trick.

marginalia.name: Marginalia
taunt: "Is this right?" says the margin. "Check with legal," says the margin.
Somebody has annotated you.
death: The queries are resolved. {name} was only ever questions and the questions have answers now.
You answer the margin. It has been asking for forty years and had stopped expecting anything.

effective_immediately.name: Effective Immediately
effective_immediately.atk2: in force before you read it
taunt: "This took effect while you were reading the first line."
"Continued use constitutes acceptance."
death: {name} takes effect immediately and, immediately, stops being in effect. It is the same trick both ways.
You stop using it. {name} has no mechanism for that and comes apart looking for one.

the_redline.name: The Redline
the_redline.atk1: a query in the margin of you
taunt: "Why did you do it that way?"
"This is not a criticism. I would just like to understand the reasoning."
"Every choice you have made since Intake is marked up here. Would you like to see?"
death:
The markup resolves.

Every query answered, every change accepted or rejected, and what is left when {name} goes down is a clean copy of everything you have done since Intake with no comments in the margin at all.

You look at it for longer than the situation allows. It reads, on the whole, better than you expected.

the_rider.name: The Rider
taunt: "There is one more condition."
"It is very short. It is only a sentence."
"Riders are how everything important gets in."
death: {name} is severed from the thing it rode in on, which is a Clause 9 move and works here too.
You strike the additional term. {name} was never load-bearing; it just travelled with something that was.

the_amendment.name: The Amendment
the_amendment.atk2: whatever is in force this second
taunt: "WE MAY AMEND THESE TERMS AT ANY TIME."
"WHAT YOU LEARNED LAST ROUND IS SUPERSEDED."
"CONTINUED PRESENCE CONSTITUTES ACCEPTANCE. YOU ARE STILL HERE."
death:
It runs out of revisions.

Five reissues is what the clause allows and you counted them, and on the sixth there is nothing left to amend it into. The Amendment stands there in its final wording, which is short, and which reads, in its entirety:

THESE TERMS MAY NOT BE FURTHER AMENDED.

"Well," it says, in a voice that has been about nine different voices tonight and is now only one. "That's that fixed, then."

And Clause 11 stops changing, and the whole floor settles into one version and stays in it, and behind you every room you walked through becomes, permanently, whatever it last was.

You beat the version that is in force.

That is the only version there has ever been able to be: the current one, in force, singular. It amends around your first blow and your second and your fifth, and the sixth arrives before the amendment does.

"Effective immediately," says {name}, out of habit, and nothing takes effect, and that is the end of it.

shutdown_notice.name: Shutdown Notice
taunt: "This facility will close. It has said that for eleven years."
"Please make alternative arrangements."
death: {name} takes effect at last, on itself, and closes.
You give it a date. It has never had a real date and cannot survive one.

ash_clerk.name: Ash Clerk
ash_clerk.atk1: a handful of what is left
taunt: It is still filing. There is nothing to file into.
It is made of the ash and the ash is made of the files.
death: {name} comes apart into what it was always made of, which settles on your shoulders and stays there.
The filing stops. It is the first thing in this building to finish a job.

last_day.name: Last Day
taunt: "I've got until five."
It is carrying a cardboard box and it is not letting go of it.
death: {name} finishes at last, sets the box down, and does not pick it up again.
It is five o'clock somewhere in {name} and it goes home.

wound_down.name: Wound Down
taunt: It has not been maintained since the acquisition and it is still going.
Something inside it is grinding and it does not care.
death: {name} runs out. That is all. It was always only ever going to run out.
The last of the momentum goes. {name} coasts to a halt, tidily, in gear.

the_skeleton_staff.name: The Skeleton Staff
taunt: "There's four of us left. There were four hundred."
"We're managing."
They are not managing.
death: {name} finally stops covering for everybody else and goes down with what looks a great deal like relief.
You relieve {name}. Of duty, mostly. It had been waiting forty years for somebody to.

the_final_notice.name: The Final Notice
taunt: "This is the last one. There are no more after this."
"We did write. Repeatedly."
"There will be no further correspondence on this matter."
death:
{name} is served on itself and there is no further correspondence.

It goes down neatly, in an envelope, and the envelope is addressed to somebody who left in 1974.

the_liquidator.name: The Liquidator
taunt: "Everything in this building has a number and I have written all of them down."
"You are on the inventory. Page nine."
"Nothing personal. It is an orderly process."
death: {name} realises its last asset, balances, and closes the ledger on itself, which is the only tidy death in the building.
You are not on the inventory after all. {name} cannot proceed with an incomplete inventory.

reaper_of_records.name: The Reaper of Records
