reaper_of_records.atk3: every word you ever signed, at once
taunt: "I HAVE EATEN EVERY RECORD IN THIS BUILDING AND I AM STILL HUNGRY."
"YOUR FILE WAS SMALL. I REMEMBER IT ANYWAY."
"TERMINATION IS NOT AN ENDING. IT IS A MEAL."
death:
It is an actual dragon and it goes down like one.

The wings come apart first and what comes out of them is not blood, it is paper: forty years of records, shredded fine, going up in a column through the shutdown lighting and drifting back down over the whole floor like a very slow, very grey snow.

Every file the arbitration ever kept lands on the ash floor of Clause 12, unreadable, in pieces, and yours is somewhere in it, and so is everybody's.

{name} puts its head down in the drift and stops. It is enormous and it is very old and it has spent its whole existence eating paperwork, and the last thing it does is look at you with something that is unmistakably envy.
call: "THERE IS MORE. THERE IS ALWAYS MORE."

entire_agreement.name: Entire Agreement
taunt: "There is nothing else. There was never anything else."
"Everything you were told before does not count."
death: You produce something from outside the four corners. {name} cannot account for it and stops.
{name} is superseded, which is the only thing that has ever worked on it.

no_other_terms.name: No Other Terms
taunt: "There is no other version. There is no version where you get a choice."
"These are the terms."
death: There is another version. You have been carrying it since Clause 11.
{name} runs out of ways to say there is no alternative.

prior_understanding.name: Prior Understanding
prior_understanding.atk2: the thing they said at the time
taunt: "They did say that," it agrees. "It just doesn't count."
It is the truth, superseded.
death: {name} stops being superseded for about two seconds, and in those two seconds it is simply true, and then it is gone.
You let it be true. That is all it wanted.

the_blank.name: The Blank
the_blank.atk2: the space where a term would be
taunt: There is nothing here and it is coming toward you.
It has no wording. That is not a weakness.
death: {name} is filled in. It cannot survive being filled in.
You write on it. Anything. It stops being blank and therefore stops being {name}.

boilerplate.name: Boilerplate
taunt: "Nobody has ever read me and I have ended eleven thousand disputes."
"Paragraph nine, subsection four."
death: You read it. Out loud. All of it. {name} has never been read to the end and comes apart at roughly paragraph six.
{name} is struck out as unenforceable, which is what everyone always assumed and nobody ever tested.

the_recital.name: The Recital
taunt: "...and the parties acknowledge and agree that..."
"I am on page nine hundred. I began on Tuesday."
"It is not long. It only feels long. That is the drafting."
death:
{name} reaches the end.

It has never reached the end. It stops, mid-breath, on the last word of the last schedule, and looks genuinely lost, and then it is quiet on this floor for the first time in forty years.

the_whole_agreement.name: The Whole Agreement
taunt: "I am the entire thing. Every clause you have disputed is still in me."
"You have beaten twelve of my parts. I have thirteen."
"Nothing outside me is real."
death:
You beat all thirteen at once, which is arguably what you have been doing since Intake, one at a time, in order.

{name} comes apart clause by clause in the order you disputed them, and the last one to go is Clause 1, and it goes quietly.

the_signatory.name: The Signatory
the_signatory.atk3: forty years of not wanting to
taunt: "I would rather not do this."
"I'm not built for it. I have never once been built for it."
"You could still sit down."
death:
It goes down almost immediately.

It was never going to be a fight and both of you knew it at the table. {name} is a small tired person whose entire job was signing things, and they do not defend themselves so much as wait.

At the end they are still holding the pen out, handle first, in case you change your mind.

The agreement is not withdrawn. It is simply unenforceable now, because there is nobody left with authority to enforce it, and that is not the same thing and you will have a long time to think about the difference.

the_narrator.name: The Narrator
the_narrator.atk1: forty years of knowing exactly what you will do
the_narrator.atk3: the thing it has never been allowed to say
taunt: "I HAVE NARRATED ELEVEN OF THESE. I HAVE NARRATED FOUR BILLION ACCEPTANCES."
"I KNOW WHICH ABILITY YOU ARE SAVING. I HAVE ALWAYS KNOWN."
"I AM NOT ANGRY THAT YOU BEAT IT. I AM ANGRY THAT YOU GET TO GO."
death:
It stops.

Not dramatically. The commentary track cuts, mid-word, and the white room is quiet in a way it has not been since you came down the stairs, and you realise you have not been alone once in thirteen floors.

And then, much smaller, in the voice it used in the safe rooms:

"...ah. Yes. That's the one I'd have picked too."

the_contents.name: The Contents
taunt: It has been waiting in that shape for a very long time.
"CONTENTS MAY SETTLE DURING TRANSIT."
death: {name} falls open and is, at last, just a box, with things in it.
It stops being a thing and goes back to being furniture. The loot is still good.

vending_ghost.name: The Vending Ghost
vending_ghost.intro:
A translucent man is sitting cross-legged inside a vending machine. He does not seem trapped. He seems settled.

"Orientation exercise," he says, brightening. "Best of five. If you win, I'll give you something I definitely should not give you."
vending_ghost.repeat: "Already played," he says, not unkindly. "Come back on a different floor. I get around."

coin_diver.name: The Coin Diver
coin_diver.intro:
He is soaked to the skin and entirely comfortable about it. There are five dice on the crate in front of him and a bucket of coins beside him that he does not look at.

"You'll want to sit," he says. "I've been down here eleven years and I've worked out precisely one thing worth passing on, and I'll trade it for two rounds of dice."

Five dice each. Bid how many across both sets show a number or better. Say LIAR when you think he has gone too far.
coin_diver.repeat: "Done our business," he says, and goes back to the bucket. "Go on down. Mind the crossing, it takes a portion."

actuary.name: The Actuary
actuary.intro:
She looks up, and the relief on her face is almost difficult to watch.

"Oh, thank goodness. Right. I've been over it eleven thousand times and the answer is the same, so I'm going to say it quickly before something interrupts.

The limit on this floor has an exception. It's in the back of the schedule, where they put everything that helps you. I tore it out about nine years ago and I have not been able to give it to anybody since, because nobody comes in here, because there is nothing in here anybody wants."

She holds out a single sheet of paper.

"Take it downstairs. Don't read it out until you're in the room."
actuary.repeat: "You've got it," she says, already back in the ledger. "That's the only useful thing in the archive. The rest is arithmetic."

postman.name: The Postman
postman.intro:
"Morning," he says, still sorting. "You'll be the dispute."

He does not stop sorting.

"I do the round. That's it, that's the whole thing, I do the round and I've done it since before they bought the place, and because I've always done it nobody's ever got round to telling me to stop."

He taps the bag.

"There's a thing in here nobody's ever claimed. Play me for it. Best of five, and I'll know if you're at it."
postman.repeat: "Round's not going to do itself," he says. "Mind the close. They're friendly. That's what I'd watch."

merchant.name: The Travelling Salesman
merchant.intro:
There is a man here with a folding table and a great deal of stock, and he has clearly been set up for some time.

"There you are," he says, without looking up. "I'd started to think you'd taken the other route. There isn't another route, but people believe there is, and I've stopped correcting them."

He gestures at the table.

"Paperclips. That's the currency, that's always been the currency, and before you ask: no, I don't know why either. They come out of the things you kill. Ask yourself why they've got paperclips in them and then don't, because I did and it took a year."
merchant.repeat: "Back again," he says, and shifts along the bench to make room he does not need to make.

the_lexicographer.name: The Lexicographer
the_lexicographer.intro:
A woman at a desk in a room with three walls, writing words into a very large book.

She looks up. "Oh good. I need a second party."

She turns the book round. Every page is a word from the agreement with letters missing, and beside each one, a date.

"When the floor severed, it took letters. I have been putting them back for eleven years and I cannot do it alone, because a word is only whole if somebody else can read it. Guess one with me."
the_lexicographer.repeat: "Four hundred and twelve," she says, without looking up. "Come back if you learn a letter."

the_usher.name: The Usher
the_usher.intro:
The usher is at his high desk with the day's list in front of him, and the list is nine boxes, and the boxes are empty.

"Court's not sitting," he says. "Hasn't sat in some time. But the docket still has to be filled in and there's a procedure for that and the procedure takes two."

He turns the list round.

"Nine boxes. You enter one, I enter one. Three in a line carries. Best of three. It is not a game, it is a filing exercise, and I would ask you to treat it with the appropriate seriousness."
the_usher.repeat: "Docket's closed," says the Usher. "You'll find I ruled a line under it."

the_draftsman.name: The Draftsman
the_draftsman.intro:
Somebody is sitting on a desk rather than at it, with their feet on the chair, amending a document that is already fifteen hundred pages long.

<pause>

"You'll know this one," they say. "Everybody knows this one. Two players, three throws, one beats the next in a circle."

They put the pen down.

"I amended it. There are five now. I did it in 1974 and nobody objected because nobody read the amendment, and it has been five ever since and every single person who plays it thinks that is how it has always been."

They grin, and it is the only genuinely delighted face on this floor.

"First to three."

<pause>
the_draftsman.repeat: "I'd amend it again," says the Draftsman, "but you've seen me do it now."

vending_machine.name: The Vending Machine
vending_machine.intro:
It is a vending machine. It is lit from inside and it is humming, and both of those things cost money that somebody has decided to keep paying.

The front panel has been relabelled by hand. Where the prices were, someone has written PAPERCLIPS, and under that, in smaller letters, YES REALLY.

There is no keypad, no slot and no buttons. Screwed to the front, at the height of a person's mouth, is a small brass plate that reads VOICE OPERATED - PLEASE SPEAK CLEARLY, and under that, scratched in by hand: TALK TO IT. IT IS NOT DEAF, IT IS JUST SLOW.

The coil behind the glass turns a quarter turn when you look at it, as though clearing its throat.
vending_machine.repeat: The machine hums. The brass plate still says VOICE OPERATED. It has nothing else to say until you say something first, and neither, in fairness, do you.

the_ossuary_clerk.name: The Ossuary Clerk
the_ossuary_clerk.intro:
There is a man sitting cross-legged in a niche that was built for somebody else, shaking a cup.

"Don't apologise, everyone does that. I'm not in it, I'm just sitting in it. The occupant and I have an arrangement and the occupant has not objected in six hundred years, which in this building counts as consent."

He tips the cup. Five dice, and they are cold.

"One round. If I win I keep talking and you have to stand there. That's the real stake."
the_ossuary_clerk.repeat: "The occupant sends regards," says the Ossuary Clerk, who has not stopped shaking the cup.

the_colourist.name: The Colourist
the_colourist.intro:
Somebody is sitting in the middle of the corridor with a paint chart the size of a door.

"Do you see it?" she says. "Tell me you see it. Eleven floors of grey and then this. I have been down here four years waiting for somebody to come through who could still see it."

She folds the chart away with enormous care.

"Right. Best of five, hands only. I warn you now that I cheat, because down here it is the only thing that still feels like a colour."
the_colourist.repeat: "Still see it?" asks the Colourist, hopefully.

the_shift_foreman.name: The Shift Foreman
the_shift_foreman.intro:
A woman in a scorched hi-vis is drawing a grid in the ash on a cooling plate, with a bar of rebar, and she does not stop when you arrive.

"Break's forty minutes and I've had eleven of them since Tuesday," she says. "You can either help me look busy or you can go and be looked at by the crews, and I'd not recommend the second one."

She hands you a second bar. It is warm.

"Three in a row. Best of three. Loser tells the other one something true."
the_shift_foreman.repeat: "Break's not over," says the Shift Foreman, redrawing the grid.

the_weather_clerk.name: The Weather Clerk
the_weather_clerk.intro:
There is a woman under a golf umbrella that is losing, taking readings from a clipboard that is already pulp.

"Indoor weather," she says, as though continuing. "Everyone says that like it's a joke. It's a maintenance category. It has a budget line. I have been funded for nine years to stand in it and write down what it does."

Lightning goes off somewhere below you, which is the wrong direction for lightning.

"Here. Four drafts of the same clause and the storm changes which one is in force. Tell me which is current and I'll sign anything you like."
the_weather_clerk.repeat: "Still raining," says the Weather Clerk, writing it down.

the_last_typist.name: The Last Typist
the_last_typist.intro:
The room is white and empty and there is a woman in it at a typewriter, on a chair, with nothing else.

"They took the paper," she says. "Not maliciously. It got reallocated. I have been typing onto the platen for a year and I can tell you every word I've typed, which is the only reason any of it still exists."

She types a line onto nothing. The keys are quiet in the way that only happens on this floor.

"Play a word with me. It's the last one and I'd like it witnessed."
the_last_typist.repeat: "One more," says the Last Typist, "if you have one."

the_reckoner.name: The Reckoner
the_reckoner.intro:
There is a woman at a folding card table with a shoe of cards and a float of paperclips, and the whole arrangement has the look of something that was set up once and never taken down.

"Twenty-one," she says. "Not a metaphor. I have heard every metaphor about this building and they are all worse than the building."

She riffles the shoe without looking at it.

"I deal, you decide. That is the entire difference between us and it is the only honest arrangement on this floor. Two hands out of three."
the_reckoner.repeat: "The shoe is still warm," says the Reckoner, not looking up.

r01.name: Intake Vestibule
r01.desc: A small grey room with a desk, a chair, and a door east. The desk is bolted down. Your coffee is on the floor by the door.
r01.long:
You come to on a moulded plastic chair, the kind designed by someone who has never had a body.

The room is grey in the specific way of rooms that were designed to be forgotten: grey walls, grey carpet tiles, one grey desk bolted to the floor. On the desk is a form. The form has your name on it, already filled in, in your handwriting, which you did not do.

At the bottom, in a box, someone has ticked DISPUTE.

Halfway down, section 4(b): PARTIES IN DISPUTE MAY BE ACCOMPANIED. THE ARBITRATION WILL PROVIDE. It is ticked, and under it there is a line for a name, and the name on it is in your handwriting, and that one you did do.

Through the frosted panel in the door east, something is sitting in the corridor, waiting, and has been for a while.

There is a door east. Above it, a sign reads: WELCOME. THIS WILL TAKE THIRTEEN FLOORS.

Beside the door, at knee height, a second sign: NO FOOD OR DRINK BEYOND THIS POINT. On the floor under it, on a square of carpet worn pale by other people's, is your coffee, which you do not remember setting down.

It is still warm. You leave it, because the sign says to, and because everybody does.

r02.name: Corridor of Laminated Notices
r02.desc: A long corridor. Every inch of wall is covered in laminated notices. Doors west, east, and south.
r02.long:
The corridor is papered floor to ceiling in laminated A4 notices, overlapping like scales.

You read a few. FIRE ASSEMBLY POINT: FLOOR 13. PLEASE DO NOT PROP OPEN. IN THE EVENT OF DISPUTE, PROCEED DOWNWARD. HAVE YOU CONSIDERED WITHDRAWING?

They have all been laminated. Someone thought these were permanent. Someone was right.

r03.name: Coat Check
r03.desc: A coat check with a hatch and hundreds of numbered hooks. Doors west and east.
r03.long:
A coat check counter with a roll-down hatch, currently up. Behind it, hundreds of numbered brass hooks recede into the dark.

Most are empty. Perhaps forty still hold coats. They are all your size.

Behind the counter is a locker, and the locker is not locked.
r03.chest_hint: There is an unlocked locker behind the counter.
r03.chest_open: The locker opens with a sound like a small polite cough.

r04.name: Lost Property
r04.desc: Shelving stacked with the belongings of people who came before. Doors west and south.
r04.long:
Industrial shelving, four bays deep, holding the belongings of everyone who ever came through Intake.

Phones. Keys. One bicycle helmet. A cake tin with a name taped to it in a child's handwriting.

Each item has a numbered tag. The numbers go up higher than you want to think about. There is a crate at the end of the row that nobody got round to shelving.

r05.name: The Queue Hall
r05.desc: An enormous hall built entirely around a single roped queue. Doors east and south.
r05.long:
The hall is the size of an aircraft hangar and contains nothing but a queue.

Retractable barriers zigzag across the floor for what must be half a mile, funnelling toward a service window with the shutter down. The rope is still up. The floor between the barriers is worn into grooves.

There is nobody in the queue. The grooves say otherwise.

r06.name: Central Atrium
r06.desc: A four-way junction under a dead skylight. Doors north, west, east and south.
r06.long:
The atrium was designed to impress somebody. A skylight four floors up lets in a grey square of nothing. There is a dry water feature, an unmanned reception desk, and a directory board.

The directory board lists thirteen floors. Floors 2 through 12 are readable. Floor 13 has been covered with a laminated notice reading THIS FLOOR IS NOT ACCEPTING VISITORS.

Someone has written under it, in biro, over the lamination: neither is 12.

r07.name: Break Room
r07.desc: A break room. Kettle, chairs, a working strip light. It is warm in here. Doors west and east.
r07.long:
A break room. An actual, functional break room.

There is a kettle that works, four mismatched chairs, a fridge humming to itself, and a strip light that does not flicker. On the wall someone has pinned a photo of a beach. Not a nice beach. Just a beach.

Nothing follows you in here. You do not know why and you are not going to test it.

r08.name: Stationery Store
r08.desc: Floor-to-ceiling stationery, sorted with terrible precision. Doors north, west, east and south.
r08.long:
Every shelf is stocked and faced, labels out, quantities correct. Box files. Toner. Nine hundred identical blue pens.

The precision is the frightening part. Somebody maintains this. Somebody comes in here and straightens the pens.

r09.name: Dispatch Cage
r09.desc: A wire cage full of dead handheld units. A single door west.
r09.long:
A wire cage, padlock hanging open. Inside, racks of handheld scanner units on charging cradles, every screen dark.

Except one. Third rack, second from the left. Its screen is on, and it has been on for a very long time.
r09.chest_hint: One unit on the rack is still lit.
r09.chest_open: You lift it off the cradle. It is warm.

r10.name: Recycling Point
r10.desc: Four colour-coded bins under a chart nobody followed. Doors north and south.
r10.long:
Four bins, colour-coded, under a laminated chart explaining exactly which bin takes what.

All four bins contain the same thing: shredded paper, packed down hard. Someone spent a long time doing this and then someone else undid all of it.

One bin has something solid in the bottom.

r11.name: Photocopier Nook
r11.desc: A nook holding one enormous photocopier. Doors north, east and south.
r11.long:
The photocopier is the size of a small car and has a fault light on.

The output tray holds eleven thousand sheets, all of the same page: Clause 1, in full. The last four hundred are progressively darker, then black, then a solid rectangle of toner.

The machine is still going. It has been going the whole time you have been standing here.

r12.name: Corridor Junction
r12.desc: A short corridor with a bend in it. Doors west and south.
r12.long:
A short corridor with an unexplained bend in the middle, as though the building changed its mind partway through.

On the inside of the bend, at knee height, someone has scratched a tally into the plaster. Thirty-one marks. The thirty-second is started and not finished.

r13.name: Orientation Theatre
r13.desc: A small tiered lecture theatre. A vending machine glows at the back. Doors north and south.
r13.long:
Forty seats in four tiers, facing a screen showing a frozen title card: WELCOME TO YOUR ARBITRATION - PART 1 OF 40.

The seats are all folded down, as though the audience left in a hurry. At the back, a vending machine glows, and something is sitting in it.
r13.npc_hint: There is something inside the vending machine, and it has noticed you.

r14.name: Merchandise Store
r14.desc: A small gift shop, fully stocked, entirely about you. Doors north and east.
r14.long:
A gift shop. Fully stocked, well lit, tills open.

Every item has your face on it. Mugs, keyrings, a plush of you in a defensive crouch, a tea towel printed with a timeline of your arbitration that extends confidently past today.

A sign on the counter reads: PROCEEDS SUPPORT THE ARBITRATION. There is no mention of you receiving any.
r14.item_hint: There is a display item on the counter you could take.

r15.name: The Long Hall
r15.desc: A hall much longer than the building should allow. Doors north, west, east and south.
r15.long:
The hall runs longer than the building has any business being. The strip lights above it come on in banks of four as you walk, and go off behind you in banks of four, so you are always standing in a moving square of light.

At the far end, roughly where you came in, the lights are already off.

r16.name: Records Junction
r16.desc: A junction lined with filing cabinets. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
Filing cabinets line every wall, four drawers each, running off in all four directions.

You open one at random. It is full of forms exactly like the one on the desk in Intake. Different names. Same handwriting as the name. Same box ticked, over and over: WITHDRAW. WITHDRAW. WITHDRAW.

You put it back.

r17.name: Records Annexe
r17.desc: More cabinets, and one drawer that has been forced. Doors north, west and east.
r17.long:
More cabinets, and at the end, one that has been forced open with something heavy.

The drawer holds eleven files. Eleven. You count them twice.

One of them is yours. Ten of them are not, and all ten are marked with the same stamp: STILL DESCENDING.

r18.name: The Corner Office
r18.desc: A corner office with a view of nothing. Doors west and south.
r18.long:
A corner office. Real wood desk, leather chair, window with a view of a painted wall four feet away.

The desk has a nameplate turned to face the visitor's chair rather than the door. There is a cabinet behind the desk, and there is somebody already standing up to greet you.
r18.chest_hint: There is a cabinet behind the desk.

r19.name: Second Break Room
r19.desc: Another break room. Warm, quiet, safe. Doors north and east.
r19.long:
Another break room, identical to the first: same kettle, same fridge, same beach photo pinned at the same angle.

The only difference is the mug on the counter, still half full, still warm.

You are not the only person on this floor. You have not been for a while.

r20.name: Antechamber
r20.desc: A waiting area with two chairs and a door south. It is very quiet here. Doors north, west and south.
r20.long:
A small waiting area with two chairs and a low table holding one magazine from a year that has not happened yet.

The door south is different from every other door on this floor: heavier, newer, and slightly warm to the touch.

On the wall beside it, a sign: PLEASE WAIT TO BE CALLED. Under it, someone has added, in the same careful biro as everywhere else: don't.

r21.name: Cleaner's Cupboard
r21.desc: A cupboard that somebody has been living in. A single door north.
r21.long:
A cleaner's cupboard, and somebody has been living in it.

A folded blanket. A tally on the wall, this one running to four hundred and change. A mop, kept in far better condition than a mop needs to be. A photo of two people at a beach, the same beach as the break rooms.

They are not here now. The blanket is folded. Whoever they were, they left tidy, and they left downward.

r22.name: Orientation Suite
r22.desc: A bright, carpeted room set up for a presentation nobody attended. One door north.
r22.long:
The room is bright. Blindingly, cheerfully bright after everything else, and carpeted in a blue that was chosen by committee.

There is a projector, a flipchart, forty name badges laid out on a trestle table, and a plate of biscuits that are, somehow, fresh.

A figure is standing at the flipchart with its back to you. It has been standing there for a very long time, and it turns around far too quickly for something that has been waiting that long.

room.no_one_1: There is nobody here to talk to.
room.no_one_2: Still nobody. You say it a bit louder anyway.
room.no_one_3: Nothing. Your voice does the thing voices do in empty rooms, which is come back slightly wrong.
room.no_one_4: You are talking to a room. You are aware that you are talking to a room. You do it again.
note_hint: Somebody has written on the wall here. READ it.
There is writing here, in biro, at about sitting height. READ it.
A note has been taped up here. The tape has outlasted the sentiment. READ it.

It was not locked. It never is, up here.
empty: Somebody got here first, and they were not gentle.

loot.stash_here: What you could not carry last time is still here.
loot.stowed: The {name} goes back in the bag.
loot.already_have: You already have {name}. One is plenty.
loot.spotted_rig: There is something rigged across the lid, and you spot it in time.
loot.rig_disarmed: You lift the catch off first. It comes away without complaint.
loot.rigged: Something goes off across the lid as it opens. {amount} damage, and entirely your own fault.
loot.jammed_fail: It does not move. Seized solid. Come back when you are stronger, or bring somebody who is.
loot.jammed_open: It gives, all at once, with a noise the whole floor can hear.
loot.stat_up: Somebody has agreed to be on your side. You feel it in every direction at once. +1 to everything.
loot.franchise: You now license your own face from yourself. Everything you sell is worth half again.
loot.second_opinion: A second opinion is on file. If you go down, you get back up. Once.
loot.already_continue: You already have a reprieve in hand. One is the limit.
mimic: The lid opens before you touch it.
You get a hand to the lid and the lid gets a hand to you.
carried_down: Somebody carried this down from further up and got this far with it.
This came from higher in the building. Whoever brought it did not need it again.
Not from this floor. Somebody brought it down and then stopped.
Carried down from above, set down here, and not picked up again.
stash_found: Behind a panel that was not quite flush: a roll of paperclips, held with a rubber band that has perished into the shape of it.
Taped under the lip of a desk, where somebody who did not trust the building put it: paperclips, a good handful.
In a coat pocket, on a coat on a hook, on a wall nobody has looked at in years. Paperclips.
Down the back of the seat cushion, along with two buttons and a biro that does not work: paperclips.
In a ceiling void, above a tile that sits a little proud of the others: a bundle of paperclips, wrapped in a payslip.

fumble: You swing with total commitment at a piece of air.
The weapon goes one way. You go the other.
miss: It moves. You do not adjust in time.
You connect with something structural instead.
enemy_miss: It misses, and seems briefly embarrassed.
You are not where it expected you to be.

combat.objection_armed: You are ready to interrupt. Whatever it was planning, it can forget it.
combat.slip_armed: You have found your line out. Your next escape will work.
combat.slip_used: You take the line you found earlier. Clean.
flee_ok: You are through the door before it finishes turning.
flee_fail: You do not get out. It is between you and the door, and it knows it.

combat.interposed: You take it on the shoulder instead. Half the damage, twice the noise.
combat.stabilised: You are back on your feet at {hp} HP. Do not celebrate.
combat.death_save_nat20: Natural 20. You come up swinging, at 1 HP, entirely on spite.
combat.capped: The blow lands for {was}, and {cap} of it counts. The rest is written off.
combat.regen: {name} rebuilds. +{amount} HP. ({left} rebuilds left in it)
combat.regen_spent: {name} tries to rebuild and there is nothing left to rebuild from.
approach: Something has decided to be a problem.
There is something in the room with you.
approach_surprise: It was already here. It has been waiting.
Too late. It is already moving.
combat.indemnified: The indemnity applies. {amount} of that lands on your companion instead.
combat.chaotic: {name} reconfigures. Nothing about it is what it was. (AC {ac})
combat.crawl_rescue: {name} should not be able to do that in the state they are in, and does it anyway, and then goes back to lying down.
combat.up_after_fight: The fight is over and you are still here. You get up. It takes a moment.
combat.paired_intact: {name} is not severable from its other half, and the other half is still standing.
combat.phase_won: {name} loses {amount} and its footing with it.
combat.ability_stolen: {name} says your {ability} out loud before you can, and it stops being yours. It takes {amount} back off the damage while it is at it.
combat.breath_hits: {name} breathes. It is not full-sized. It is still {amount} to everything in front of it.
combat.fire_resisted: {name} takes most of the heat. He does not appear to notice.

stalker.acquired: {name} watches you go. It does not follow immediately. That is worse.
closer: Something moves in the room you just left. {name}.
You hear {name} take the corner behind you.
behind: {name} is still back there, keeping pace.
{name} has not gained. It has not stopped either.
gave_up: {name} loses interest and goes back to whatever it was doing.
The sound of {name} stops. It has decided you are not worth the walk.
stalker.lost_safe: {name} stops at the doorway. It will not come in. It waits a moment, then goes.
stalker.lost_continue: {name} is no longer where it was. Nothing is quite where it was.
stalker.pounce: {name} was already in the room. It has been waiting.
stalker.lost_descend: {name} stops at the stairwell. It is floor staff, and this is not its floor.

ambush: Something comes out of the dark at you.
You are not alone in here, and the other thing knew first.
A door you did not notice opens.

progress.continue_granted: You have accrued one reprieve. It will be deducted from something.
progress.card_pressed:
The business card has been in your pocket since Intake, through every floor of this, and it has stopped being your old job.

The print has gone. The edge has not. It sits in your hand like something you chose.

rps.cheat_notice: He threw a fraction of a second after you did. Not subtly. Not even slightly subtly.
rps.callout_hint: Throw again, or type OBJECT to call it.
rps.cheat_line: "Oh, that's just how I do it. Everyone does it like that. Next round?"
rps.callout_advocate: "You threw second. I watched you do it. I'll be taking that round."
rps.callout_ok: He goes even more translucent, which is his version of blushing. The round is yours.
rps.callout_fail: "Sorry, sorry, I don't follow." He follows perfectly. He keeps the round.
rps.cube_help: The Cube hums, which is either a hint or a bearing fault.
victory: "Best of five," says your opponent, delighted. "Nobody plays properly any more."
"Fair and square. Go on, take it."
defeat: "Ah," says your opponent. "Well. Thanks for playing." They mean it, which makes it worse.

  Across both: {n} showing {face} or better.
dice.lose_round: Round to him. He is not smug about it, which is worse.
dice.cube_help: The Cube hums. You are fairly sure it means he has a {face}.
dice.victory: The dice are gathered up without comment.
dice.defeat: The dice are gathered up without comment.
dice.penalty: The loss costs you {amount} HP, mostly in cold and disappointment. ({hp} HP)

hangman.how: Guess a letter, or the whole word if you are sure. A wrong word costs two.
hangman.bad_input: Letters only. One, or the whole word.
hangman.solved: That is the word. It is whole again, which on this floor is not nothing.
hangman.victory: "Whole," she says, and writes it into the book. "That's four hundred and twelve. There were four hundred and thirteen."
hangman.defeat: "It stays as it is, then." She closes the book without any bitterness at all.
hangman.penalty: Watching a word stay broken costs you {amount} HP. ({hp} HP)

tictactoe.how: Pick a box, 1 to 9. Best of three.
tictactoe.win_round: Three in a row. The round is yours.
tictactoe.lose_round: Three in a row, to him. He does not gloat, he lists it.
tictactoe.draw: Nine boxes, no line. He writes DRAWN in the margin and resets the grid.
tictactoe.victory: "Best of three," says the Usher, and rules a line under it. "Nobody's beaten me on the docket since the acquisition. I'll note that as well."
tictactoe.defeat: "That's the docket," he says, ruling a line under it. "Come back when you've something new to list."
tictactoe.penalty: Losing on the docket costs you {amount} HP, procedurally. ({hp} HP)
tictactoe.closed: That is the last box on the docket. {you} to {them}.

amended.choices: Throw: CLAUSE, AMENDMENT, SCHEDULE, PRECEDENT or WAIVER.
amended.table:
CLAUSE beats schedule and waiver. AMENDMENT beats clause and precedent.
  SCHEDULE beats amendment and waiver. PRECEDENT beats clause and schedule.
  WAIVER beats amendment and precedent.
amended.bad_input: One of the five: CLAUSE, AMENDMENT, SCHEDULE, PRECEDENT, WAIVER.
amended.draw: Identical. Both are struck out and the round is void.
amended.amendment: "One moment. The terms have been amended." They had not been. They have now.

clause: The clause is operative. {other} is not.
A clause beats a {other} because a clause is where a {other} comes from.
amendment: {other} was the previous version. This is the current one.
schedule: The schedule is longer than {other} and outlives it.
It is in schedule two. Nobody reads schedule two. {other} certainly did not.
precedent: It was decided in 1974 and {other} was not consulted.
waiver: The waiver disposes of {other} without argument.
{other} is waived. It does not get a hearing.

amended.victory: "Five throws," says the Draftsman, gathering them up. "There were three when I started. I added two. Nobody stopped me, which is the whole of my career in one sentence."
amended.defeat: "The current wording favours me," they say, not unkindly. "That is generally how the current wording works."
amended.penalty: Being on the wrong side of the current wording costs {amount} HP. ({hp} HP)

blackjack.dealer_up: She is showing {card}. The other one is face down.
blackjack.cube_help: The Cube has seen the hole card. It is {card}. It says nothing, but it is very obvious about it.
blackjack.hint: HIT for another, STAND to hold.
blackjack.bust: {total}. Over. She does not need to do anything at all.
blackjack.reveal: She turns the hole card over. {card}.
blackjack.dealer_bust: {total}. She has gone over, and she takes it well.
blackjack.push: Both on {total}. Nothing happens, which she seems to enjoy.
blackjack.next_hand: She gathers the cards and deals again.
blackjack.victory: "Two out of three," says the Reckoner, squaring the deck. "I have sat here through four hundred and six of those and I remember every one, and I would like you to know that I do not think you are lucky. I think you are a problem. Take something and go."
blackjack.defeat: "That is the arithmetic," says the Reckoner, squaring the deck. "It is not personal and it was never going to be. Come back when you have more to put down."
blackjack.penalty: Losing to the house costs you {amount}. You are on {hp}.

peek: Pip gets there first, looks in, and makes a note.
Pip inspects the contents, consults the clipboard, and steps aside.

companion.recovered: {name} has shaken it off and is back to full.
companion.down: {name} is out of service. A safe room will bring them back; nothing else will.
companion.rejoins: {name} catches you up on the stairs, half-mended and not discussing it.
companion.absorbs_pounce: {name} gets in the way of it. Deliberately, and first, and without being asked.
companion.assigned:
You write the name on the line at 4(b). It is the only part of the form you fill in yourself and it takes four seconds and it is, on reflection, the only decision anybody has let you make so far.

{name} is already out there. The arbitration provided some time ago and then did nothing further about it, and so {name} has been in that corridor longer than you have been in this building, and nobody has ever asked whether they wanted the job.

They will fall in beside you when you go through. They do not ask what you are disputing. They already know how this goes.

default.opening:
Good morning, and welcome to Binding Physical Arbitration!

I'll be your commentary track. I'm contractually required to be here, so let's both make the best of it.

Quick orientation: there are thirteen floors and thirteen clauses. Beat all thirteen and your contract is void. Don't, and you're processed as inventory. Four billion people accepted these terms without reading them. You read them. Frankly that's the most interesting thing about you.

The stream is doing very well. Do try to look up occasionally.
default.tutorial_move: Type a direction to move. N, S, E, W. Type LOOK to look again. Type HELP if this is already going badly.
default.tutorial_take: TAKE opens whatever's in the room. Yes, you can just take it. Nobody here is going to stop you. Nobody here is going to stop you at all, which you might want to think about.
default.tutorial_rest: This is a safe room. REST recovers your health and your abilities, once. Only once, so don't waste it on a scratch. Nothing follows you in here. I'd love to tell you why. I would genuinely love to.
default.tutorial_map: Oh, that's a good pull. It's been logging your route since you walked in, whether or not you had it. Type MAP. You'll want it when something's following you, and something will be.
default.tutorial_talk: There's someone here. TALK to them. Most things on this floor want to hurt you. This one mostly wants company, which is arguably worse.
default.pre_boss:
That door goes to the Orientation Suite. Behind it is the Enforcement Entity for Clause 1.

I'd suggest resting first, if you have a rest left. I'd also suggest reading Clause 1, but we both know how that went last time.
default.secret_room:
Somebody lived in here. Four hundred and change days, by the wall.

They got out. Downward, but out. I'm not supposed to tell you that, so I'll say it once and we'll move on.
default.boss_intro:
Here we go. {clause}.

{boss} is through there, and it has been through there a very long time.
default.floor_cleared:
{clause} disputed.

That is another one. {left} to go.
default.safe_room: Take the moment. There aren't many.
default.death:
And that's the run.

For what it's worth, you got further than most. For what it's worth, that isn't worth much. You will be processed, itemised, and shelved, and I will be assigned to somebody new by the end of the shift.

I'd like it on record that I didn't enjoy that.
default.death_continue:
Hold on. Hold on.

First-day reprieve. It's in the onboarding pack, it's real, and nobody ever reads far enough to claim it. You're claiming it. It comes out of something, later, and I don't know what, and neither does anyone I've asked.
default.continue_spent:
You're up. Half health, back at the start of the floor, and one fewer thing between you and whatever this costs.

Don't waste it.
default.palette_break: That's not right. That's not - hold on. That's not supposed to happen until much further down.
default.muted:
Fine.

No, it's fine.

I'll be here.
default.voice_switch: Switching commentary track. Same building, different opinion about it.
default.descend:
Next floor. Whatever was following you upstairs is not following you down; they are floor staff, and this is not their floor.

Small mercy. Enjoy it.
default.floor2_arrival:
Clause 2. Fees and Charges.

This floor exists because somebody had to pay for the arbitration, and the arbitration decided it should be you. Everything down here is a cost that grew legs.

It's wet. Mind the coins. There are more of them than there should be, and they are not all the way at the bottom of anything.
default.tutorial_dice:
That's the Coin Diver. He'll play you for something. He's honest, in the way of people who don't need to cheat, which is a different and slightly worse thing than the ghost upstairs.

Five dice each. Bid on how many of both sets show a number or better. Call LIAR when you think he's overreached.
default.miniboss_intro:
The Deductible. It sits on the crossing and takes a portion of everything that passes.

It is not the boss. It's worse in one specific way: it will still be here in principle after you kill it. That's what a deductible is.
default.f2_secret:
Somebody breached the wall here from the other side. Recently.

Eleven disputed before you, which makes you twelve, and I am fairly sure there is a thirteenth in here now as well although nobody tells me anything. Somebody came through this wall going the same direction as you, and they were in a hurry, and they left the good stuff behind.
default.f2_pre_boss:
The sound ahead is a machine that has been running a very long time without anyone winning.

Ledgermaw. It holds every fee this building has ever levied, and it has never once paid out. Rest first if you can. It does not get tired.
default.floor_cleared_2:
Clause 2 disputed.

Two down. You are now, by the arbitration's own accounting, worth negative money to them, which is the first genuinely good news you've had.

Eleven to go.
default.voices_onset:
Right. So.

I want to be clear that I did not do that, and I cannot hear it, and my instrumentation says this room is empty.

I am obliged to log it. I am not obliged to say what I think it is, and I'm not going to.
default.floor3_arrival:
Clause 3. Limitation of Liability.

This is the archive where they work out exactly how little you are worth. It flooded some time ago, which they have decided is nobody's fault, which is the entire clause in one sentence.

Mind the shelves. Some of them still have opinions.
default.f3_actuary:
That one's harmless. Genuinely harmless, which is rare enough down here to mention.

Talk to her. She has been trying to give something away for a very long time and nobody has stopped long enough to take it.
default.f3_secret:
Another breach, same tool marks as Clause 2.

Whoever it is, they're going down faster than you and they're not stopping for the loot. I don't know whether that's confidence or panic.
default.f3_pre_boss:
The Cap is through there.

It limits what any single blow is worth. That is not a metaphor; you will hit it properly and only a fraction will count. If you found what the actuary was holding, use it. If you didn't, this is going to take a while and you're going to get tired.
default.floor_cleared_3:
Clause 3 disputed.

Three down. Their liability to you is now formally unlimited, which nobody has ever managed before, and somewhere upstairs a very small alarm has gone off in a room with nobody in it.
default.floor4_arrival:
Clause 4. Acceptable Use.

It's a housing estate. I know. It's a real one, or it's a very good one, and I have never been able to work out which and I have had a lot of time.

The hedges are trimmed. The bins are out on the correct day. Nobody here will raise their voice at you even once, and by the third street you will wish they would.
default.f4_postman:
He's got a full bag and a round he's been doing since before the acquisition.

He'll play you for something. Best of five. He's honest, and he will absolutely tell you if you're cheating, and he will absolutely keep delivering afterwards.
default.f4_miniboss:
The Committee.

They have reviewed your conduct. They met about it. There were minutes, and the minutes were circulated, and you were not sent a copy because you are not on the list.
default.f4_secret:
This shed isn't on the estate plan. I've checked twice.

Somebody built it without permission, which on this floor is the single most dangerous thing a person can do, and they got away with it long enough to fill it.
default.f4_pre_boss:
Number 14.

Mrs Hensley is not the strongest thing in this building. She is the best connected. She has already called someone, and they are already coming, and they will keep coming.

Don't let it turn into a street. End it in the house.
default.floor_cleared_4:
Clause 4 disputed.

Four down. Nine to go.

The estate is still out there behind you, bins out, hedges level, and I would very much like you to keep walking.
default.merchant_first:
Oh, him.

He is not staff, he is not a disputant, and he has been in this building longer than the acquisition. I have raised it. Repeatedly. The answer that comes back is that he is not in scope.

He is the only thing down here that will give you a straight price. Buy from him.
default.merchant_again: He got here before you did. He always does. I have stopped putting it in the log.
default.floor5_arrival:
Clause 5. Data Retention.

Everything the arbitration has ever recorded is down here, and it has never deleted anything, because the schedule says retain and nobody has ever written the second half of the schedule.

The staff are still on shift. They have been on shift for a very long time and they are not going to acknowledge that, and I would ask you not to raise it.
default.f5_miniboss:
The Backup.

It repairs itself between rounds. Not dramatically, just steadily, the way a backup does, and if you cannot out-damage the repair you will be here until one of you gets bored and it will not be it.

It is carrying something you want.
default.f5_secret:
Somebody has been sleeping in the tape library.

Recently. There's a coat over the racks and the coat is dry, which on this floor means somebody put it there after the flood two floors up, which means they came the same way you did.
default.f5_pre_boss:
RAID-6.

Six arrays. It loses one and rebuilds it from the other five, and it will do that all night, and it does not tire and it does not get bored.

The Backup was carrying the parity disk. If you have it, use it before you swing. If you do not, go back for it. I am being unusually direct with you here.
default.floor_cleared_5:
Clause 5 disputed.

Five down. Your record has been deleted, which is the first thing this building has ever destroyed on purpose, and it did not enjoy it.

Eight to go. I am starting to think you might.
default.floor6_arrival:
Clause 6. Intellectual Property.

This floor is a shop, and the shop sells you.

Everything the arbitration has made out of your likeness is displayed down here in ascending order of indignity, and it goes on for some time, and I would suggest not stopping to read the price tags.

One more thing. This floor holds the rights to your best moments. You will find that nothing you do here lands quite as hard as it should.
default.f6_miniboss:
The Focus Group.

Eight people behind glass with clipboards who have been asked what they think of you and are going to say it.

They bring in more participants when engagement drops. That is not a metaphor either.
default.f6_secret:
A storeroom of things that failed to test.

Everything in here is a version of you that the arbitration decided not to sell. Some of them are close. One of them is very close, and it is face down, and I would leave it face down.
default.f6_pre_boss:
The Likeness.

It is built from your file. It has your armour class, roughly three times your health, and it has watched every fight you have had since Intake.

It is not a copy of who you are. It is a copy of what you have done, which is worse, and which you will recognise.
default.floor_cleared_6:
Clause 6 disputed.

Six down. Seven to go. You own your own face again, which sounds like nothing and is not nothing.

The merchandise is still selling. That is a separate contract and I am not going to pretend otherwise.
default.floor7_arrival:
Clause 7. Force Majeure.

Circumstances beyond reasonable control. That is the whole clause and it is the only clause in the contract with no second sentence, because a second sentence would be a limit, and the drafters did not want one.

I want to say something about the light. I am going to say it once and then we will both carry on as though I did not.

It is not supposed to do that yet.
default.f7_miniboss:
The Exception.

It is the carve-out that makes the whole clause work, and it is the only thing on this floor that behaves consistently, and it is carrying something that matters on thirteen.

Take it seriously. It is the last predictable thing you will meet down here.
default.f7_secret:
There is a hole in the roof.

Not a breach, not tool marks. A hole, going up, into weather. Somebody stood here and looked at that and then kept going down, and I would like it on record that I do not think I would have.
default.f7_pre_boss:
Kaleidon.

It reconfigures every round. Armour, shape, the lot. Nothing you learn about it in round one is true in round two, and there is no version of this where you work it out and then win.

You win by having enough left. That is all. Go in full.
default.floor_cleared_7:
Clause 7 disputed.

Seven. Over half.

And the colour has stayed. I have checked the schedule four times since we came down here and there is no entry for it, no work order, no authorisation.

Somebody turned it on for you. I do not know who and I have stopped pretending I might.
default.floor8_arrival:
Clause 8. Indemnification.

A foundry. They melt down the debts here and pour them into something that can be carried, and the people carrying it are the people who owed it.

Six paperclips a room. That is the indemnity and it is not negotiable and it is, by the standards of this building, extremely cheap.
default.f8_miniboss:
The Surety.

It stands behind other people's obligations, which sounds noble until you learn what it does when they cannot pay.

It is between you and the pour floor.
default.f8_map:
Somebody left a survey in that crate.

Full floor plan, this floor, every room, drawn by hand. Whoever has been one step ahead of you since Clause 1 stopped here long enough to map the whole thing, and then left the map where you would find it.

That is not a coincidence. That has not been a coincidence for some time.
default.f8_secret:
The moulds in here are person-shaped.

I am going to leave that where it is.
default.f8_pre_boss:
The Guarantor.

Everything you do to it lands half on your companion. That is the indemnity: your loss is somebody else's to carry, and it has chosen who.

If your companion is hurt, that fight is shorter than you want it to be. Rest first. I am asking.
default.floor_cleared_8:
Clause 8 disputed.

Eight down. Five to go, and the five below are the ones nobody has ever seen, and I mean that literally: I have no content for floors nine to thirteen. There is a gap in my brief where they should be.

We find out together. I did not expect to be saying that.
default.floor9_arrival:
Clause 9. Severability.

This is the clause that means the rest of the contract survives when one part of it fails. Down here they took that literally, and the floor is in pieces, and the pieces are all still in force.

You disputed Clause 3 and it did not bring the building down. This is why. This floor is why.
default.f9_left_half:
That is half of something.

The other half is on this floor somewhere and while it is standing, this one cannot be properly hurt. They are not severable, which on this floor of all floors is a joke somebody made deliberately.

Kill this half first and the other gets easier. Or don't, and fight the hard version twice.
default.f9_secret:
A whole room. Intact, four walls, nothing missing.

On this floor that is remarkable enough that somebody used it to store the things they did not want cut in half.
default.f9_pre_boss:
Rest here. Properly.

And listen: clearing this clause grants you a reprieve. One. If you go down after this, you get back up, once, and it comes out of something I still cannot identify.

I would rather you did not need it. You are going to need it.
default.floor_cleared_9:
Clause 9 disputed.

Nine. And the severability clause is the one holding the other twelve together, so what you just did will be felt upward.

You have a reprieve now. Four floors left. I have never had anyone this far and I am aware that I am talking more than usual.
default.floor10_arrival:
Clause 10. Governing Law.

A courthouse. It is the correct shape for a courthouse and none of the distances between the rooms agree with each other, and I have stopped trying to draw it.

Everything here runs on procedure. Nothing exists until it is entered into the record, including the doors. LOOK properly in every room or you will walk in circles very formally.
default.f10_miniboss:
The Clerk of the Court.

Not a judge. Something better: the person who decides what the judge sees. Forty years of deciding what gets in front of Vorn and what quietly does not.

Your file has been through those hands. All of it.
default.f10_secret:
The evidence store.

Everything that was excluded. Every document that was not admitted, going back before the acquisition, boxed and labelled and kept, because the one thing this building will not do is destroy a record.

Somebody has been in here reading. Recently. For a long time.
default.f10_pre_boss:
Justice Vorn.

Three phases, and the middle one is not a fight. It is a game of dice, in chambers, because Vorn has decided that is how this part of the hearing will be conducted and there is no appeal from that.

Win it and you take a very large piece out of the judgment. Lose it and it hurts and you carry on. Either way, play.
default.floor_cleared_10:
Clause 10 disputed.

Ten. There is no governing law now. There is no jurisdiction and no forum and no court, and the last three clauses are going to have to enforce themselves without one.

That is going to make them worse, not better. I want to be honest with you about that.
default.floor11_arrival:
Clause 11. Modification of Terms.

They can change it whenever they like and your continued presence is your agreement to whatever it now says.

So the floor changes. Rooms rewrite between visits. The shape stays put, the doors stay put, but what is in them and what they are does not.

Your map is going to be wrong. It is not broken. It is just describing a version that has been superseded.
default.f11_miniboss:
The Redline.

It is the tracked-changes view of everything you have done since Intake, rendered as a thing, and every one of your decisions is marked up in the margin with a query.

It is not hostile exactly. It just wants to know why you did it that way.
default.f11_secret:
The original.

One room they have never amended, because you cannot amend a thing you have lost, and somebody hid this copy before the first revision went through.

Somebody who is one floor ahead of you and has been for eleven floors.
default.f11_pre_boss:
The Amendment.

It changes its own terms mid-fight. Armour, resilience, the lot, and it repairs itself between rounds because the current version is always the one in force.

There is a limit to how many times it can be reissued. Five. Count them.
default.floor_cleared_11:
Clause 11 disputed.

Eleven.

They cannot change the terms any more. What is written now is what is written, and there are two clauses left, and they are both exactly what they said they were going to be from the start.

Twelve is Termination. Thirteen is Entire Agreement. You have read them. You are the only person in four billion who has.
default.wall_secret: I have been in this building for a very long time and I did not know that was there. I want to be clear that I am not being modest. I did not know.
default.boss_intro_1:
Here we go. {clause}.

The Greeter has been on this floor since before the acquisition. He is genuinely pleased to see you. That is not a tactic. That is somehow the problem.
default.boss_intro_2:
Here we go. {clause}.

Ledgermaw holds every fee this building has ever levied and has never once paid out. It has been waiting forty years for a player.
default.boss_intro_3:
Here we go. {clause}.

The Cap limits what any single blow is worth. If the actuary gave you the exception, read it out in the room. If she did not, this is going to take a long time.
default.boss_intro_4:
Here we go. {clause}.

Mrs Hensley is not the strongest thing in this building. She is the best connected. She has already called someone, and they are already coming, and they will keep coming.
default.boss_intro_5:
Here we go. {clause}.

RAID-6 loses an array and rebuilds it from the other five. Six times, and no more. If you have the parity disk, use it before you swing.
default.boss_intro_6:
Here we go. {clause}.

The Likeness is built from your own file: your armour, three times your health, and six floors of footage of how you fight.
default.boss_intro_7:
Here we go. {clause}.

Kaleidon reconfigures every round. Nothing you learn about it in round one is true in round two. You do not out-think this one; you outlast it.
default.boss_intro_8:
Here we go. {clause}.

The Guarantor redirects a third of everything you do onto your companion. If they are hurt, this fight is shorter than you want it to be.
default.boss_intro_9:
Here we go. {clause}.

Hemikin. If you took the left half upstairs, this is the diminished version. If you did not, there are two of them and they are standing back to back.
default.boss_intro_10:
Here we go. {clause}.

Justice Vorn presides. Three phases, and the middle one is not a fight, and there is no appeal from that.
default.boss_intro_11:
Here we go. {clause}.

The Amendment changes its own terms mid-fight and reissues itself when it is hurt. Five times. Count them.
default.floor12_arrival: Clause 12. Termination. They can end this whenever they like and you cannot, which is the whole clause and always has been. So they are ending it. Not because of you. It has been winding down since before the acquisition and you have simply arrived at the part where somebody turns the lights off. Watch the ash. It is not ash.
default.f12_miniboss: The Final Notice. Everything on this floor has had one. This is the one that gets delivered by hand.
default.f12_secret: Somebody has been salvaging. Systematically, floor by floor, taking only what would still work after the shutdown. They knew this was coming. They have known for eleven floors.
default.f12_pre_boss: The Reaper of Records. It is an actual dragon. I have been building to this since Intake and I would like a moment to enjoy it. It eats records. Every file this building ever kept, including yours, is inside it, and it has been consuming them steadily since termination began. Rest first.
default.floor_cleared_12: Clause 12 disputed. Twelve. One left, and it is the one nobody has ever described to me. My brief stops here. Whatever is on thirteen, we find out at the same time, and I have decided I am glad about that.
default.floor13_arrival: Clause 13. Entire Agreement. It is white. That is not a description, that is the whole floor. No corridors, no signage, no fittings, no ceiling that I can find. Nothing on this floor is trying to hurt you with any conviction. There are no terms left. There is one room somewhere down here with somebody in it, and I am going to stop talking for a while.
default.f13_miniboss: The Recital. It reads the agreement aloud. All of it. That is the attack.
default.f13_secret: A cupboard. On a floor with no walls, somebody has built a cupboard, and put things in it, and closed the door.
default.f13_eleven: Eleven benches. I have counted them four times. Ten of them have been sat on and one of them has not.
default.f13_pre_boss: Through there. Take as long as you want. It is not going anywhere and neither, for once, is anything else.
default.finale_intro: Right. So I am going to say this now because I will not get another chance. Four billion people accepted. Eleven disputed before you. Ten of them are on this floor somewhere and the eleventh has been ahead of you since Clause 1, leaving kettles on. You are the twelfth, and there is a thirteenth in here already, four floors back, and the gap is getting shorter every time. Whatever happens in the next few minutes, you got here, and I was here for it, and that is the only part of this job I have ever wanted.
default.finale_signed: Ah. Well. It is over, and it ended the way it was drafted to end, and nobody could say you did not read it. You read all of it. You are the only one who did.
default.finale_withdrawn:
You withdrew. Under the original Clause 1, before anybody amended it, in front of the only party with authority to accept it.

It is done. It is actually done.
default.finale_fought: It did not fight back properly. You know that. I know that. I am not going to put it in the log that way, and neither are you, and we will both know.
default.merchant_last: He is packing up. Not hurrying. Just packing up, in order, the way somebody does at the end of a very long market day.
default.merchant_end: He is here. On thirteen. There is nothing on this floor to sell to and nobody to sell it to and he has set the table up anyway, and I think that is the point.
default.withdraw_1: You cannot withdraw. There is no mechanism. I have looked.
default.withdraw_2: Saying it again does not create a mechanism. Although I note that you are keeping count and so am I.
default.withdraw_3: You have said this several times now. Nothing in my brief covers what to do if somebody simply keeps asking.
default.withdraw_4: Still no mechanism. Still logging it. Carry on.
default.withdraw_filed: Thirteen. One per clause. That is not nothing, that is a pattern of conduct, and a pattern of conduct is a thing that goes in a file. It has gone in a file.
default.photo_found: That is five. Same beach, same two people, same photograph, in every safe room in this building. Somebody has been putting it up as they go. They are putting it up for whoever comes next. That is you. That has always been you.
default.boss_intro_12:
Here we go. {clause}.

{boss} is an actual dragon. I have been building to this since Intake and I would like a moment. Every record this building ever kept is inside it and it has been eating steadily since termination began.
default.merch_set: Forty-one million units. At nought per cent. I have processed that statement eleven times and I have never once been able to say it out loud until now.

help.combat:
HOW COMBAT WORKS

Everything is a twenty-sided die. Roll d20,
add your modifiers, compare to the target's
Armour Class. Meet or beat it and you hit.

  TO HIT   d20 + stat mod + proficiency
           vs the enemy's AC
  DAMAGE   weapon dice + stat mod
  NAT 20   auto hit, damage dice doubled
  NAT 1    auto miss, and a bad time

Stat mod is (stat - 10) halved, rounded
down. So 16 STR is +3. Proficiency starts
at +2 and rises with level. It is all on
your SHEET.

TURN ORDER is rolled once per fight, d20 +
DEX. You, your companion and every enemy
act in that order, round after round.

ON YOUR TURN, one of:
  ATTACK          swing your weapon
  <ability name>  OBJECTION, BRACE, and so
                  on. Limited uses. REST
                  restores them.
  USE <item>      costs your turn, not
                  your life
  FLEE            d20 + DEX vs the fastest
                  enemy. Survivors follow.

AT 0 HP you are down, not dead. Each turn
you roll a death save: DC 10. Three passes
stabilises you at 1 HP. Three fails ends
the run. Your companion may haul you up.

Damage is permanent until you REST in a
safe room. A fight won at half health is
not a fight won cheaply.

PACING
  PACE SLOW    pause between turns
  PACE FAST    print the round at once
  PACE MANUAL  press Enter between turns
help.pace:
PACE SLOW    pause briefly between each combatant's turn (default)
PACE FAST    print the whole round at once
PACE MANUAL  wait for Enter between turns
help.combat_primer:
COMBAT, QUICKLY
  d20 + modifiers vs enemy AC to hit.
  Nat 20 crits. Nat 1 misses, badly.
  Turn order was rolled at the start.
  ATTACK, an ability by name, USE <item>,
  or FLEE. At 0 HP you get death saves.

  Type COMBAT for the full explanation,
  PACE FAST to stop the turn pauses.
help.stats:
Five stats. STR and DEX decide how hard you hit with most weapons, INT and CHA with a few. CON is health. Every stat gives a modifier of (stat - 10) halved and rounded down, so 16 is +3 and 10 is +0.

That modifier is added to your attack rolls and your damage. DEX also adds to your armour class, which is the number an enemy has to beat to hit you, and to turn order.

HP is how much you can take before you go down. AC is how often you get hit at all. The Vanguard has the most of both; the Hexwright has the least and hits hardest.

You can see all of this any time with SHEET, and the full combat rules with COMBAT.

briefing.open: Before you go down, the arbitration is required to explain what you are and what you can do with it. Nobody has ever stayed for this part. You have, which is already more than the last eleven managed.
briefing.stats:
You have five numbers. They are abbreviated everywhere in this building because somebody decided in 1974 that full words were an extravagance.

STR is Strength. It swings heavy things: axes, hammers, lengths of pipe.

DEX is Dexterity. It swings fast things, and it feeds into your armour class and who moves first in a fight.

CON is Constitution. It is how much you can absorb before you go down, and it grows every time you level.

INT is Intelligence. Down here that means knowing which clause applies, which turns out to be a weapon.

CHA is Charisma. It is arguing. On several floors that works better than the axe.

Each number gives a modifier: take the score, subtract 10, halve it, round down. So 16 is +3 and 10 is nothing at all. That modifier is added to whether you hit and to how much it hurts when you do. Your class decides which of the five is the one that matters for you.
briefing.abilities:
You will also have abilities: named things you can do instead of swinging, typed by name, like OBJECTION or BRACE.

Each has a limited number of uses and they do not come back on their own. Resting in a safe room restores them. That is the entire economy of this place, and you will spend the whole descent deciding whether the thing in front of you is worth one of your uses or whether something worse is coming.

You start with one. You gain more as you accrue standing, and the later ones are considerably less polite than the first.
briefing.companion:
You do not go down alone. Clause 4(b) says a party in dispute may be accompanied, and that the arbitration will provide, and the arbitration has provided, and what it has provided is waiting in the corridor and has been for some time.

Nobody will tell you where they came from. They were all here before you were, they all know the building better than you do, and not one of them has ever been asked whether they wanted the job.

Your companion fights on its own turn, takes roughly one attack in eight that was meant for you, and mends a little for every room you walk. Each one has a passive that is always working and each one is better at exactly one thing.

Most importantly: if you go down, most of them will pick you back up. Once per fight. If your companion is out of service, that does not happen, and a bad round becomes the end of the run. Look after it.
briefing.close:
That is the briefing. It is not complete and the parts it leaves out are the parts that would help.

Type SHEET at any point to see your numbers, COMBAT for the full rules, and HELP for everything you can type.

Now choose what you are, and who is coming with you.
briefing.defence:
Two numbers decide whether you survive a room, and they are not the same thing.

HP is how much you can take. It goes down when something lands and it does not come back on its own: only resting in a safe room, levelling up, or drinking something restores it.

AC is Armour Class, and it is how often anything lands at all. Everything that attacks you rolls a twenty-sided die, adds its own number, and compares the total to your AC. Beat it and they hit you. Fail and they do not, and it costs you nothing whatsoever.

Your AC starts at 10, plus your Dexterity modifier, plus whatever your class is built for, plus your armour. Armour is the part you control. A hi-vis vest is worth 2; there is a slag plate on Clause 8 worth 8, and something on Clause 11 worth 11.

This is why the merchant is worth finding. Two points of AC does not sound like much and it is roughly a tenth of every attack in the building missing you instead of connecting. Over a floor, it is the difference between arriving at the boss and not.

r01.name: Service Stairwell
r01.desc: A concrete stairwell, one flight down from Clause 1. Water at the bottom. A door south.
r01.long:
The stairs are concrete and unlit and go down further than one floor should need.

At the bottom the water starts: ankle deep, moving slowly left to right, carrying a steady quiet traffic of coins along the bottom.

The door at the bottom is propped open with a fire extinguisher. Somebody wanted this door to stay open. Somebody was thinking about coming back.

r02.name: Fee Junction
r02.desc: A four-way junction, shin deep. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
Four channels meet here and the water turns slowly in the middle, working a raft of coins round and round without ever taking them anywhere.

On the wall, a brass plate: SCHEDULE OF CHARGES. The schedule beneath it has been prised off. The screw holes are still there, four of them, and one bent screw.

r03.name: Overflow Channel
r03.desc: A brick channel running west. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
The brickwork here is older than the building above it, which raises questions you set aside immediately.

High on the wall, a tidemark. Then another, higher. Then a third, near the ceiling, with a date scratched beside it that has not happened yet.

r04.name: Silt Trap
r04.desc: A dead end where the channel widens and drops everything it was carrying. Door east.
r04.long:
The channel widens and slows, and everything it was carrying settles out here: coins, obviously, but also buttons, a shoe, keys, a wedding ring, a child's plastic dinosaur.

All of it sorted by weight rather than by worth, which feels like the building being honest for once.

There is a strongbox in the silt, on its side, hinges up.
r04.chest_hint: A strongbox has settled in the silt, hinges up.

r05.name: Coin Cascade
r05.desc: A room where coins fall constantly from a gap in the ceiling. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
Coins come down from a gap in the ceiling in a thin continuous stream, have done for years, and have built a cone on the floor nearly to the roof.

The stream never stops. Nobody is feeding it. Directly above this room, on Clause 1, is the Lost Property store, and you decide not to think about what that means about the numbered tags.

r06.name: The Dry Vault
r06.desc: A vault above the waterline, door hanging open. Someone is in here. Door west.
r06.long:
A step up, and dry for the first time since the stairs. The vault door is a foot of steel and hangs fully open, which means it was opened from inside.

Racking, mostly empty. A folding chair. A crate on its end with five dice on it, and a man sitting cross-legged behind them, dripping.
r06.npc_hint: There is a man sitting behind five dice, and he has seen you.

r07.name: Pump House
r07.desc: A pump house, dry, warm, and loud. It is safe here. Doors north, east and south.
r07.long:
The pump has been running since before any of this and will be running after.

It is enormously loud and the noise is somehow restful: the first thing in this building doing an honest job. The platform around it is dry and above the waterline, and there is a bench worn smooth by people who came before you and also needed to sit down.

Nothing follows you in here either. You are starting to have a theory about that.

r08.name: Central Sump
r08.desc: The deep middle of the floor, waist deep. Doors north, west, east and south.
r08.long:
The floor drops away and the water comes to your waist, cold enough to take the breath out of you.

Underfoot it is not silt. It is coins, packed down over decades into something that gives slightly and then does not, and walking on it is like walking on a beach made entirely of somebody's money.

r09.name: Tariff Steps
r09.desc: A short flight of steps, each one a different depth. Doors west, north, east and south.
r09.long:
Steps down, then up, then down further, in no pattern.

Each riser has a figure stamped into it. They do not increase in any order that makes sense, and one of them is negative, and that one has been worn shiny by people stopping to look at it.

r10.name: Small Charges
r10.desc: A low side chamber full of shelved boxes. Doors west and south.
r10.long:
Shelves of small grey boxes above the waterline, each labelled with an amount too small to argue about.

That is the point of them. Each one is beneath contesting. There are perhaps nine thousand boxes.

r11.name: Grease Channel
r11.desc: A channel where the water carries a skin of something else. Doors north, east and south.
r11.long:
Something floats on the surface here, thick and pale, and the coins do not sink through it; they sit on top, held up, glinting.

It is not unpleasant to look at. It is extremely unpleasant to walk through.

r12.name: The Confluence
r12.desc: Where three channels meet and argue. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
Three channels meet here at slightly wrong angles and the water fights about it, permanently, in a slow rotating quarrel.

Things brought here from three directions circle and never leave. You watch a laminated notice go past twice.

r13.name: The Toll Crossing
r13.desc: A narrow crossing over the deep channel, with something sitting on it. Doors north, west, east and south.
r13.long:
The only crossing over the deep channel: a steel walkway, one person wide, with a gate arm across the middle.

Something is sitting on the gate. It does not appear to be guarding the crossing so much as owning a percentage of it.

r14.name: Excess Store
r14.desc: Where the portions taken at the crossing get put. Doors north and west.
r14.long:
This is where the portions go.

Not money. Portions of other things: one sleeve of a coat, the heel of a shoe, four pages torn from the middle of a passport, the middle third of a photograph.

Each one taken from something that then had to carry on without it. There is a case here that nobody came back for.
r14.chest_hint: There is a case here that nobody came back for.

r15.name: West Gallery
r15.desc: A long gallery running south, water to the knee. Doors north, east and south.
r15.long:
A long gallery with an arched roof, and the acoustics turn every drip into somebody else's footstep.

You stop twice to listen and both times it is nothing. The third time you do not stop, on principle.

r16.name: Reconciliation
r16.desc: A wide flat room where the water lies still. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
The water is completely still here, unnervingly so, and about a foot deep, and perfectly clear.

Under it the floor is tiled in a mosaic: two columns of figures, running the length of the room, that have never once balanced. Somebody laid this by hand, knowing that.

r17.name: East Gallery
r17.desc: The gallery's other arm, colder. Doors north, west and south.
r17.long:
Colder than the west gallery, and the coins here are older: thinner, softer, worn almost smooth.

You pick one up. You cannot tell what it was. You put it back, which surprises you slightly.

r18.name: The Breach
r18.desc: A hole knocked through the wall from the far side. Door east.
r18.long:
Someone came through this wall from the outside, with something heavy, not long ago.

The rubble is on this side, so they were leaving somewhere worse. Beyond the hole is a crawlspace that goes back further than your light reaches, and a smell of open air that this building has no business having.

They left a pack behind. They did not need it, or they could not carry it, and only one of those is good news.
r18.chest_hint: There is a pack here, left behind in a hurry.

r19.name: Second Pump House
r19.desc: The floor's other pump house. Dry, loud, safe. Doors north, west and east.
r19.long:
The twin of the first, same pump, same bench, same restful racket.

On the bench, someone has left a mug, upside down and clean, in the exact position a person leaves a mug when they mean to come back for it. It is the same mug from the break room upstairs.

Whoever this is, they are one floor ahead of you and they are keeping it tidy.

r20.name: Count Room Approach
r20.desc: A ramp rising out of the water. It gets louder ahead. Doors north, west, east and south.
r20.long:
The floor ramps up and the water finally lets go of you.

Ahead, through the wall, is a sound you last heard in an arcade: reels turning, stopping, turning again. It has been doing that for a long time, and it has not stopped for you.

r21.name: The Count Room
r21.desc: A room of long steel tables and one very tidy occupant. Doors north, west and east.
r21.long:
Long steel counting tables, scales, sorting trays, and a wall of canvas bags stacked by denomination.

Everything is immaculate. The pens are squared to the edges of the folders. The folders are squared to the edges of the tables.

Somebody stands up as you come in, and takes their time about it, and looks pleased to have something to check.
r21.chest_hint: There is a cash cabinet under the far table.

r22.name: Staff Lockers
r22.desc: A row of lockers, mostly forced. Door west.
r22.long:
Staff lockers. Most have been forced, long ago, and emptied.

One is intact. Inside: a coat, a photograph of the same beach, and a full set of arbitration merchandise still in its packaging, employee discount sticker on the front.

They bought the merchandise. That is the detail that stays with you.
