r22.item_hint: There is merchandise here, still in its packaging.

r23.name: Payout Corridor
r23.desc: A corridor of dead payout windows. Doors north and south.
r23.long:
A corridor of payout windows, nine of them, every shutter down.

Under each window the floor is worn into a shallow dish by people who stood there. Not one of the dishes leads anywhere. Nine queues, nine hollows, no payouts.

The noise ahead is very close now.

r24.name: The Jackpot Floor
r24.desc: A vast room built around one machine. One door north.
r24.long:
The room is enormous and it holds one machine.

Ledgermaw stands three storeys high in the middle of a floor of packed coin, reels turning, lights running in sequence, and every fee this building has ever charged is inside it. You can hear them shifting.

It has been running without an audience for forty years. As you step onto the coin floor, the reels slow, and it turns its front toward you with an eagerness that is much, much worse than hostility.

It has been waiting for a player.

r10m.name: The Dry Ledge
r10m.desc: A ledge above the waterline with a folding table on it. Doors west and south.
r10m.long:
A concrete ledge two feet above the water, wide enough for a table, and there is a table on it.

Behind the table, a man on a folding stool with a bag at his feet that is far too small for the amount of stock arranged in front of him.

He has a lamp, a flask, a tally book, and the settled air of somebody who has been open for business for a very long time and is not worried about footfall.

speaker: Something in the wall
Something two rooms over
Somebody who is not here
A voice with no room attached to it
Several people, at once, cheerfully
voices.onset:
Somebody answers.

Not in the room. Not from a direction. Just an answer, arriving, in the tone of a colleague leaning over a partition.
reply: "Oh, it talks. Say something else. Say something with a K in it, we like those."
"We have been having the same conversation for nine years and you have improved it enormously by turning up."
"Do you want to know what is behind you? No? Correct. Very good. Full marks."
"There were four of us this morning. There are four of us now. It is just that they are not the same four."
"You have lovely handwriting. We have seen your handwriting. We have seen you sign things you had not read."
"Somebody left a sandwich on Floor Six in nineteen ninety-one. We check on it. It is doing fine. Better than the man who left it."
"Keep walking, keep walking. Not that way. That way. No, we were joking, it was the first way. This is the most fun we have had in a decade."
"You are the only person who has ever answered us and we are going to be unbearable about it."
"Ask us about the lift. Go on. Ask us about the lift. THERE IS NO LIFT. Ha. That gets us every time."
"We do not know what we are either, if that helps. We suspect it does not help. It has never helped us."
"Everything in this building is load bearing, including the paperwork, including you."
"We counted the doors once. Twice, actually, and got two different numbers, and we have never told anybody that until now."
"Do the thing where you breathe. We love that. We used to do that."
"There is a room on this floor with nothing in it. We are not going to say which one. Enjoy the rest of your day."
"You have been very brave and we are not going to say about what, because you have not done it yet."
"If you meet a man with a folding table, tell him the seventh floor says he still owes us."
"We have opinions about your shoes. We are keeping them to ourselves. That is called professionalism."
"One of us used to work in payroll. We do not talk about it. It comes up constantly."
"Have you noticed the building is warm? It was not warm before you got here. Draw whatever conclusion you like, we have drawn ours."
"Nod if you can hear us. ...We cannot see you. That was a test and you have failed it beautifully."
"The thing about being a voice in a wall is that the commute is excellent."
"We are not haunting this place. We are ON THE ROTA. There is a difference and it is a difference of about forty pence an hour."
"We would like to be clear that we are not evil. We are just extremely bored and there are a lot of us."
"You will be fine. You will be fine. You will be fi- sorry, that was three, that sounds worse, doesn't it."
"Do you ever think about the fact that a door is just a wall that gave up?"
"Somebody has to remember the ninth floor and it has been us for a while now and we would very much like a hand with it."
"We have never once been asked how our day was. Not once. In eleven years. Anyway."
"There is a version of this where you and us are friends and it is going quite well and it is this one, in case that was unclear."
ambient: Somebody laughs, two rooms over, at nothing you can hear.
A conversation you cannot make out stops the moment you listen for it.
Somebody is counting, very quietly, and they are not near thirteen yet.
Something agrees with you. You had not said anything.
A kettle clicks off somewhere. Nobody put a kettle on.
Somebody says your name, in the friendliest way imaginable, from a room you have already been in.
A chair scrapes. Then it scrapes back, as though somebody thought better of standing up.
Somebody hums four notes and stops, embarrassed, as if they had been caught.
Somebody says "not yet" and it is not clear whether they are talking to you.
Somebody is being talked out of something, at length, in the next room, patiently.
A door closes politely, several floors up, and the sound arrives late.
Somebody starts to explain the building and gives up halfway through the first sentence.
Somebody says "tell them about the sandwich" and somebody else says "no".
A pen is being clicked, unhurriedly, by somebody with nothing else on.
Somebody in the wall says "go on then" with real warmth, to nobody.
Something moves through the floor above at exactly your walking pace, and stops when you stop.
Somebody sighs. It is the most human sound you have heard all day and there is nobody there.
Somebody says "eleven" and is immediately shushed.
Two voices disagree about what you are. Neither guess is flattering.
Somebody is reading the terms out loud, softly, to themselves, for comfort.
voices.payoff:
You have started finishing their sentences, and they have started letting you.

Something in you has settled that probably should not have. (+1 CHA)
voices.first: Finally. We have been going round in circles waiting for you to start.

r01.name: Archive Landing
r01.desc: A landing above the flood line. Shelving as far as the light goes. A stair down south.
r01.long:
The archive begins here and does not appear to end.

Shelving runs off in every direction to the limit of your light and past it, forty feet high, and about six feet up the whole thing goes into water. The water is perfectly still and perfectly clear and the shelves continue down through it, legible, for a long way.

r02.name: Index Hall
r02.desc: A hall of card indexes, thigh deep. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
Card index drawers, thousands of them, and the water has taken the bottom two rows.

You pull one at random. The cards are swollen and unreadable except the tab, which says a year that has not happened, and a number that is either a claim reference or a body count.

r03.name: Aisle 400-600
r03.desc: A flooded aisle running west. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
The aisle is numbered 400 to 600 and each number is a category of thing that can go wrong with a person.

You stop at 512. It is a good deal more specific than you were expecting. You do not stop at any of the others.

r04.name: Dead Files
r04.desc: Where closed cases were put. Door east.
r04.long:
Cases closed, boxed, and stacked to the ceiling, and every box lid is dated with the day the claim died rather than the day the claimant did.

The two dates are on the same label. They are rarely the same date. The gap is the whole business of this floor.

One box near the bottom has been opened recently and not put back straight.

r05.name: Aisle 601-800
r05.desc: A colder aisle. The water moves here. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
Something has disturbed the water in this aisle recently and it has not gone still again.

The shelves here hold the categories nobody wants to file under: unforeseeable, unattributable, nobody's fault. It is the largest section in the archive by a considerable margin.

r06.name: Reading Room
r06.desc: A reading room above the water. Lamps, desks, silence. Doors north, east and south.
r06.long:
Six feet up a mezzanine and suddenly dry.

Green-shaded lamps, long desks with brass fittings, and a silence that is not the archive's silence but a deliberate, maintained, do-not-disturb sort of silence.

One lamp is on over one desk. There is a chair pushed in. Nothing follows you up here.

r07.name: Central Stack
r07.desc: The middle of the archive. Waist deep. Doors north, west, east and south.
r07.long:
The shelving forms a rough square here around a well of open water, and the well goes down further than the floor should allow.

You can see shelves continuing down through it. There is a light on down there, or a reflection of yours, and you find you have been standing still for some time.

r08.name: Aisle 801-999
r08.desc: The last numbered aisle. Doors north, west, east and south.
r08.long:
The numbering stops at 999 and then there is one more shelf, unnumbered, with one box on it.

The box is empty. The label reads: RESERVED.

r09.name: Actuary's Office
r09.desc: A dry office off the stacks. Someone is working. Doors west and south.
r09.long:
A small office, dry, orderly, with a desk lamp and a ledger and a woman working at it who does not look up straight away.

When she does, she looks enormously relieved.

She has been calculating something for a very long time and has nobody to give the answer to.
r09.npc_hint: There is someone at the desk, and she has been waiting to be interrupted.

r23.name: Transfer Aisle
r23.desc: A short connecting aisle. Doors north, west and south.
r23.long:
A connecting aisle between sections, mostly empty racking.

Someone has written on the end panel in marker, at head height: THEY ARE ALL THE SAME FILE. It has been half-scrubbed off and then written again in a different hand.

r10.name: Aisle 200-399
r10.desc: An aisle where the shelves have gone over. Doors north, east and south.
r10.long:
Two shelving runs have come down against each other and formed a low tunnel you have to wade through bent double.

Under the water, the files have gone soft and fused into one continuous mass, which is exactly what the marker on the end panel said.

r11.name: Cross Aisle
r11.desc: A wide crossing. Doors north, west, east and south.
r11.long:
The main cross aisle. Wide enough for a trolley, and there is a trolley, jammed against a pillar and rusted into it.

On the trolley, one box, above the waterline, dry. It is empty and it has been dusted.

r12.name: Rejected Claims
r12.desc: An aisle that is fuller than the others. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
This aisle is packed floor to ceiling and along both sides and the shelves are bowing.

Rejected claims. There are more of these than every other category put together, and somebody has kept every single one, which suggests either extreme diligence or a plan.

r13.name: Underwriting
r13.desc: A room of long desks and dead calculators. Doors north and west.
r13.long:
Underwriting. Forty desks, forty mechanical calculators, all of them stopped mid-sum.

Every one is stopped on a different figure. You check six. They are all the same figure. You stop checking.

There is a cabinet at the end that the water has not reached.
r13.chest_hint: One cabinet at the end has stayed dry.

r14.name: Aisle 001-199
r14.desc: The first aisle. The oldest. Doors north, east and south.
r14.long:
The first files. Handwritten, on paper heavy enough to have survived the flood standing up.

The first one is dated a very long time ago and concerns a man who slipped on a step. It has been assessed, adjusted, reduced, and closed. He got nothing.

The handwriting is neat and it is not sorry.

r15.name: Aggregate Hall
r15.desc: A hall where every figure on the wall is a total. Doors north, west, east and south.
r15.long:
The walls are covered in totals: sums of sums, running along at chest height in a continuous band around the whole room.

None of them are itemised. You cannot tell what any of them is a total of, and following the band around brings you back to where you started with a different number to the one you left.

r16.name: The Adjuster's Room
r16.desc: A dry room with one desk and one occupant. Doors north, west and south.
r16.long:
Dry, warm, and lit by a single anglepoise over a single desk.

On the desk: your file. Open. Annotated in three colours.

Somebody is sitting behind it who has clearly been through the whole thing twice and would like to go through it once more with you present.
r16.chest_hint: There is a strongbox under the desk.

r17.name: Flooded Stairwell
r17.desc: A stairwell that goes the wrong way. Door east.
r17.long:
A stairwell going down into water that has no business being here; you are already below the sewer.

Someone has been through this wall too, same tool marks, and left in a hurry, and left a pack wedged in the banister where the water would not take it.

On the wall, freshly: 4 DOWN. KEEP GOING. It is not addressed to anyone.
r17.chest_hint: There is a pack wedged into the banister.

r18.name: Second Reading Room
r18.desc: Another dry mezzanine. Lamps, desks, safety. Doors north, west and east.
r18.long:
The twin of the first reading room, same lamps, same silence.

On the nearest desk, a cup. Cold, but recently cold, and beside it a sheet of paper with a list of thirteen items, four of them ticked.

The handwriting is the same as the marker on the end panel.

r19.name: Approach to Limits
r19.desc: The shelving stops here. Doors north, west, east and south.
r19.long:
The archive simply stops, and the last twenty feet before the far door are open floor and standing water and nothing at all.

Nobody built shelves here. Something did not let them.

r20.name: Staff Cloakroom
r20.desc: Coats, and a display. Door north.
r20.long:
A cloakroom with eleven pegs. Ten coats. One peg empty and the coat that belongs on it is on the floor, which nobody down here would have allowed.

Against the wall, a small display of arbitration merchandise with a handwritten sign: STAFF DISCOUNT.
r20.item_hint: There is merchandise on the staff display.

r21.name: Limit Antechamber
r21.desc: A low room, very quiet, with a heavy door south.
r21.long:
The ceiling comes down here, sharply, and keeps coming down toward the far door until you are walking bent.

It is not architecture. It is the room being clear about something.

The door at the end is small and heavy and has one word on it, and the word is ENOUGH.

r22.name: The Aggregate Limit
r22.desc: A room with a ceiling you can feel. One door north.
r22.long:
The room is enormous in every direction except up.

The ceiling is six feet from the floor and made of something that is not material; it is a decision, held in place, and it presses down on everything under it including the sound of your own breathing.

Under it, at the centre, The Cap is waiting, and it is not large, and it does not need to be.

It is the reason nothing in this building has ever been worth what it cost.

r24.name: Aisle 000
r24.desc: An aisle numbered before the numbering started. Doors north and south.
r24.long:
The shelf ends are numbered 000, which is not a category, and the boxes on them are unlabelled.

You open one. It is empty and clean and the dust has been disturbed recently, which means somebody else opened it first and put it back.

r25.name: West Ladder
r25.desc: A service ladder and a run of low shelving. Doors north, east and south.
r25.long:
An iron ladder bolted to the wall going up into a hatch that is bolted shut from the other side.

Someone has scratched a running total into the rungs. It stops at four hundred and eleven.

r26.name: Salvage Bay
r26.desc: A dry bay with a table set up in it. Doors north and east.
r26.long:
A raised bay where the archive staff used to dry out water-damaged files, and it has been repurposed.

The drying racks are gone. In their place: a folding table, a lamp run off something you cannot see, and a very great deal of stock.

He waves you over before you have decided whether to go over.

r01.name: Willowmead Close
r01.desc: The mouth of a cul-de-sac. Trimmed hedges. A road south.
r01.long:
You come out of the stairwell onto a pavement.

An actual pavement, with a kerb, under an actual sky the colour of a Sunday afternoon in a month you cannot name. Semi-detached houses down both sides, hedges trimmed level, cars washed.

A sign says WILLOWMEAD CLOSE. Below it, a smaller one: PLEASE DRIVE CAREFULLY, WE LOVE OUR CHILDREN.

There are no children. Every curtain on the street moves at the same time, once, and then does not.

r02.name: The Turning Circle
r02.desc: The head of the close. Roads north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
The turning circle at the head of the close, with a small round of grass in the middle and a single tree that has been pruned into a shape it would not choose.

Someone has swept the road. Not a machine. Someone has swept the road, by hand, right to the kerbs.

r03.name: Odd Numbers
r03.desc: The odd side of the street. Doors east and south.
r03.long:
Numbers 1 through 11, odd, and each front garden is a slightly different arrangement of exactly the same plants.

At number 7 the arrangement is identical to number 5. You go back and check. It is identical. Same plants, same spacing, same one dead stem left in on the left-hand side.

r04.name: The Garages
r04.desc: A block of lock-ups behind the houses. Doors west and south.
r04.long:
A row of concrete lock-up garages behind the terrace, each with a green up-and-over door.

All are shut except one, which is open exactly four inches, and behind that gap is a light on and a radio playing something with no words.

There is a chest freezer just inside.

r05.name: Allotment Shed
r05.desc: A shed at the end of the allotments. Warm, safe, smells of soil. Doors north, east and south.
r05.long:
A shed at the top of the allotments, and inside it is dry and warm and smells like the inside of a bag of compost.

Tools on the wall, all clean. A kettle on a shelf, a folding chair, and a radio that is off.

Nothing on this floor will come into a shed. You do not know why. You are getting used to not knowing why.

r06.name: The Green
r06.desc: An open green with a bench. Doors north, west, east and south.
r06.long:
A rectangle of grass with one bench, one bin, and one sign listing seven things that are not permitted on the green.

The seventh is ASSEMBLY. Somebody has added an eighth in marker and it has been almost entirely scrubbed off, and what is left is the word ASKING.

r07.name: Even Numbers
r07.desc: The even side. Doors north, west, east and south.
r07.long:
Numbers 2 through 12, even. Same houses, mirrored.

At number 8 a man is washing a car that is already clean, and he raises a hand to you without looking up, and keeps washing, and is still washing when you look back from the next street.

r08.name: The Post Box
r08.desc: A post box on a corner, and a postman on his round. Doors west and south.
r08.long:
A red post box on the corner, collection times listed for a day of the week that is not on it twice.

Beside it, a postman with a full bag, sorting by hand, taking his time about it.

He looks up as you approach and does not look surprised, which by now is the thing that surprises you.
r08.npc_hint: The postman has stopped sorting and is looking at you.

r09.name: The Ginnel
r09.desc: A narrow path between fences. Doors north, east and south.
r09.long:
A path between two high fences, just wide enough, with a strip of concrete down the middle and nettles either side that have been cut back to exactly the concrete.

Halfway along, a gate in the left-hand fence stands open. Beyond it, a garden that is not maintained. It is the first untended thing you have seen on this floor and the sight of it is an enormous relief.

r10.name: The Village Hall
r10.desc: A community hall with the lights on. Doors north, west, east and south.
r10.long:
A single-storey hall with a noticeboard outside listing a bring-and-buy, a yoga class, and an EGM.

The EGM is today. The EGM has been today for a very long time.

Inside, the lights are on and the chairs are out in rows, and at the front there is a table with a jug of water and four glasses and four people who have already started.

r11.name: Playground
r11.desc: A playground in perfect repair. Doors north, west, east and south.
r11.long:
Swings, a slide, a roundabout, a springy horse on a thick coil.

Everything is in perfect repair. The rubber matting has no cracks in it. The swings are all hanging exactly level, which is not a thing swings do.

The roundabout is turning. Slowly, evenly, and it does not slow down while you watch it, and you watch it for longer than you meant to.

r12.name: Number 6
r12.desc: A house with the front door open. Doors north and west.
r12.long:
The front door of number 6 stands open onto a hall with a runner and a hall table and a bowl for keys.

The bowl has keys in it. The house is empty in the way a house is empty when somebody has gone out, not in the way a house is empty when nobody lives there.

On the hall table, a note in biro: BACK SOON. It has faded almost to nothing.
r12.chest_hint: There is a sideboard in the hall, and the drawer is not shut.

r13.name: Back Lane
r13.desc: A service lane behind the gardens. Doors north, east and south.
r13.long:
A cinder lane behind the gardens, bins out along it in a line, each one exactly a hand's width from its neighbour.

You measure two of them because you have to know. It is exactly a hand's width. Your hand.

r14.name: The Crossroads
r14.desc: Where the two streets cross. Doors north, west, east and south.
r14.long:
The two streets cross here under a lamp post that is on, in daylight, and has been for some time.

There is a small brass plaque at the base of the lamp post. It commemorates something in 1974, and the wording has been chosen with tremendous care to avoid saying what.

r15.name: The Watch Hut
r15.desc: A hut with a window, a logbook, and a torch. Doors north, west and south.
r15.long:
A wooden hut at the corner with a window facing the street, a chair, a flask, and a logbook open on the sill.

The logbook records everyone who has passed this corner, with times, in a clear hand, going back thousands of pages.

Today's entry is already written. It describes you. It is timed to the minute you arrived on this floor, which was before you passed this corner.
r15.chest_hint: There is a locker under the window.

r16.name: The Unpermitted Shed
r16.desc: A shed that is not on the estate plan. Door east.
r16.long:
A shed at the bottom of a garden with no house attached to it.

Somebody built this without permission. On this floor that is the gravest thing a person can do, and they did it, and they got away with it long enough to fill the shed with everything they were not supposed to have.

There is a camp bed. There is a wall of notes. There is a map of the estate with a route marked in red that does not use any of the roads.
r16.chest_hint: There is a pack under the camp bed, packed and ready.

r17.name: Second Shed
r17.desc: Another allotment shed. Warm, quiet, safe. Doors north, west and east.
r17.long:
Another shed, the twin of the first, and the kettle in this one is warm.

On the bench: a mug, upside down, clean. The same mug. Four floors now.

Whoever they are, they have stopped bothering to hide that they are ahead of you, and have started leaving the kettle on.

r18.name: Bottom of the Close
r18.desc: Where the estate runs out. Doors north, west, east and south.
r18.long:
The houses stop and the road carries on for thirty yards into a turning head with a low fence across it, and past the fence there is nothing at all.

Not darkness. Nothing, of the specific kind that means the estate was built to this size and no further, by someone who thought this would be enough.

r19.name: The Show Home
r19.desc: A house furnished for viewing. Doors north and west.
r19.long:
Number 22 is furnished but not lived in. Everything is arranged for a photograph: fruit in the bowl, throw on the sofa at an angle, three books on the coffee table nobody has read.

In the front room, a display stand of arbitration merchandise with a card: A WARM WELCOME TO YOUR NEW HOME.
r19.item_hint: There is merchandise on the display stand.

r20.name: Outside Number 14
r20.desc: A front path, a gate, and a door. Doors north and south.
r20.long:
Number 14 has a low gate that clicks, a path of even slabs, and a doorstep that has been donkey-stoned.

The curtains at every other window on the street are still.

Somewhere behind you, at the top of the close, a door closes. Then another. Then, further off, a third.

They are not leaving. They are coming out.

r21.name: Number 14
r21.desc: A front room with the good light on. One door north.
r21.long:
The hall is warm. There is a runner, and a hall table, and a telephone on it with a cord, and the receiver is off the cradle and lying beside it.

The front room door is open and the good light is on.

Mrs Hensley is standing in the middle of her own front room with her hands folded, and she is very pleased that you have come in rather than making a scene on the step, and behind you the gate clicks.

Then it clicks again.

r22.name: Number 1
r22.desc: The first house on the odd side. Its gate is open. Doors east and south.
r22.long:
Number 1 has its gate propped open with a brick, which on this estate is practically a scream.

The front door is shut. The milk on the step is from a delivery that stopped years ago and has not gone off.

r23.name: The Side Path
r23.desc: A path down the side of the houses. Doors north, east and south.
r23.long:
A concrete path running between fence and wall, wide enough for a bin, and there are bins.

Halfway along, somebody has drawn a hopscotch grid in chalk. It is fresh. It goes up to twelve and then, in a different hand, thirteen.

r24.name: Garages, Rear
r24.desc: The back of the lock-up block. Doors north, east and south.
r24.long:
The rear wall of the garage block, and somebody has been sleeping against it.

Cardboard, folded. A ring of stones. No fire in years. Whoever it was, they were outside the houses, and on this estate that is the same as being outside everything.

r25.name: The Corner Pitch
r25.desc: A patch of hardstanding with a table on it. Doors north and east.
r25.long:
A square of hardstanding where somebody once meant to put a shop, and never did, and it has stayed hardstanding for forty years.

There is a table on it now, and a folding stool, and a man behind them who nods at you as though you had arranged to meet.

Nobody on the estate looks at him. Not pointedly. They simply do not.

r26.name: The Back Field
r26.desc: Scrub and a beaten path. Doors west and south.
r26.long:
Past the last fence there is a strip of unmown field with a path worn diagonally across it by people taking the short cut.

The path is the only unplanned thing on this floor and walking it feels like getting away with something.

r27.name: The Lock-Up
r27.desc: One garage with the door up. Doors north and west.
r27.long:
A garage with the up-and-over door raised and the light on.

No car. A workbench, a vice, and a wall of tools in painted outlines, every tool in its outline except one, and the empty outline is the shape of something long.

Against the back wall, a chest freezer, humming.
r27.chest_hint: There is a chest freezer against the back wall, humming.

r28.name: The Cut-Through
r28.desc: A gap between two gardens. Doors north and east.
r28.long:
A gap between two gardens that is not on the estate plan and has been used by everyone for years.

The fence panels either side have been repaired repeatedly and the repairs have always left the gap. Somebody keeps mending the fence around the hole rather than closing it, which is either kindness or a rule.

shop.hint: BUY <number> to buy. BUY BAG for more carrying room. SELL <item> and he takes it at a third. LEAVE when you are done.
shop.haggle_good: He looks at you properly before he says a number. Everything here is about {percent}% under the ticket, and he gets the same back when he buys.
shop.haggle_bad: He does not look up. Everything here is about {percent}% over the ticket, and he gives back the same when he buys.
shop.already_sold: You have already had that one off him.
shop.too_dear: You are {short} {unit} short. He is sympathetic and immovable.
shop.no_room: You cannot carry it. He offers to hold it, then withdraws the offer himself.
sold_line: "The {name}. Good choice. Nobody buys that and everybody should."
"Take the {name}. It has been in the bag since floor two."
bought_line: "I'll take the {name} off you. It'll find a home."
farewell: "I'll be one floor down. I usually am."
"See you lower. Everyone sees me lower."
shop.upgrade_desc: +{slots} carrying slots, permanently. Takes you to {cap}.
shop.upgrade_maxed: "That's the lot," he says. "There's a limit to what a person can carry and we've found yours."
upgrade_line: "Straps, mostly. And a frame. You'd be amazed."
"I've been carrying more than you for eleven years. There's a technique and there's also a frame, and I'm selling you the frame."
shop.upgrade_done: +{slots} slots. You can carry {cap} things now.
shop.machine_hint: BUY <number> and the coil turns. LEAVE when you are done. The prices are printed on the front: it does not care who is reading them, and it does not want your things.
shop.machine_wont_buy: There is no slot for that. It is a vending machine, not a colleague.
machine_sold_line: The coil turns, and {name} drops into the tray.
A clunk, a pause long enough to worry you, and {name} arrives.
Down the chute at an angle, and {name} lands on its side.
Something inside works hard for a moment, and delivers {name}.
shop.machine_already_sold: That row is empty. The coil turns anyway when you look at it, which is worse.
machine_farewell: The machine hums on, lit and unbothered.
The coil turns a quarter turn as you step away, which you choose not to think about.
It goes back to humming. It was always going to.
The light behind the glass flickers once, and settles.

rooms_common.merchant_hint: Somebody has set up a folding table here and is open for business.
rooms_common.photo_here: Above the bench there is a photograph of a beach, pinned up. Type PHOTO to look at it properly.
rooms_common.photo_here_again: The same beach photograph is pinned above this bench too.
rooms_common.photo_same_floor: The beach photograph is up here too. It is the same one as the other on this floor.
merchant_again: The Travelling Salesman is still here, behind the folding table. Still open.
The folding table is where you left it, and so is the man behind it.
The Travelling Salesman looks up, sees it is you, and does not get excited.
vending_hint: A vending machine hums against the wall, lit from inside. A brass plate on the front says VOICE OPERATED.
There is a vending machine here, humming. It has no buttons at all, and a plate that says it listens.
A vending machine stands in the corner, glowing, patient, and waiting to be spoken to.
vending_again: The vending machine is still humming, still listening.
The vending machine waits, lit and unbothered, for somebody to say something to it.

quirk.toll_taken: Something takes {amount} on the way in. You do not see what.
quirk.no_ability_restore: You rest, but whatever powers your abilities does not come back here.
quirk.f2:
THIS FLOOR: FEES

Every new room on this floor takes two paperclips off you on the way in. There is no gate and nobody asks. It is simply applied, which is the entire clause.

Encounters are slightly more frequent down here. There is more of everything down here.
quirk.f3:
THIS FLOOR: THE LIGHT

The archive is too dark to see the exits from the doorway. Room descriptions will not list the ways out until you LOOK properly.

Get in the habit. It costs nothing but a turn, and the things on this floor do not use turns.
quirk.f4:
THIS FLOOR: NEIGHBOURS

Running away is harder here. Everyone knows everyone, the fences are low, and escape checks are four harder than anywhere above.

Stalkers move faster too. Nobody on this estate has ever had to hurry, so when they do, it means something.
quirk.f5:
THIS FLOOR: NO RECOVERY

Resting restores your health here. It does not restore ability uses. Whatever powers them is not on the retention schedule and does not come back.

Spend them like they are gone, because on this floor they are. Encounters are up slightly too.

The merchant sells consumables. Buy consumables.
quirk.f6:
THIS FLOOR: NO CRITS

Nothing you do here crits. A natural 20 hits, and hits normally, and that is all it does.

The floor holds the rights to your best moments and is not licensing them back. Skirmishers lose their 19-20 range too, for the first and only time.

Bring damage that does not rely on spikes.
quirk.f7:
THIS FLOOR: NOTHING IS SETTLED

Encounters are up sharply and stalkers move faster. The floor does not follow rules because the clause says it does not have to.

There is no quirk to work around here. There is only more of it, arriving unpredictably, which is the clause working exactly as drafted.
quirk.f8:
THIS FLOOR: THE INDEMNITY

Six paperclips per new room. The foundry runs on debt and you are carrying some.

Escape is two harder. Nobody leaves a foundry mid-pour.

And the boss splits your damage onto your companion. Read that again before you go down there.
shifted: This is not how you left it.
Something about the room has been revised since you were last in it.
You have been here. You are fairly sure you have been here.
quirk.f9:
THIS FLOOR: SEVERED

The floor is in pieces. Whole blocks of rooms connect to the rest by a single doorway, and the map will show you gaps that look like bugs and are not.

One mercy: nothing here holds together well enough to chase you properly. Escape checks are two easier.
quirk.f10: THIS FLOOR: PROCEDURE. Everything here happens at the speed the court does it, which is slowly, and the text arrives at that speed too. It is not a fault and you cannot appeal it. Press Ctrl-C during a passage if you genuinely cannot wait, and it will stop doing it for the rest of the run. Encounters are slightly up: there is a lot of building and everyone in it has all day.
quirk.f11:
THIS FLOOR: AMENDED

Rooms rewrite themselves between visits. Walk back into somewhere you have been and it may describe itself differently, because it is different now.

The geometry does not change. Doors stay where they are and you cannot be stranded. Your map is accurate about the shape of the floor and wrong about everything else, and it will not tell you which is which.
quirk.f12: THIS FLOOR: CLOSING DOWN. The building is being shut off around you and whatever is still working knows it has very little time left. Stalkers move much faster here; there is no patience left anywhere on this floor. Encounters are up. Everything down here has one last thing it wants to do.
quirk.f13: THIS FLOOR: NOTHING LEFT TO ENFORCE. There is almost nothing here, and what there is does not chase. Escape checks are four easier and encounters are rare. This is not mercy. It is that the agreement has run out of terms, and a clause with nothing behind it cannot make you do anything at all.

clips: A drawer has been left open. Inside, a paperclip caddy, mostly full.
There are paperclips in the carpet here. A lot of them. Somebody upended something.
tannoy: A tannoy clears its throat somewhere above you, thinks better of it, and clicks off.
Somewhere on this floor a phone rings four times and stops.
lights: The strip lights above you go off in sequence, all the way down the corridor, and then come back on in the wrong order.
biscuit: There is a plate of biscuits on a filing cabinet. They are fresh. You eat one before you can talk yourself out of it.
flicker: Every light in the corridor goes out at once, and comes back one at a time, in the wrong order, taking about four seconds about it.

haul: The silt gives up a handful of paperclips, and then rather more than a handful.
There is a caddy wedged under the grating. It has been down here a long time and it is still full.
cold: The cold gets through. You lose feeling in one hand for long enough to matter.
bottle: A bottle is wedged upright in the brickwork, capped, labelled in the same handwriting as everything else down here.
pump: You stand in the warm air off a pump housing for a minute longer than you need to, and it helps more than it should.
wake: Something upstream notices the water move. It does not shout. It just starts walking.

shelf: A shelf gives without warning and catches you across the shoulder before it goes in.
file: A box file has burst and the contents are mostly paperclips, thousands of them, because that is how they used to bind a claim.
lamp: You find a working anglepoise and take a minute to actually see something. It clarifies more than the room.
name:
You open a drawer at random and the file on top has your name on it.

You put it back without reading it. You are not sure that was the right call and it is too late now.
There is a name pencilled on the shelf end, very small, and it is not a name from your life, and you recognise it anyway.
tea: Somebody left a full cup on a shelf. It is stone cold and it was made properly.

curtain: Every curtain on this side of the street moves at once and then does not move again.
A door opens two houses down, and nobody comes out, and it stays open.
casserole: There is a dish on the step with a tea towel over it, still warm, with a name taped to the bottom.
change: There is a jar of paperclips on a windowsill with a handwritten label: TAKE WHAT YOU NEED. You take rather more than you need.
hedge: You cut through a gap in a hedge that turns out to be hawthorn all the way down.
watch: Somebody in a hi-vis tabard writes something in a book, looks at you, and starts walking. Not fast. Just started.
flicker: Every curtain on the street twitches at the same moment, and then the street lamps come on, in daylight, all together.

fan: A cooling fan somewhere spins up, runs for nine seconds, and stops. Nothing needed cooling.
Every rack light on the aisle blinks amber at once and then settles back to green.
clips: A parts drawer has spilled. Screws, blanking plates, cable ties, and a great many paperclips.
There is a jar of paperclips on top of a rack, above head height, where somebody put it to keep it safe.
static: You put a hand on a rack door and something in it puts a hand back.
log:
A console flickers awake and prints one line before dying: LAST ACCESS - TODAY.

It is not your access. It is timestamped four minutes ago and you have been alone for an hour.
A monitor on a shelf shows a login prompt with a username already filled in. It is your name, spelled the way only two people ever spell it.
cache: A wall-mounted cabinet, glass front, seal broken by somebody in a hurry. There is one auto-injector left.
flicker: Every rack light in the catacomb goes amber at once and stays amber for nine seconds, which is eight seconds longer than any fault should take to clear.

display: A display stand rotates to face you as you pass. It is motorised. Everything here is motorised.
A screen overhead plays six seconds of you, from Clause 2, in slow motion, with music.
royalty: A cash drawer has been left open on an unmanned till and it is full of paperclips, which are, you now understand, your royalties.
There is an envelope pinned to a display with your name on it. Inside: paperclips, and a compliments slip reading WITH THANKS FOR YOUR CONTINUED PARTICIPATION.
mirror: You walk into a mirrored panel at speed because the version of you approaching it did not slow down either.
plush: A plush of you has fallen off a shelf. You pick it up, because you cannot leave it on the floor, and now you are carrying it.
sample: A sampling stand offers something in a tiny paper cup. It is genuinely good. You have three.
flicker: Every screen in the hall cuts to the same frame of you at the same instant, holds it, and resumes.

weather: It rains indoors for about nine seconds and then does not, and the floor is dry.
The wind changes direction inside a corridor with no openings in it.
clips: A cash box has been thrown clear of something and burst. Paperclips everywhere and no box in sight.
strike: Something goes through the room at head height and is gone before you have finished ducking, and you have not finished ducking.
calm: For about a minute there is nothing at all. No wind, no noise, no threat. You stand in it and it does more for you than any of the food has.
colour: The colour deepens for a moment. Everything you can see gets more of itself, and then settles back to the new normal, which is still colour, which you are still not used to.
gift: There is a sealed pouch sitting on a ledge, perfectly dry, in the middle of all this. Nobody put it there. That is the floor's whole thing.
downpour: The corridor rains. Properly, from a ceiling that is eight feet up and has weather behind it, for about a minute, and then it stops and the carpet steams.
It comes down hard enough that you stand in a doorway and wait it out, indoors, on the seventh floor of a building.

pour: A ladle swings past closer than it should and the heat off it takes the hair off your arm.
slag: The slag heap is threaded with paperclips, unmelted, because paperclips apparently do not melt here and nobody has ever asked why.
debtor: Somebody goes past pushing a barrow of something molten and does not look up, and their tally board reads a number with too many digits.
quench: You put your hands in the quench trough. It is cold, properly cold, the first cold thing since Clause 5, and it is worth more than it should be.
ledger:
A tally board on the wall lists debts by name. Yours is on it.

The figure beside it is not money. It is a number of floors, and it says thirteen, and somebody has been keeping this up to date.
bond: Something in a good coat writes down your name, closes the book, and starts walking after you at exactly your speed.

gap: The corridor stops. Not at a wall: it stops, and past the stopping point there is a room you can see and cannot reach.
There is a doorway in the middle of the floor, standing on its own, with nothing either side of it. You go through it. It works.
clips: A supply cupboard has been cut clean in half. The half you can reach is the half with the paperclips in it.
edge: You misjudge where the floor stops. Not badly. Badly enough.
whole: A room that is entirely intact, all four corners, ceiling to floor. You stand in the middle of it for a minute and it is the best minute of the last hour.
half:
You find half a chair, half a desk, and half a photograph, all cut on the same plane.

The half of the photograph you have is a beach. You are fairly sure about the other half.
cache: Somebody stashed a bottle in a wall cavity that only exists because the wall was severed.

usher: An usher crosses the corridor ahead, carrying nothing, going somewhere, and does not acknowledge you.
A bell rings twice somewhere below. Nothing happens. Twenty seconds later it rings twice again.
costs: Costs were awarded in somebody's favour a long time ago and never collected. The envelope is still in the pigeonhole.
contempt: You say something out loud in a corridor that turns out to be part of the court, and the corridor takes it badly.
recess: A bench in an empty corridor, and above it a sign reading COURT NOT SITTING. You sit for as long as it takes to stop shaking.
transcript:
A transcript has been left on a windowsill, open at a page where somebody says: I only wanted to cancel.

The next line is redacted. So is every line after it.
writ: A sealed writ in a pigeonhole with your name on it, and inside the seal, instead of a document, a bottle.

revised: The sign on the door says something different from what it said when you read it thirty seconds ago.
A notice on the wall is being amended while you look at it. Not by anyone.
clips: A drawer that was empty last time is not empty this time. Nobody has been in here. It has simply been revised.
struck: A section of the floor is struck through and you go most of the way into it before it is reinstated.
favour: An amendment lands in your favour for once: the room is now a room with water in it, and the water is clean, and you drink.
notice:
A notice of variation, addressed to you, correctly spelled, dated today.

It amends the definition of 'disputant'. You read the new definition twice and decide it is broadly survivable.
draft: Someone left a clean unamended draft of something in a drawer, and a bottle on top of it to stop it being revised.

ash: The fall thickens for a minute and then eases, and what settles on your shoulders is warm.
A whole page comes down unburnt, turning, and lands face up. It is a leave request from 1974. It was approved.
clips: A desk has gone over and its drawers with it, and the ash is threaded with paperclips that will not burn and never have.
Somebody's box, never collected. Pens, a photo frame, and a jar of paperclips with a name taped to the lid.
ember: Something still hot comes down on the back of your hand and you get it off before you look at it, which is the correct order.
kettle: A kettle on a standby socket, boiled within the hour, beside a mug that has been rinsed. You have some. It is very good.
notice:
A shutdown notice has been pinned over another shutdown notice, which is pinned over another, and the one at the bottom is dated eleven years ago.

Every one of them is final.
A hand-written card on a dead machine: INSTALLED 1971. THANK YOU.
cache: A crate, taped, labelled in the careful biro: FOR WHOEVER IS BEHIND ME. STILL GOOD.

quiet: Nothing happens for a while. Not ominously. It simply does not.
You realise you have been walking in silence for several minutes and that nothing in the white has moved, and that this is the first time in thirteen floors that has been true.
You stop and listen properly. There is no plant, no extract, no distant machinery. The building has finally run out of things to run.
clips: A small neat pile of paperclips on the white floor, arranged deliberately, as if somebody emptied a pocket and could not think of a reason to pick them up again.
clause:
A single line of the agreement is printed on the white at eye height, out of context, and reads: 'the parties acknowledge that no representation has been relied upon.'

You relied on several. So did four billion other people.
A clause number without a clause under it. Just the number, waiting.
rest: You sit down on the floor, because there is nothing else and nothing is coming, and you stay there for a bit. It helps more than any of the food has.
edge: The floor ends and starts again half a step later, and you find the gap with your shin rather than your eyes.
mug:
A mug, on the floor, in the middle of nothing. Upside down. Clean.

There is no bench here, no kettle, no room. Somebody carried it this far and set it down and went on.

r01.name: Catacomb Head
r01.desc: A landing at the top of the racks. Cold air rising. A stair down south.
r01.long:
The stairs come out onto a walkway above the racks, and the racks go down and away in every direction under a haze of their own cold air.

Thousands of them. Every light green. Everything working perfectly, doing nothing, for nobody, and it has been doing that since before the acquisition.

The noise is enormous and completely even and after two minutes you stop hearing it.

r02.name: Aisle Head
r02.desc: The top of the main aisle. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
The main aisle runs the length of the floor and you cannot see the end of it.

Every rack has a printed label. The labels have dates on them and the dates go back further than the company.

r03.name: Cross Connect
r03.desc: A tangle of patch cable at head height. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
The overhead trays have failed and forty years of patch cable has come down in a hanging mass you have to push through.

Every cable is labelled at both ends. Somebody did that. Somebody labelled every one of these at both ends and then the tray fell anyway.

r04.name: Spares
r04.desc: Shelves of parts, all still in packaging. Doors east.
r04.long:
Spares. Drives, plates, rails, fans, every one still shrink-wrapped, ordered against a failure that never came because nothing down here has been allowed to fail.

There is a parts crate at the end of the run that somebody had started to open.

r05.name: Hot Aisle
r05.desc: The air here is wrong. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
The exhaust side. The air coming off the racks is hot enough to dry your mouth in seconds and it smells like the inside of an old television.

At the far end, the aisle containment doors are propped open with a fire extinguisher. Somebody wanted a way through, in a hurry, and did not care what it did to the airflow.

r06.name: Decommission Row
r06.desc: Racks stripped to the frame. Doors east and south.
r06.long:
Empty frames, doors off, cable stubs hanging. This is where things were taken out of service.

Nothing has been taken out of service since the acquisition. All of this is older than the contract, and you file that away, because a man in a vault two floors up told you it mattered.

r07.name: UPS Room
r07.desc: Batteries, warmth, and a low steady hum. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r07.long:
The uninterruptible power supply: two walls of sealed batteries, warm to the touch, and a hum you can feel in your teeth.

It was installed before the acquisition. Anything older than the contract, the contract cannot touch, and that is why nothing follows you in here, and you finally understand why the pump houses were safe.

Somebody has left a chair. And a blanket. And, on the floor by the chair, four hundred and eleven marks scratched into the concrete.

r08.name: Main Aisle
r08.desc: The middle of the run. Doors north, west, east and south.
r08.long:
Halfway down, and it looks identical in both directions, and you have to check the labels to be sure you are making progress.

The labels say you are. You check twice.

r09.name: Aisle 14
r09.desc: A rack row with one door open. Doors north, west, east and south.
r09.long:
One rack door stands open in an otherwise sealed row, and the drive bays inside it are empty, and the dust says they came out recently.

Six bays. Six empty bays, in a row, and something about that number is going to matter shortly.

r10.name: The Loading Dock
r10.desc: A shuttered dock with a table set up on it. Doors west and south.
r10.long:
A goods dock, shutter down, and in the middle of the empty floor a folding table with a lamp and a great deal of stock.

He has hung a bedsheet behind him to make the space feel smaller. It works, which is somehow the most impressive thing you have seen down here.

r11.name: Aisle 21
r11.desc: Racks, and a smell of ozone. Doors east and south.
r11.long: The ozone smell is strongest here and there is a scorch mark up one rack door that has been painted over and has come back through the paint.

r12.name: Cold Aisle
r12.desc: The intake side. Very cold. Doors north, east and south.
r12.long:
The intake side, and the air is coming in hard enough to move your clothes.

The floor tiles are perforated and under them the void goes down and the cold comes up and something down there is not a fan.

r13.name: The Long Row
r13.desc: A rack row you cannot see the end of. Doors north, west, east and south.
r13.long: This row is longer than the floor is wide. You check that twice as well, and it remains true, and you decide to keep walking.

r14.name: Tape Library
r14.desc: A robotic tape library, still running. Doors north, west, east and south.
r14.long:
A tape library the size of a shipping container, glass-fronted, and the picker arm inside is still working: selecting, seating, reading, returning.

It has been doing that continuously. There is no request queue. There has been no request queue for decades.

It stops when you come in. That is the first thing on this floor that has reacted to you at all.

r15.name: Aisle 28
r15.desc: Racks with the labels torn off. Doors north, west and south.
r15.long:
Every label on this row has been torn off, cleanly, from the same corner, by someone working methodically down the aisle with a purpose.

Somebody was hiding something and did not have time to be subtle about it.

r16.name: The Dead Row
r16.desc: Racks that have finally failed. Doors east.
r16.long:
The only failed row in the catacomb: every light out, every fan still.

It is the first silent place you have found on this floor and after the noise it is almost unbearable.

Something is stashed at the bottom of the last rack.
r16.chest_hint: There is something stashed in the bottom of the last rack.

r17.name: Aisle 33
r17.desc: Racks, and a chair pulled out. Doors north, east and south.
r17.long: Somebody has pulled a chair out into the aisle and sat facing the racks. The chair is still warm, or the racks are, and you cannot tell which.

r18.name: The Console Row
r18.desc: A row of maintenance consoles, most dark. Doors north, west, east and south.
r18.long:
Crash carts and consoles, most of them dark, one or two still showing a login prompt.

Every prompt has a username already filled in and a cursor blinking in an empty password field. They have been waiting for a password for a very long time.

r19.name: Aisle 40
r19.desc: The last numbered aisle. Doors north, west, east and south.
r19.long:
The numbering stops here. Past it the racks continue but they are not labelled and not on any diagram on the wall.

Somebody added them later. Somebody is still adding them.

r20.name: Network Operations
r20.desc: A NOC with every screen green. Doors north, west and south.
r20.long:
A network operations centre. Six desks, eighteen screens, every dashboard green, every alert cleared.

One desk is occupied. It has been occupied for twenty-two years, and the occupant stands up as you come in, and adjusts a lanyard, and does not look pleased to see you at all.
r20.chest_hint: There is a locked drawer under the occupied desk.

r21.name: Second UPS Room
r21.desc: More batteries, more warmth. Safe. Doors north and east.
r21.long:
The second battery room, identical, and there is a kettle in this one and it is warm.

On the shelf beside it, upside down, clean: the mug.

Five floors. They are still ahead of you and they are still leaving the kettle on, and you say thank you out loud before you can stop yourself.

r22.name: Sub-Floor Access
r22.desc: A hatch in the floor, bolted. Doors north, west, east and south.
r22.long:
A floor hatch with sixteen bolts in it, all done up, and every bolt head has been painted over and the paint is unbroken.

Something is under this floor that somebody wanted sixteen bolts' worth of certainty about.

r23.name: Aisle 44
r23.desc: Unlabelled racks. Doors north, west and east.
r23.long:
Unlabelled, undocumented, and warmer than the rest.

These are the ones that are still being added to. You put a hand near a drive bay and it is working hard, and you have a good idea what it is recording.

r24.name: Archive Interface
r24.desc: Where this floor talks to Clause 3. Doors north, west and south.
r24.long:
A run of ancient interface equipment linking the catacomb to the archive two floors up: the digital end of all that flooded paper.

The link is still live. Everything you did on Clause 3 came down this cable within seconds, and is now somewhere in these racks, permanently, as necessary.

r25.name: Staff Kitchen
r25.desc: A kitchen, and a display. Doors west.
r25.long:
A kitchen for people on long shifts: microwave, sink, a rota on the wall going back decades with the same four names on it.

Against the wall, a small merchandise display, because of course there is.
r25.item_hint: There is merchandise on the display.

r26.name: Aisle 51
r26.desc: A row with a gap in it. Doors north, east and south.
r26.long:
One rack has been removed from the middle of this row and the gap has not been filled.

The floor where it stood is a different colour. It has been gone a very long time and nothing has been put back, which on this floor is unheard of.

r27.name: Spares, Rear
r27.desc: The back of the parts store. Doors west and east.
r27.long:
The other end of the spares run, and here the packaging has been opened, methodically, by somebody looking for one specific component.

They found it. There is one empty space on an otherwise complete shelf.

r28.name: The Approach
r28.desc: A wide clear floor before a set of doors. Doors north, west and south.
r28.long:
The racks stop and there is thirty feet of clear raised floor before a set of double doors with a card reader beside them.

The card reader is dead. The doors are open. They were forced, from this side, with something long, and the tool marks match a gap in a wall on Clause 2.

r29.name: Tape Library, Rear
r29.desc: Behind the library. Somebody has been living here. Doors east.
r29.long:
Behind the tape library there is a gap the width of a person between the machine and the wall, and it is warm, and somebody has been sleeping in it.

A coat over the racking, dry. A tally on the wall. A pack, packed, ready to go, that they have not come back for.

The pack is not abandoned. It is staged. There is a difference and it means they are coming back.
r29.chest_hint: There is a pack here, packed and staged.

r30.name: Array Six
r30.desc: An enormous room holding one array. Doors north.
r30.long:
The room beyond the doors holds one machine and the machine is six storeys of it.

RAID-6 fills the space from floor to ceiling in six columns, each one a wall of drives, and every light on every one of them is green.

As you come in, one column goes amber. Then it rebuilds itself from the other five, in about four seconds, and goes green again.

It does that to show you. It has been waiting a long time to show somebody.

r01.name: Retail Atrium
r01.desc: A bright shopping atrium. Escalator down south.
r01.long:
The doors open onto a retail atrium: polished floor, soft lighting, a two-storey void with an escalator running down into it.

Every surface is branded. There is a scent in the air, deliberately, the way there is in a shop that wants you to stay.

On the far wall, four storeys high, is your face.

r02.name: Concourse
r02.desc: The top of the shop floor. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
The concourse, and the displays start here and do not stop.

Mugs. Keyrings. A rail of t-shirts, sized, in your size, with your face on all of them, and a sign reading NEW SEASON.

r03.name: Apparel
r03.desc: Racks of clothing. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long: Apparel. Everything in your size, everything with you on it, arranged by colour into a gradient that took somebody a full day.

r04.name: Homeware
r04.desc: Kitchen goods with your face on. Doors west, east and south.
r04.long:
Homeware. Tea towels, oven gloves, a chopping board, a set of coasters that together form a picture of you at the moment you first read Clause 13.

The coasters are the bestseller. There is a small handwritten card saying so.

r05.name: Stockroom
r05.desc: Boxes, unopened, floor to ceiling. Doors east.
r05.long:
The stockroom, and it is full, and every box is sealed and labelled with a product code and a quantity.

The quantities are enormous. Somebody expects this to sell for a very long time.

r06.name: Green Room
r06.desc: A quiet room behind the shop floor. Safe. Doors north, east and south.
r06.long:
A green room: sofa, mirror with bulbs round it, a rail of clothing, a jug of water and two glasses.

The mirror is the only one on the floor that shows you as you are, and after the last hour that is genuinely restful.

The sofa is older than the fit-out. Older than the contract, in fact, which is why nothing comes in here.

r07.name: Central Display
r07.desc: A rotating display in the middle of the floor. Doors north, west, east and south.
r07.long:
A slowly rotating plinth carrying the flagship product, whatever that is this week, under a spotlight.

It is a statuette of you, half a metre high, at the moment you clicked Dispute. Limited edition. Numbered. The number is four figures.

r08.name: Media Wall
r08.desc: Screens showing your arbitration. Doors north, west, east and south.
r08.long:
A wall of screens, forty of them, showing the arbitration.

It is edited. There is music. Some of the shots are from angles that had nothing in them at the time, and you spend a while working out where the camera was, and then stop.

r09.name: Licensing Office
r09.desc: A back office of contracts. Doors west and south.
r09.long:
A back office with filing drawers of licence agreements, territory by territory.

The territories include places that do not exist and one that is not a place.

r10.name: Loading Bay
r10.desc: The service end of the shop. Doors east and south.
r10.long:
The loading bay, roller shutter down, pallets stacked and wrapped and ready to go out.

Out where. You spend a minute on that and get nowhere.

r11.name: Seasonal
r11.desc: Merchandise for occasions. Doors north, east and south.
r11.long:
Seasonal lines. A Christmas jumper with your face on. A birthday card with your face on. A sympathy card with your face on, which stops you for a moment.

The sympathy cards are near the front. They are well stocked.

r12.name: Books
r12.desc: Publications about you. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
A book table. The Dispute: An Unauthorised Account. Thirteen Clauses: The Official Companion. A children's edition with softer illustrations and a happier ending than you have earned yet.

All of them have a chapter thirteen. You open one. Chapter thirteen is blank pages, correctly bound, deliberately.

r13.name: Collectables
r13.desc: Glass cases of limited editions. Doors north, west, east and south.
r13.long:
Locked glass cases of numbered editions, each with a certificate of authenticity signed by somebody with your handwriting.

You have never signed any of these. The signature is better than yours.

r14.name: The Kiosk
r14.desc: A concession unit taken over by somebody. Doors north and south.
r14.long:
A concession kiosk that used to sell something official and does not any more.

The branding has been taped over with cardboard and there is a folding table across the front of it and a man behind that, and he raises a hand as you come in.

He is the only thing on this floor that is not for sale.

r15.name: Corridor, Service
r15.desc: A grey service corridor. Doors north and south.
r15.long:
Behind the fit-out, the building is grey again: breeze block, cable tray, a strip light with one tube out.

It is the first honest wall you have seen on this floor and you stand and look at it for a second longer than you need to.

r16.name: Clearance
r16.desc: Reduced merchandise, badly stacked. Doors east and south.
r16.long:
Clearance. Reduced-to-clear bins of merchandise that did not sell, and it is all versions of you from earlier floors: you at Intake, you in the sewer, you with the wrong hair.

Everything here is a you that stopped being current. There is a crate at the back that has not been sorted.
r16.chest_hint: There is an unsorted crate at the back.

r17.name: Fitting Rooms
r17.desc: A row of curtained cubicles. Doors north, east and south.
r17.long:
Six fitting rooms, curtains half drawn, mirrors at three angles in each.

Five are empty. The sixth has the curtain fully closed, and there are no feet under it, and you do not open it.

r18.name: The Viewing Room
r18.desc: A room with a long mirrored wall. Doors north, west, east and south.
r18.long:
A viewing room: a table, eight chairs, water glasses, and one wall that is mirrored from this side.

You know what that means. They know you know. Somebody behind the glass writes something down as you work it out, and you hear the pen.

r19.name: Photography
r19.desc: A studio with lights and a backdrop. Doors north, west, east and south.
r19.long:
A photography studio: seamless backdrop, softboxes, a mark taped on the floor where the subject stands.

The mark is worn through to the concrete. Somebody has stood on that mark a great many times, and you do not remember doing it once.

r20.name: Rights Store
r20.desc: Cases of contracts and releases. Doors north and south.
r20.long:
Where the rights themselves are kept: bound volumes of releases, assignments, and waivers, by year.

The volume for this year is open on a lectern, and it is open at your page, and it has been open at your page for some time.

r21.name: The Brand Vault
r21.desc: A vault holding the approved version of you. Doors north and west.
r21.long:
A vault door standing open onto a small white room with one item in it, on a plinth, under glass.

It is the approved version of your face. Not a photograph. The master, whatever that means here, and everything on this floor was struck from it.

Something is standing beside the plinth with a style guide in its hand and it is extremely unhappy about your hair.
r21.chest_hint: There is a case beside the plinth.

r22.name: Second Green Room
r22.desc: Another quiet room behind the floor. Safe. Doors north, east and south.
r22.long:
The other green room, and this one has been used more recently.

The mirror bulbs are warm. There is a mug on the counter, upside down, clean, and beside it, for the first time, a note.

It says: SIX DOWN. THE MIRROR ON EIGHT IS THE WAY. DON'T STOP ON SEVEN, WHATEVER IT DOES.

r23.name: Concourse, Lower
r23.desc: The bottom of the shop floor. Doors north, west, east and south.
r23.long:
The lower concourse, and the displays are thinning out, and the lighting has not been maintained down here.

Half the spots are out. The merchandise is dustier. This part of the shop has not had a customer in a very long time.

r24.name: Returns
r24.desc: A counter for goods coming back. Doors north, west and south.
r24.long:
A returns desk with a queue rail in front of it and a shutter down over it.

On the counter, outside the shutter, one item left by somebody who could not wait: a plush of you, with a note pinned to it reading NOT AS DESCRIBED.

r25.name: Failed Concepts
r25.desc: A storeroom of versions that did not test. Doors east.
r25.long:
A storeroom of prototypes that never went to market.

Versions of you, in a rack, in polythene. Some are close and some are not and all of them were made from the same file.

One is very close. It is face down and you leave it face down, and the narrator, for once, says nothing at all.
r25.chest_hint: There is a crate here, marked DO NOT DISPLAY.

r26.name: Print Room
r26.desc: Where the merchandise is made. Doors north and east.
r26.long:
A print room: heat presses, vinyl rolls, and a queue of jobs on a screen that will never clear.

The machines are running. They are printing more of you, right now, for a shop with nobody in it.

r27.name: Warehouse Floor
r27.desc: Racking and pallets. Doors north, west, east and south.
r27.long:
Warehouse racking, four levels, packed with the same eleven products in enormous quantity.

There is a forklift parked neatly in the charging bay. You look at it for a while. Fourteen years of standing between other people and one of those, and here is one, harmless, plugged in, waiting for a shift that will not come.

r28.name: Distribution
r28.desc: Where it all goes out. Doors north and west.
r28.long:
A distribution office with a wall map, and the map is marked with pins, and the pins are in places.

The pins are not in this building. Somebody is buying this. Somewhere, somebody is buying it, and that means somewhere is out there, and that is more than you had an hour ago.

r29.name: Staff Sales
r29.desc: A staff discount rail. Doors west.
r29.long:
A rail of merchandise at staff prices, with a laminated notice about the discount policy.

Somebody has been buying it. There is a running tab pinned up with a name and a column of small amounts going back years.

They bought their own face, at a discount, every month, for years.
r29.item_hint: There is merchandise on the staff rail.

r30.name: Service Corridor
r30.desc: Grey walls again, and quiet. Doors north, east and south.
r30.long:
Out the back of the shop and into the building's actual bones: breeze block, conduit, a fire door with a push bar.

The push bar has been used recently. There is a hand's worth of clean metal in the middle of the dirty bar.

r31.name: The Rights Antechamber
r31.desc: A small room with one door and one mirror. Doors north and south.
r31.long:
A holding room with a bench, and one door out, and a full-length mirror on the wall opposite the bench.

You sit down without deciding to. In the mirror, you sit down about half a second late.

You watch that happen. It does not happen again, no matter how long you sit there, and you sit there for a while.

r32.name: The Likeness Suite
r32.desc: A white room with your face in it. Doors north.
r32.long:
The room is white and lit from everywhere and there are no shadows in it at all.

In the middle, standing on the photography mark, is you.

Not a plush, not a statuette, not an approved version. You: your build, your armour, the fire axe or the briefcase or whatever you have been carrying since Intake, held the way you hold it.

It has been practising. That is the thing you understand immediately and completely. It has had six floors of footage and nothing else to do.

"Right," it says, in your voice, and rolls its shoulder the way you do before a fight. "Let's see it."

r01.name: Weather Front
r01.desc: A landing where the air is moving. Stairs behind, a door south.
r01.long:
You come down the stairs and stop on the last one.

The corridor ahead has weather in it. Not damage, not a leak: weather, moving, with a front edge you can see, working its way along the ceiling.

<<rainbow>>And it is in colour.

You stand there for a while. Six floors of grey walls and grey carpet and grey people, and now there is a red fire point on the wall and the red is genuinely red, and the sign above the door is green, and you had forgotten. Actually forgotten.

The narrator does not say anything for a long moment.

r02.name: Pressure Junction
r02.desc: A four-way junction with weather in it. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
Four corridors and the air is moving between them in a slow rotation, carrying dust in a visible band.

The walls have watermarks going up rather than down, which takes you a moment.

r03.name: Unstable Corridor
r03.desc: A corridor that is not the same length twice. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
You walk the corridor and it takes eleven paces. You walk back and it takes eight.

You do it a third time out of stubbornness. Fourteen. You stop doing it.

r04.name: Risk Register
r04.desc: A room of assessments nobody made. Doors east.
r04.long:
A wall-sized risk register, printed and pinned, with every row filled in and a probability against each one.

Every probability is low. Every row is marked, in the same red pen, OCCURRED.

There is a document case under the board.
r04.chest_hint: There is a document case under the risk board.

r05.name: The Downdraught
r05.desc: A room where the air goes down. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
The air in here is going down and there is no down for it to go to; the floor is solid and unbroken.

Your coat pulls at you. Loose paper on the floor stays exactly where it is, which is the part you cannot make work.

r06.name: Squall Line
r06.desc: A room you cross between gusts. Doors west and south.
r06.long:
The gusts come every fourteen seconds and are strong enough to take you off your feet, and between them the room is dead calm.

Fourteen seconds, exactly, every time. You count nine of them before you go. The regularity is somehow the least reassuring thing about it.

r07.name: Lee Side
r07.desc: A sheltered corner. Doors east and south.
r07.long:
A corner the weather does not reach, for reasons of geometry you cannot see, and the dust has piled up here in a soft grey drift over years.

Someone has sat in this corner. The drift has the shape of it.

r08.name: Barometric Hall
r08.desc: A hall where the pressure changes as you cross. Doors north, west, east and south.
r08.long:
The pressure drops as you walk in and comes back as you cross the middle and drops again at the far door.

On the wall, a bank of forty barometers. Thirty-nine are hard against STORMY. One is at FAIR, and it is the oldest one there, and it is not connected to anything.

r09.name: The Bunker
r09.desc: A concrete shelter under the weather. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r09.long:
A concrete shelter, pre-cast, half sunk into the floor, with a door that closes properly.

Inside: a bench, a light, and nothing else. The weather stops at the doorway and does not come in.

Someone has written on the inside of the door, at sitting height: IT'S THE PRISM. FIND THE PRISM. And underneath, later, in the same hand: no, keep it. take it down.

r10.name: Open Ground
r10.desc: A wide room with no cover at all. Doors west, east and south.
r10.long:
The room is forty yards across and completely empty, and the weather has the whole run of it.

There is no reason for a room this size in a building like this and you cross it quickly and do not look up.

r11.name: Static Corner
r11.desc: A corner where everything stands on end. Doors west and south.
r11.long:
The charge in here lifts the hair on your arms and your coat stands away from you, and every loose thing in the room is a few inches off the floor and staying there.

Including the dust. Especially the dust. It looks like the room is holding its breath.

r12.name: Under the Awning
r12.desc: A pitch under an overhang, out of the weather. Doors west and south.
r12.long:
Somebody has set up under a concrete overhang where the weather cannot reach, and pegged a tarpaulin out from it for good measure, and put the table under that.

He has done this before. He has clearly done this on every floor and will do it on every floor after.

The lamp on the table is the same lamp. You are oddly pleased about that.

r13.name: Windward
r13.desc: The exposed side. Doors east and south.
r13.long:
The weather hits this wall first and has been hitting it for a long time, and the paint has gone and the plaster under it has gone and the block under that is scoured smooth.

Inside a building. Scoured smooth, inside a building.

r14.name: Cloud Level
r14.desc: A room with weather at chest height. Doors north, west, east and south.
r14.long:
There is cloud in here, a proper flat-bottomed layer of it, sitting at chest height across the whole room.

You walk through it with your head in clear air and the rest of you in white, and it is the single most pleasant thirty seconds of the entire arbitration.

r15.name: Contingency Store
r15.desc: Shelves of plans for things that happened anyway. Doors north, west, east and south.
r15.long:
Ring binders, hundreds, each one a contingency plan, each one thoroughly prepared and thoroughly indexed.

You pull one at random. It is a plan for exactly what is happening on this floor. It is dated forty years ago. It was never executed because nobody was authorised to declare the event, because declaring the event required someone to be reachable, and Clause 7 says nobody has to be.

r16.name: The Barometer Room
r16.desc: A room built around one instrument. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
A single enormous barometer, floor to ceiling, mercury column and brass, and it is the only fixed thing on the floor.

It reads FAIR.

Something is sitting on the base of it with its hands folded, and it has been reading FAIR the entire time that thing has been sitting there, and the weather outside this room is doing what it is doing regardless.

r17.name: Aftermath
r17.desc: A room that has already been through it. Doors north, west, east and south.
r17.long:
Whatever happened here has finished happening.

Everything is on the floor, sorted by weight, in a fan pattern radiating from the middle of the room. There is nothing in the middle of the room.

r18.name: The Long Gust
r18.desc: A corridor with a permanent wind down it. Doors north, west and south.
r18.long:
A corridor with a steady wind running its length, always the same direction, never varying.

Walking it one way is effortless. The other way is not. You note which way is which, because you will be coming back.

r19.name: Emergency Stores
r19.desc: Supplies for a declared emergency. Doors east and south.
r19.long:
Shelves of emergency supplies behind a glass panel that says BREAK IN CASE OF DECLARED EVENT.

No event has ever been declared. The glass is intact. The supplies are forty years past date except the ones that are not.

Somebody has already broken a small panel at the bottom, neatly, and taken exactly what they needed and nothing more.
r19.chest_hint: A small panel at the bottom has been broken, neatly.

r20.name: Rain Shadow
r20.desc: A dry strip in a wet room. Doors north, east and south.
r20.long:
It is raining in here, properly raining, and there is a dry strip about a yard wide running from the near door to the far one.

You walk down it. It is exactly a yard wide the whole way and it goes exactly where you need to go, and you do not say thank you out loud but it is a near thing.

r21.name: Hail Floor
r21.desc: A floor covered in ice that should not exist. Doors north, west, east and south.
r21.long:
Hailstones, thousands, ankle deep and not melting.

The ceiling is eight feet up and solid concrete. You look at it for a while. There is no arrangement of facts that makes this work and Clause 7 is not required to provide one.

r22.name: The Still Room
r22.desc: A room with no weather in it at all. Doors north, west, east and south.
r22.long:
Nothing is happening in here. No wind, no cloud, no charge, no noise.

After everything else on this floor the stillness is aggressive. You keep checking behind you. There is nothing behind you.

That is the point. It is the only room on the floor doing nothing, and it makes you feel more watched than any of the others.

r23.name: Rising Front
r23.desc: A room where the weather is building. Doors north, west, east and south.
r23.long:
It is getting worse in here, continuously, and has been for some time, and shows no sign of topping out.

You do not stay to find out where it tops out.

r24.name: The Contingency Office
r24.desc: An office where the plans were made. Doors north and west.
r24.long:
The office where all those binders were written: four desks, a wall planner, and a phone with no dial.

The wall planner covers forty years. Every week has an entry. Every entry is a plan for something that then happened, unmanaged, because nobody was reachable.

Somebody stands up behind the furthest desk. They have three plans for you and they are going to try all of them.
r24.chest_hint: There is a document safe behind the furthest desk.

r25.name: Sheltered Run
r25.desc: A corridor with the weather stripped out. Doors north and east.
r25.long:
Somebody has run a line of concrete baffles down this corridor and the weather cannot get past them, and the corridor is dry and quiet and usable.
