It is enormous work. It was done by hand, by one person, over what must have been years, and it serves no purpose except that somebody wanted a way through.

r26.name: Second Bunker
r26.desc: Another shelter. Warm, quiet, safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r26.long:
The second bunker, same pre-cast shell, same bench.

The kettle is warm. Of course it is. And beside it, this time, a mug the right way up, with tea in it, made properly, still steaming.

They heard you coming and they put the kettle on and then they left before you arrived, and you sit down on the bench and drink somebody else's tea and something in your chest goes tight for a second.

r27.name: Debris Field
r27.desc: Everything the floor has moved, in one place. Doors north, west, east and south.
r27.long:
Where the weather has been putting things for forty years: a drift of office furniture, signage, ceiling tiles, and one bicycle, piled twelve feet deep against a wall.

Every item in it came from somewhere else in this building. Some of it you recognise from floors above.

r28.name: Colour Store
r28.desc: A supply room somebody has been quietly keeping.
r28.long:
Shelves of paint tins, sorted by shade, in a building that has not been decorated in living memory.

Somebody comes down here on their breaks and puts them in order. You can tell because they are in order. There is a chair, a flask, and a radio that is not plugged into anything. Nothing follows you in.

r29.name: Salvage Shelf
r29.desc: A shelf of things the weather brought. Doors north and west.
r29.long:
A shelf built into an alcove, out of the wind, and someone has been putting the interesting things on it as they come past.

Most of it is junk. Three items are not. One of them is a full set of arbitration merchandise, weather-beaten, which somebody rescued and dried and shelved, and you cannot work out whether that is funny or not.
r29.item_hint: There is merchandise on the salvage shelf.

r30.name: Approach, Descending
r30.desc: The floor tilts down toward a door. Doors north, east and south.
r30.long:
The floor slopes down toward a set of doors at the far end and the weather slopes with it, all of it, everything on this floor draining toward the same point.

That is where it has all been going. You have been walking around the edge of a drain for an hour.

r31.name: The Roof Hole
r31.desc: A room open to a sky that should not be there. Doors west.
r31.long:
There is a hole in the ceiling.

Not a breach. Not tool marks. A hole, going up, through concrete and steel and however many floors of grey office, and at the top of it there is sky. Real sky, with weather in it, in colour, at a distance that does not fit inside a building.

Somebody stood here and looked up at that and then turned round and went back down. Their kit is still here, stacked, because they did not need to carry it any further.
r31.chest_hint: Somebody's kit is stacked here, neatly, and left.

r32.name: The Eye
r32.desc: A perfectly still room with a door at the far end.
r32.long:
The room is completely calm and completely silent and the light in it is extraordinary.

This is the eye. Around it, in every direction, the floor is doing what it does. In here, nothing, and the door at the far end is standing open, and beyond it there is colour of a kind you have not seen even since the stairs.

You could stay in here. You are aware of that as a real option and you turn it over properly before you put it down.

r33.name: The Unforeseeable
r33.desc: A room that will not hold a shape. One door north.
r33.long:
The room does not settle.

Walls, ceiling, floor, all of it moving through configurations, none of them impossible individually and none of them compatible with the last, and all of it in colour so saturated it is difficult to look at directly.

In the middle, Kaleidon.

It is not a shape. It is the process of becoming shapes, running continuously, and it turns whatever it currently has toward you.

"AH," it says, with what sounds like real pleasure. "SOMETHING THAT WAS NOT PREDICTED."

r01.name: Foundry Head
r01.desc: A gantry above the pour floor. Heat rising. Stairs down south.
r01.long:
The stairs come out on a gantry and the heat hits you like a hand.

Below, the foundry: eight furnaces in a row, all lit, and crews working the pour in the orange light, and every one of them is carrying something.

It is in colour, and here the colour means something different. Up on Clause 7 it was a gift. Down here it is just what molten metal looks like.

r02.name: Charge Floor
r02.desc: Where the debts go in. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
This is where they charge the furnaces, and the charge is not scrap.

It is paper. Bales of it, wire-bound, fed in by the barrowload: statements, demands, judgements, forty years of somebody owing somebody. It burns hot and it burns clean and what comes out the other end is metal, and nobody has ever explained that step.

r03.name: Barrow Run
r03.desc: A run worn into the floor by wheels. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
Two grooves in the concrete, a barrow's width apart, worn eight inches deep over decades.

They run from the charge floor to the furnaces and back and they are the most honest thing in this building: forty years of somebody pushing something they owed, in a straight line, both ways.

r04.name: Tally Office
r04.desc: A room of running totals. Doors east.
r04.long:
Boards floor to ceiling, each one a name and a running total, chalked, adjusted, chalked again.

Most totals go up. A few go down slowly. Three have been wiped clean, and under the clean patch you can still see the ghost of a very large number.

There is a cash box on the desk and it has not been locked in years.
r04.chest_hint: There is a cash box on the tally desk.

r05.name: Furnace Row, North
r05.desc: Four furnaces, all lit. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
Four furnaces, doors banded shut, the metal of them a colour that means do not touch and do not stand there either.

The crews work around you without acknowledging you. Not hostility. They are simply on shift and you are not.

r06.name: Sand Floor
r06.desc: Moulds laid out in green sand. Doors west, east and south.
r06.long:
Casting floor: moulds pressed into green sand in long rows, waiting on the pour.

The moulds are ingots, mostly. Bars. Sensible shapes.

A row at the far end is not ingots and you decide, deliberately and with effort, not to walk down and confirm what shape they are.

r07.name: Pattern Store
r07.desc: Wooden patterns, hung by size. Doors west and south.
r07.long:
The pattern store: wooden masters for every mould the foundry makes, hung in order.

They are beautiful. Somebody made these with real care, by hand, in a building that has never cared about anything, and they are oiled and dusted and hung in size order and it is the only room on eight floors that has been loved.

r08.name: Slag Heap
r08.desc: Where the waste goes. Doors east and south.
r08.long:
The slag heap: forty years of what was left over, cooled into black glassy lumps, heaped to the ceiling.

Running through it, unmelted, undamaged, in enormous quantity: paperclips.

They do not melt. Nothing here melts them. You put one in your pocket and it is exactly the same temperature as your hand.

r09.name: Crucible Wash
r09.desc: Where the vessels are cleaned. Doors north, east and south.
r09.long: Crucibles up-ended on racks, being scraped out by somebody who has been scraping out crucibles for a very long time and does not look up.

r10.name: The Crib
r10.desc: A crew room with the heat shut out. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r10.long:
A crib: brick walls, a heavy door, a bench, a water urn, and forty years of crew names scratched into the plaster around the bench at sitting height.

It was built before the acquisition, into the original foundry wall, which is why nothing follows you in.

The urn works. The water is cold. You sit down among the names.

r11.name: Pour Aisle
r11.desc: The working aisle. Doors north, west, east and south.
r11.long:
The main aisle between the furnaces and the sand floor, and the ladles come along it on an overhead rail at head height, full, swinging.

You learn the rhythm quickly because the alternative is not learning it.

r12.name: Furnace Row, South
r12.desc: Four more furnaces. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
The southern four, and one of them is out.

Cold, dark, door open, and inside it is clean, swept, and dry. Somebody has been sleeping in a furnace. It is, on reflection, the safest place on this floor.

r13.name: The Overhang
r13.desc: A pitch under the rail gantry. Doors west and south.
r13.long:
Under the gantry, out of the drip line, he has set up again: table, lamp, flask, stock.

"Eight," he says, by way of greeting. "You've done eight. Do you want to know how many people I've sold to on eight?"

He does not tell you and you do not ask.

r14.name: Ladle Repair
r14.desc: Ladles in various states. Doors east and south.
r14.long: Ladles up on stands being relined, and the lining material is stacked in bags with a manufacturer's name on it from a country that stopped existing.

r15.name: Weighbridge
r15.desc: A platform scale sunk into the floor. Doors north, east and south.
r15.long:
A weighbridge, and a hut beside it with a printout roll going back decades.

Every barrow that has crossed this plate is on that roll. The weights are consistent, and then, about a third of the way through, they all step up by roughly the weight of a person, and stay there.

r16.name: The Long Pour
r16.desc: A channel of moving metal. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
A runner channel a foot wide crossing the room, full and moving, and the only way across is three steel plates laid over it.

The plates are hot. You do not stop on them.

r17.name: The Guarantee Post
r17.desc: A post where obligations were sworn. Doors north, west, east and south.
r17.long:
A cast-iron post in the middle of the floor with a ring at the top, worn bright.

This is where they swore the guarantees: hand on the ring, obligation stated, witnessed.

Something is standing beside it with its hand resting on the ring, and it has been standing there long enough that the shape of its hand is in the wear.

r18.name: Cooling Bay
r18.desc: Rows of castings cooling down. Doors north, west and south.
r18.long:
Fresh castings in racks, ticking as they cool, going from orange to red to grey over about an hour.

The grey ones at the far end look exactly like the walls of the first floor, and that is not a coincidence, and you work out what this building is made of and wish you had not.

r19.name: Scrap Return
r19.desc: Failed castings, returned. Doors west and south.
r19.long:
The scrap return: castings that failed inspection, stacked to go back in the furnace.

Most have a visible flaw. A few do not, and those ones have a tag on them reading REJECTED - NO REASON RECORDED, and there are more of those than there should be.

r20.name: Records Vault
r20.desc: A brick vault off the pour floor. Doors east and south.
r20.long:
A brick vault with a steel door, cool inside, holding the foundry's own records rather than anyone's debts.

Somebody has been in here recently and been through it methodically, and left everything squared up, and left one crate open on purpose in the middle of the floor.
r20.chest_hint: There is a crate left open in the middle of the floor.

r21.name: Sand Reclaim
r21.desc: Where the sand is recovered. Doors north, east and south.
r21.long:
The reclaim plant: used moulding sand shaken out, screened, and returned to the floor to be used again.

Nothing is wasted here. Not the sand, not the metal, not the slag, not the people.

r22.name: Ingot Store
r22.desc: Bars, stacked and numbered. Doors north, west, east and south.
r22.long:
Ingots stacked in courses to the roof, each one stamped with a number.

The numbers are not weights or dates. They are debts: this bar is that amount, permanently, in a form somebody can carry.

That is the whole clause, cast in metal and stacked eleven high.

r23.name: The Bond Aisle
r23.desc: An aisle of sealed documents in cases. Doors north, west, east and south.
r23.long:
Glass-fronted cases down both sides, each holding one document under a wax seal.

They are bonds. Guarantees given, unexercised, waiting. The dates go back before the foundry and one of them, in the last case, has no date on it at all.

r24.name: Heat Treatment
r24.desc: Ovens for hardening. Doors north, west, east and south.
r24.long:
Long low ovens for hardening what has been cast, and a chart on the wall of times and temperatures, annotated by hand in four different inks over decades.

The last annotation is recent. Same handwriting as the mug, the note, the marker on Clause 3.

r25.name: The Bond Room
r25.desc: A room where guarantees are called in. Doors north and west.
r25.long:
A panelled room, incongruously smart, with a table and two chairs and a decanter.

This is where they call the bonds in: politely, over a drink, in a room designed to make it feel reasonable.

Somebody is already seated, and has poured two, and gestures at the other chair with genuine warmth.
r25.chest_hint: There is a strongbox under the table.

r26.name: Survey Office
r26.desc: A drawing office, disused. Doors east and south.
r26.long:
A drawing office with a plan chest and boards on stands, unused for decades.

One board has a fresh sheet pinned to it. It is a survey of this floor, hand-drawn, complete, and it is finished, and there is a note in the corner reading: for whoever's behind me. sorry about the pace.

There is a crate underneath with more in it.
r26.chest_hint: There is a crate under the drawing board.

r27.name: Second Crib
r27.desc: Another crew room. Cool, quiet, safe. Doors north, east and south.
r27.long:
The second crib, same brick, same bench, same names in the plaster.

And on the bench: the mug, and beside it, a second mug.

They have started setting out two.

r28.name: Moulding Shop
r28.desc: Where the moulds are made. Doors north, west, east and south.
r28.long:
The moulding shop, and the patterns from the store are in use here, pressed into sand and lifted clear.

One bench is working a pattern that is not in the store, and the mould in the sand is person-shaped, and the moulder is doing it with the same care as everything else in this room, which is the worst possible way for it to be happening.

r29.name: Runner Junction
r29.desc: Where the channels meet. Doors north, west, east and south.
r29.long:
Four runner channels meet here in a basin and the metal turns in it slowly, and the light off it is the brightest thing on the floor.

You can see your face in it. Not clearly. Clearly enough.

r30.name: Cooling Bay
r30.desc: Off the foundry floor, and twenty degrees down.
r30.long:
The crews use this to stand in when the heat gets past what a person can do, and it works: the air is merely warm, and after the foundry that is close to cold.

There is a water butt with a tin cup chained to it, a bench worn smooth, and a rota on the wall with every name crossed out but one. Nothing follows you in here. The heat does not either.

r31.name: Crew Store
r31.desc: Kit, and a display. Doors north and west.
r31.long:
The crew store: gloves, aprons, visors, boots, all in sizes, all worn, all put back.

And on the counter, a small display of arbitration merchandise, with a card reading FOUNDRY EXCLUSIVE, and a price in paperclips.
r31.item_hint: There is merchandise on the counter.

r32.name: The Approach
r32.desc: A ramp down to a set of double doors. Doors north, east and south.
r32.long:
The ramp goes down and the heat goes up and the doors at the bottom are open.

Above them, cast into the lintel rather than painted on: HELD HARMLESS.

r33.name: Under the Gantry
r33.desc: A space behind the plant. Doors west.
r33.long:
Behind the ladle plant there is a space nobody uses, and somebody has been using it.

A bedroll. A crate of supplies, most of it untouched. A tally on the brick, and this one has stopped: it runs to a number and then there is a line drawn under it and a date, and the date is recent.

They stopped counting. On a floor this far down that could mean two things and only one of them is good.
r33.chest_hint: There is a supply crate here, mostly untouched.

r34.name: The Indemnity Hall
r34.desc: A long hall to a single door.
r34.long:
A hall the length of the foundry with nothing in it, floor swept, walls bare, and one door at the end.

On both walls, at eye height, running the whole way: names. Thousands. Cut into the brick.

They are the people who stood behind other people. Every one of them held harmless somebody else at their own cost, and every one of them is on this wall, and none of them is anywhere else.

r35.name: Held Harmless
r35.desc: A room with a furnace in it and something standing between. One door north.
r35.long:
One furnace, open, roaring, and the whole room is the colour of it.

Between you and it, The Guarantor: enormous, patient, hands loose at its sides, and it has been standing exactly there for forty years while everything above it happened.

It looks at you. Then, deliberately, it looks past you, at your companion, and it holds that look for a moment too long, and then comes back to you.

"You brought someone," it says. It sounds sorry. "They didn't sign anything, did they."

vorn.intro:
Vorn stops mid-swing.

"We will take this part in chambers," it says, and sits, and produces five dice from somewhere in the robes.

"The court finds the physical arbitration inconclusive to this point. The court will therefore determine the middle of this matter on the dice, which is a recognised procedure in three jurisdictions and one of them still exists.

Best of three. Bid honestly. I will know."
vorn.win:
"Judgment for the disputant on the interlocutory matter."

Vorn stands, and there is something wrong with how it stands, and you realise it has genuinely not planned for this part going the other way.
vorn.lose:
"Judgment for the respondent."

Vorn puts the dice away without hurrying. "That is not the whole matter. That is one part of it. Do sit up."

r01.name: The Clean Cut
r01.desc: A landing that ends in a straight edge. Stairs behind, a door south.
r01.long:
The stairs come down into a room with three walls.

The fourth is not damaged. It is absent, cut off along a plane so exact that the carpet, the skirting and the wall all stop at the same line, and past the line there is nothing at all.

A laminated notice is pinned beside it, half of it gone, and the half that remains reads: ...SHALL CONTINUE IN FULL FORCE.

r02.name: Upper Fragment
r02.desc: A block of rooms that ends abruptly. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long: You are in a piece of building. It has its own corridors and its own lights and its own opinions about where things are, and it is about nine rooms across, and then it stops.

r03.name: Half Corridor
r03.desc: A corridor missing its left-hand side. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
The corridor has a left wall for the first six feet and then does not, and the rooms that were behind it are not behind it any more.

You can see the floor of them, three feet away, at the same level, unreachable.

r04.name: Store, Severed
r04.desc: A storeroom cut down the middle. Doors east.
r04.long:
Half a storeroom, and it is the half with the shelving in it, and the shelving is packed.

The cut runs through a filing cabinet. The three drawers on this side still open. The fourth was on the other side and is somewhere else now.

r05.name: The Overlap
r05.desc: A room that appears to be in two places. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
Something has gone wrong here in the opposite direction: instead of a piece missing there is a piece too many, and the room contains two versions of the same corner.

You walk into one and come out of the other and the room is fine with this.

r06.name: Rump Office
r06.desc: An office with one wall and most of a desk. Doors west and south.
r06.long:
One wall, most of a desk, and a chair that is entirely intact and pushed neatly in.

Somebody tidied up after the severance. That is either dedication or something worse.

r07.name: Fragment Edge
r07.desc: Where the upper piece stops. Doors east and south.
r07.long:
The edge of this fragment. You stand at it and look across the gap at the next piece of the floor, which is at the same height, about eight feet away, fully lit, entirely normal.

There is no way across from here. There is a way across somewhere. That is how severability works.

r08.name: Junction, Partial
r08.desc: A junction with one arm missing. Doors north, west, east and south.
r08.long: A four-way junction with three arms. The fourth is drawn on the floor in worn carpet and then simply is not there.

r09.name: The Intact Room
r09.desc: A room with all four walls, all four corners, and a kettle. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r09.long:
Four walls. Ceiling. Floor. Every corner where a corner should be.

After twenty minutes on this floor the effect of a complete room is close to physical. There is a kettle, a bench, and a wall clock that is running.

This room predates the contract. That is why nothing has been taken out of it and why nothing comes in.

r10.name: Aisle, Truncated
r10.desc: An aisle that ends in air. Doors north, west, east and south.
r10.long: The aisle runs twenty feet and stops. The last shelf is cut vertically and the boxes on the cut side have spilled their contents into the gap, where they are still falling, very slowly, and have been for some time.

r11.name: Seam
r11.desc: A narrow room joining two pieces of the floor. Doors north, west and south.
r11.long:
This room is a seam: a single narrow space that happens to touch two fragments at once, and is therefore the only way between them.

It is load-bearing in a floor where nothing is supposed to be. Somebody has scratched into the wall: NOT SEVERABLE. HA.

r12.name: The Whole Cupboard
r12.desc: A cupboard, undamaged, with a table set up in it. Doors west and south.
r12.long:
A stationery cupboard that came through the severance completely intact, and he has set up inside it.

There is exactly enough room for the table and the stool and him. He seems delighted with it.

"Best pitch in the building," he says. "Four walls. You have no idea."

r13.name: Isolate
r13.desc: A room with one door and no other features. Doors east.
r13.long:
A room with one door and nothing else. No fittings, no marks, no dust.

It is not a severed room. It is a room that was made by two severances meeting, and it has never had anything in it, and it is the newest place in the building.
r13.npc_hint: There is a woman here writing into a very large book, and she has seen you.

r14.name: Middle Fragment
r14.desc: The top of the second piece. Doors east, west and south.
r14.long:
You are in a different piece of the floor now and it has a different carpet.

Not damaged. Different. This piece came from somewhere else, or was always somewhere else, and the join between the two is the only thing holding either in place.

r15.name: Half Stair
r15.desc: A stairwell that goes down four steps and stops. Doors north, west, east and south.
r15.long:
A stairwell, cut horizontally. Four steps down, then the flat plane of the cut, then nothing.

You can see the bottom of the stairwell below, several feet down and eighteen inches sideways, still going.

r16.name: The Left Half
r16.desc: A room containing one half of something large. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
The room is large and mostly empty and there is a thing standing in the middle of it.

It is half a thing. Vertically. It has one arm, one leg, one eye, and it is standing perfectly balanced in a way that half a thing should not be able to.

When it notices you it does not turn round. It only has the one side.

r17.name: Cross Fragment
r17.desc: A wide room spanning most of the piece. Doors north, west, east and south.
r17.long:
The widest room in this fragment, and every wall of it is a cut face except one.

The one original wall has a window in it. The window looks out onto the inside of another part of the building, six inches away, wall to glass.

r18.name: Dead Section
r18.desc: A section that failed and was left. Doors north and west.
r18.long:
This part did not survive the severance well. The lights are out, the floor is at four degrees, and everything loose has slid into the low corner and stayed there.

It is still in force. Everything is still in force.

r19.name: Salvage Corner
r19.desc: Where things that survived have been put. Doors east and south.
r19.long:
Somebody has been going round the fragments collecting whole objects and putting them here.

A whole chair. A whole mug. A whole box file with all four corners. It is not hoarding. It reads more like an argument being made, item by item, that whole things exist.
r19.chest_hint: There is a case here among the whole things.

r20.name: The Narrow Way
r20.desc: A room you cross sideways. Doors north, west, east and south.
r20.long:
Two cuts have come within eighteen inches of each other and left a strip of floor you have to cross side-on with your back to one drop and your face to the other.

It is fine. It is eighteen inches. It is fine.

r21.name: The Seam, Lower
r21.desc: The one join to the bottom of the floor. Doors north, west and south.
r21.long:
The second seam, and the last one. Below this the floor is a separate thing entirely, and this room is the whole of the connection.

If this room went, the bottom of Clause 9 would be unreachable and would carry on in full force, alone, indefinitely. You think about that and then stop.

r22.name: Offcut Yard
r22.desc: Where the pieces went. Doors north, west and east.
r22.long:
A room filled to chest height with offcuts: the parts of other rooms that were removed, stacked, sorted roughly by size.

Somebody sorted them. That is the detail that keeps happening on this floor and it never gets easier.

r23.name: The Remainder Room
r23.desc: A room that is what is left. Doors north and west.
r23.long:
The sign on the door says REMAINDER and the room behind it is everything the floor did not need: fittings, sections, three doors, part of a staircase, all of it in force and none of it attached to anything.

In the middle, on a chair, something is sitting with its hands folded, and it is the only whole thing in the room, and it has been waiting.
r23.chest_hint: There is a strongbox among the remainder.

r24.name: Lower Fragment
r24.desc: The top of the last piece. Doors east and south.
r24.long:
The last fragment, and the largest, and the quietest.

The carpet here is the original grey from Clause 1. This piece is the oldest part of the floor and everything else was cut away from it rather than the other way round.

r25.name: Long Remainder
r25.desc: A corridor that survived intact. Doors north, west, east and south.
r25.long:
A full-length corridor with both walls and a ceiling, running the length of the fragment.

After everything above, walking down a corridor that simply continues feels close to luxurious.

r26.name: Second Intact Room
r26.desc: Four walls, a bench, a warm kettle. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r26.long:
The other whole room, and the kettle is warm again.

On the bench: the mug, and the second mug, and this time both have been used.

They sat here with somebody. Recently. There is no third mug and you find that you mind.

r27.name: The Sound Floor
r27.desc: A room where the cuts have not reached. Doors north, west, east and south.
r27.long:
Nothing has been taken from this room and nothing is going to be. It is at the middle of the largest fragment and it is as far from an edge as this floor gets.

It is an ordinary meeting room. Ten chairs, a table, a whiteboard with nothing on it. It is unbearable.

r28.name: Cut Face
r28.desc: A room with one enormous exposed section. Doors north, west, east and south.
r28.long:
One entire wall is a cut face, and the cut has gone through nine floors of building at once, and you can see all of them: nine storeys of severed rooms stacked in cross-section like a diagram.

Some of them have things moving in them.

r29.name: Tail End
r29.desc: Where the fragment thins out. Doors north and west.
r29.long: The fragment narrows to two rooms wide here and then one and then stops, and the stopping is gradual rather than clean, which is the only untidy cut on the whole floor.

r30.name: The Whole Store
r30.desc: A storeroom nothing was taken from. Doors east.
r30.long:
Somebody found a room the cuts had missed entirely and filled it with what they could not risk losing.

Crates, sealed. A bedroll. And on the wall, in marker: THINGS THAT ARE STILL ONE THING.

Underneath, a much shorter list in the same hand, and the last item on it is: me (so far).

r31.name: Whole Office
r31.desc: One room on this floor that the severance missed.
r31.long:
Four walls, a ceiling, a floor, and all of them meeting each other the way they were drawn. After the rest of Floor 9 the effect is almost rude.

Somebody has kept it up: a kettle, two mugs, a calendar eleven years out of date and a chair pushed in. Whatever was following you stops at the door, because the door is a real door.

r32.name: Junction, Whole
r32.desc: An ordinary four-way junction. Doors north, west, east and south.
r32.long:
A junction with four arms, all present, all going somewhere.

You stand in it for a second longer than you need to.

r33.name: Anteroom
r33.desc: A small room before the last door. Doors north, west and east.
r33.long:
A small square room with a bench along one wall and a door at the far end, and the door has been cut in half vertically and repaired, badly, by hand, with screws.

Somebody wanted this specific door to still work.

r34.name: Staff Remainder
r34.desc: Lockers, and a display. Doors north and west.
r34.long:
Staff lockers, half of them severed, and the surviving half fully stocked.

And a merchandise display, intact, complete, undamaged, which on this floor makes it the single most conspicuous object you have seen.
r34.item_hint: There is merchandise here, entirely undamaged.

r35.name: The Last Whole Room
r35.desc: Four walls, a bench, and quiet. Safe. Doors north and south.
r35.long:
One more complete room, and it is the last one on this floor.

The bench has been sat on recently. The kettle is warm. And there is a single sheet of paper on the bench, weighted with the mug, which says:

CLAUSE 9 GIVES YOU ONE BACK. TAKE THE REST HERE. IT IS WORSE AFTER THIS AND I AM NOT GOING TO PRETEND OTHERWISE.

r36.name: Both Halves
r36.desc: A room with something standing in the middle of it. One door north.
r36.long:
The room is the largest complete space on the floor and there is one thing in it.

Hemikin: the right half, standing where the left half is not, balanced the same impossible way, and it is very much larger than the half you met upstairs.

If you took the left, it is visibly diminished, listing, working harder than it should have to.

If you did not, there are two of them, and they are standing back to back, and they have been waiting like that for a very long time.

rooms9.trapdoor:
The floor of this room is a door, and it has been a door the
whole time you have been standing on it.

It opens the way a door opens: without drama, on hinges, having
been designed to. You go through it.

The fall is short and unhurried and ends on something that gives.
Floor 9 was severed into pieces that do not join up. This is one
of the joins. Nobody wrote it down because nobody survived the
paperwork, not the drop.

r01.name: Court Steps
r01.desc: A flight of stone steps up to a portico. A door south.
r01.long:
The stairwell from Clause 9 lets out at the bottom of a flight of stone steps, going up, to a portico with columns.

You are indoors. You have been indoors for ten floors. There are steps, and weather-worn stone, and pigeon spikes, and above the portico, cut into the lintel: FIAT IUSTITIA.

The doors at the top are open. Beyond them the building carries on being a courthouse in a way that does not survive counting the distances.

r02.name: Great Hall
r02.desc: A vaulted hall with corridors off it. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
A vaulted hall with a floor of black and white stone and four corridors leading off it.

The vault is eighty feet up. The floor above this one, on Clause 9, was eleven feet up. Both of those are true and you decide to be somewhere else about it.

r03.name: List Corridor
r03.desc: A corridor of court lists in glass cases. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
Glass cases down both walls holding the day's lists: which matter is being heard, where, and at what time.

Every entry is your name. Every court. Every time slot. All day, in every room, simultaneously, for the last forty years.

r04.name: Robing Room
r04.desc: Where the court dresses. Doors east.
r04.long:
Pegs, mirrors, and forty sets of court dress hanging in size order.

Nobody has taken one down in a long time. The mirrors have gone slightly milky and the wigs on the shelf above have been eaten by something.

There is a trunk at the end of the row.

r05.name: Corridor of Waiting
r05.desc: Benches down both sides. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
A corridor of benches, worn in the middle of each one, where people sat waiting to be called.

The wear is deep. Some of these benches have been sat on by the same person for years.

r06.name: Court Two
r06.desc: A working courtroom with nobody in it. Doors west, east and south.
r06.long:
Court Two: bench, dock, gallery, clerk's table, all of it, lights on, ready.

The list outside says a matter is being heard in here right now. There is nobody in the room. The stenotype on the clerk's table is running.

r07.name: Interview Room
r07.desc: A small room with a table bolted down. Doors west and south.
r07.long:
A room with one table, two chairs, and a mirror on the long wall that anybody would recognise.

The table is bolted down and the bolts are worn shiny by forty years of people holding onto the edge of it.

r08.name: Consultation
r08.desc: A cramped room for talking to your representative. Doors east and south.
r08.long:
A cupboard of a room where a person would sit down with whoever was representing them.

There is one chair. There has only ever been one chair. Nobody in this building has ever had representation and somebody built the room anyway.

r09.name: Court One
r09.desc: The main courtroom. Doors north, west, east and south.
r09.long:
Court One is enormous and the proportions are wrong in a way you cannot pin down until you count the windows from inside and then from the corridor and get different answers.

The bench is empty. The gallery is full and every seat is occupied and nobody in them is looking at anything.

r10.name: Judge's Chambers
r10.desc: A panelled room with a fire and two chairs. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r10.long:
Chambers: panelling, a fireplace with an actual fire in it, two armchairs, and a decanter with the stopper out.

This room is older than the court around it and considerably older than the contract. Nothing follows you in.

One chair has been sat in recently. The other has not been sat in for forty years and there is dust on the arm.

r11.name: Records Corridor
r11.desc: A corridor lined with judgment books. Doors north, west, east and south.
r11.long:
Bound volumes of judgments, floor to ceiling, by year, going back further than the building.

You pull one at random. Every judgment in it went the same way. You check three more volumes and stop checking.

r12.name: Court Three
r12.desc: A smaller court, in use. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
Court Three is smaller and busier: papers on the tables, a jug half full, a coat over the back of a chair.

It was in use twenty minutes ago and it is not in use now, and nobody has left the building, because you would have seen them.

r13.name: The Portico Nook
r13.desc: A dry corner under the columns. Doors north and south.
r13.long:
Between two columns of the portico there is a dry corner out of the wind, and he has set up in it with the table and the lamp and a folding screen.

"Courthouse," he says, without enthusiasm. "Everyone's very polite here and nobody buys anything. You'll be my second customer since the acquisition."

He does not say who the first was.

r14.name: Cell Corridor
r14.desc: A corridor of holding cells. Doors east and south.
r14.long:
Holding cells, six of them, doors standing open, each one with a bench and a high window.

Five are empty and clean. The sixth has been lived in: blanket, tally on the wall, a book. The door has been open the whole time.

r15.name: Usher's Station
r15.desc: A desk beside a courtroom door. Doors north, west, east and south.
r15.long:
A high desk with a list, a bell, and a chair.

The list is today's. Somebody has been crossing matters off it all morning and the pen is still uncapped.
r15.npc_hint: The usher has stopped crossing things off and is looking at you.

r16.name: Waiting Hall
r16.desc: A large hall of chairs facing nothing. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long: Two hundred chairs in rows facing a blank wall with a screen above it that has been showing PLEASE WAIT for long enough to burn the words into the panel.

r17.name: The Registry
r17.desc: Counters, ledgers, and one occupant. Doors north, west, east and south.
r17.long:
The registry: a long counter with six positions, five shuttered, one open.

Behind the open one, somebody has been working steadily for four decades and looks up as you approach with the particular expression of a person who has been expecting you specifically and has your file ready.

r18.name: Corridor, Impossible
r18.desc: A corridor that is longer inside. Doors north, west and south.
r18.long:
You enter this corridor from a hall forty feet across and walk two hundred feet down it and come out into the same hall from the other side.

Both doors are visible from the middle. The middle is not visible from either door.

r19.name: Court Four
r19.desc: A courtroom in disuse. Doors north, west and south.
r19.long:
Court Four has been closed. Dust sheets on the benches, the clock stopped, the royal arms above the bench covered over with brown paper.

Somebody covered it up rather than take it down.

r20.name: Evidence Store
r20.desc: Boxes of what was not admitted. Doors east and south.
r20.long:
Racks of boxes, each sealed, each labelled EXCLUDED with a date.

There are more of these than there are judgments. Considerably more. Everything that would have made a difference is in this room, in order, preserved perfectly, and none of it was ever seen.
r20.chest_hint: One box has been opened and left open.

r21.name: Jury Assembly
r21.desc: A room for people who never came. Doors north, west, east and south.
r21.long:
A jury assembly room with a hundred chairs, a tea urn, and a rack of leaflets explaining jury service.

No jury has ever been summoned here. The leaflets are printed, boxed, and current.

r22.name: The Long Bench
r22.desc: A corridor with one continuous bench. Doors north, west, east and south.
r22.long:
One bench, running the entire length of the corridor, unbroken, perhaps ninety feet.

The wear on it is even the whole way along. A great many people have waited here at once.

r23.name: Judgment Store
r23.desc: Where the judgments are kept. Doors north, west, east and south.
r23.long:
Every judgment this court has handed down, filed, in order.

The section for disputes is one box. The box is not full. There are eleven files in it and ten of them are closed.

r24.name: Silent Court
r24.desc: A courtroom with the sound taken out. Doors north, west, east and south.
r24.long:
You step in and the sound goes. Not muffled: removed. Your footsteps make no noise, the door makes no noise, and when you say something out loud nothing happens at all.

The stenotype on the clerk's desk is typing. You can see the keys going.

r25.name: The Cells
r25.desc: Deeper holding, below the courts. Doors north and west.
r25.long:
Down a half-flight, the real cells: heavier doors, no windows, a rail down the middle of the corridor for attaching people to.

Somebody is standing at the far end with their hands behind their back, waiting, entirely relaxed, in the manner of a person who has never once had to hurry.
r25.chest_hint: There is a property locker at the end of the corridor.

r26.name: The Excluded Room
r26.desc: Where the excluded evidence was read. Doors east and south.
r26.long:
A reading room off the evidence store, with one desk and a lamp.

Boxes are stacked around the desk in the order they were opened and there is a notepad with eleven pages of neat handwriting, and the last line reads: it was all here the whole time. all of it. eleven of us and it was in a box.

The handwriting is the handwriting from the walls of every break room in the building. They were the eleventh when they wrote that, and they counted themselves, and they had not met you yet.
r26.chest_hint: There is a case beside the desk.

r27.name: Corridor, Formal
r27.desc: A corridor with a red rope down the middle. Doors north, west, east and south.
r27.long:
A rope on brass posts divides the corridor down the middle into a side for the court and a side for everybody else.

Both sides are the same width. Both sides are empty. The rope is immaculate.

r28.name: Second Chambers
r28.desc: Another panelled room with a fire. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r28.long:
The second set of chambers, and the fire is lit in this one too.

Both armchairs have been sat in. There are two glasses on the side table, one empty, one untouched, and between them a folded note with nothing written on the outside.

Inside it says: he'll offer you the dice. take it. he is better at fighting than he is at dice and he does not know that about himself.

r29.name: The Rotunda
r29.desc: A circular room with eight doors. Doors north, west, east and south.
r29.long:
A circular room with eight doors evenly spaced around it and four of them lead somewhere.

The other four open onto the same view: this room, from the other side, with you standing in it, from behind.

r30.name: Barristers' Robing
r30.desc: A second robing room, in use. Doors north, west, east and south.
r30.long:
This robing room is in use. Coats on pegs, bags under the bench, papers spread out, three sets of court dress laid ready.

Three. There has been nobody in this building but you and one other person for a very long time.

r31.name: Public Entrance
r31.desc: Where the public came in. Doors north and west.
r31.long:
The public entrance: an airlock of glass doors, a security arch, a tray for keys and belts.

The outer doors are open. Past them there is a street. There are buildings on it. There is weather.

You walk out. Twelve feet along the pavement you are walking back into the public entrance, from the inside, having gone nowhere. You try it twice.

r32.name: Adjournment Room
r32.desc: A room with the lights on a timer and a kettle that somebody keeps descaling.
r32.long:
Nothing is listed in here. That is the whole function of the room: a space on the floor plan with no matter attached to it, and so nothing that can be called on while you are standing in it.

There is a kettle, a box of teabags with a tally on the lid, and four chairs that do not match. Whatever was following you stops at the door and waits, because it has to.

r33.name: The Well
r33.desc: A stairwell down to the last court. Doors north and east.
r33.long:
A stone stairwell going down, worn in the centre of every tread, with a handrail polished by forty years of hands.

Everybody who has ever been sentenced in this building walked down these. That is what the wear is.

r34.name: Antechamber, Court Thirteen
r34.desc: A small room outside a large door. Doors north, west and east.
r34.long:
A plain room with a bench, outside a door that is much larger than the room deserves.

The door has no number on it. Every other court in this building is numbered.

r35.name: Property Office
r35.desc: Where the effects were kept. Doors north and west.
r35.long:
The property office: shelves of sealed bags holding what people had on them when they came in.

Keys, wallets, phones, one bicycle helmet. Every bag is labelled with a name and a date and every date is a date they did not leave.

And a display case of merchandise, because there is always a display case.
r35.item_hint: There is merchandise in the property office display.

r36.name: Chambers, Vorn's
r36.desc: A panelled room, a fire, and a very old chair. Safe. Doors north and south.
r36.long:
The last set of chambers, and this is the one that is used.

A fire, a chair with the seat worn into a shape, forty years of judgments on the shelves, and on the desk a set of five dice in a leather cup, worn smooth.

Rest here. He knows you are coming and he is not going to interrupt this part.

r37.name: Court Thirteen
r37.desc: An enormous courtroom with one occupant. One door north.
r37.long:
The room is a courtroom the size of a cathedral and every seat in the gallery is full and not one of them is a person.

On the bench, alone, in full dress, Justice Vorn: older than the court, older than the building, and entirely, visibly tired.

It looks up as you come in, and it does something no other thing in this building has done.

It stands. For you. Briefly, formally, and then it sits and says:

"The court is grateful to the disputant for attending. Let us get on."

r01.name: Amendment Landing
r01.desc: A landing where the signage is being updated. A door south.
r01.long:
The stairs come down into a small landing with a noticeboard, and the noticeboard is busy.

Notices are appearing on it. Not being pinned: appearing, replacing the ones underneath, at a rate of about one every twenty seconds, each one slightly different from the last.

The current one reads: THESE TERMS WERE UPDATED 4 SECONDS AGO. CONTINUED PRESENCE CONSTITUTES ACCEPTANCE.
r01.alt: The noticeboard is empty and clean and there is a rectangle of unfaded paint where it used to be busy.

r02.name: Redraft Hall
r02.desc: A hall with the walls being rewritten. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long: The text on the walls is under revision. Whole paragraphs are being struck through and replaced while you watch, and the replacements are struck through in turn.
r02.alt: The hall is bare plaster. Whatever was written here has been settled and painted over, and the paint is dry.

r03.name: Clause Corridor
r03.desc: A corridor of numbered clauses. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long: Every panel down this corridor holds one numbered clause, and the numbers do not run in order and do not stay on the same panel.
r03.alt: The panels are in order now, 1 to 13, and every one of them is blank except the eleventh.

r04.name: Superseded Store
r04.long:
Boxes and boxes of superseded versions, each labelled with the date it stopped being in force.

The most recent box is labelled with today's date and it is already full.
r04.alt: The boxes have gone. There is one box, and it is labelled with today's date, and it is empty.

r05.name: Variation Room
r05.desc: A room whose fittings keep changing. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
The fittings in this room are not the same fittings. The chairs were a different colour, there were four of them, there is now one, and it is a different kind of chair.

You did not look away.
r05.alt: One chair, in the middle, facing the door you came in by.

r06.name: Notice Board Hall
r06.desc: A hall of notices to nobody. Doors west, east and south.
r06.long: Notices of variation pinned in overlapping layers, hundreds deep, and the layers at the bottom have fused into board.
r06.alt: A single notice, centred, correctly spelled, addressed to you by name.

r07.name: Consultation Room
r07.desc: Where changes were consulted on. Doors west and south.
r07.long:
A room set up for a consultation: chairs in a circle, flip chart, refreshments.

The flip chart says WHAT MATTERS TO YOU? and the rest of the pad is blank.
r07.alt: The chairs are stacked against the wall and the flip chart has been taken away.

r08.name: Effective Date
r08.desc: A room with a clock that will not settle. Doors east and south.
r08.long:
A wall clock whose hands move to a time, stop, and then move to a different time, none of which are now.

Under it, a printed card: ALL CHANGES EFFECTIVE IMMEDIATELY.
r08.alt: The clock has stopped. The card under it now reads: NO FURTHER CHANGES ARE ANTICIPATED.

r09.name: Marginal Notes
r09.desc: A room where everything has been annotated. Doors north, west, east and south.
r09.long:
Every surface has been written on in the margin: queries, corrections, small pointed observations, all in the same hand.

The hand is yours. It is definitely yours. You have not been in this room.
r09.alt: The annotations have been cleaned off and the surfaces are bare, and the cleaning was recent and thorough.

r10.name: The Original Copy
r10.desc: A room with one document in a case. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r10.long:
A quiet room, older than the floor, with a display case in it holding one document under glass.

It is the original. Version one. Before any amendment, and the case has never been opened, and the room around it has never been revised because nobody can revise what they cannot get at.

That is why nothing follows you in here. There is a bench, and a kettle, and forty years of somebody sitting with the original.

r11.name: Redline Corridor
r11.desc: A corridor of tracked changes. Doors north, west, east and south.
r11.long:
Everything in this corridor is in two colours: what it was, struck through, and what it is now, underlined.

Both are legible. Neither is settled.
r11.alt: Everything here is in one colour and reads cleanly, and you find you miss knowing what it used to say.

r12.name: Schedule Room
r12.desc: Appendices, incorporated by reference. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
Schedules one through nine, bound and shelved, each one longer than the agreement it is attached to.

Schedule Two is missing from the shelf. There is a gap and a card reading OUT.
r12.alt: Schedule Two has been returned to the shelf. It is warm.

r13.name: Under the Awning
r13.desc: A corner the amendments do not reach. Doors north and south.
r13.long:
He has pitched under a stone soffit, and there is a chalk line drawn on the floor around the whole pitch.

"Nothing inside the line gets amended," he says. "Don't ask me why the line works. I drew it in 1987 and it has worked ever since and I have made my peace with not knowing."

r14.name: Insertion Point
r14.desc: A room that has been added recently. Doors east and south.
r14.long:
This room is new. The plaster is new, the paint is new, and it has been inserted between two rooms that used to be adjacent.

There is nothing in it and no reason for it. It is a subclause with no content, added to make room for something later.
r14.alt: The room has furniture now. A desk, a chair, a lamp. Somebody is going to be working here.

r15.name: Deletion
r15.desc: A room that is being removed. Doors north, west, east and south.
r15.long:
This room is going. Not collapsing: being deleted, from the corners inward, and the deletion has paused about a third of the way through.

You can stand in the remaining two thirds perfectly safely. Probably.
r15.alt: The deletion has been reversed and the room is whole again, and there is no mark where the missing part was.

r16.name: Working Draft
r16.desc: A room in an unfinished state. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
Half the fittings are placeholders: a door that is a drawing of a door, a window that is the word WINDOW at the right height.

It all works. The drawn door opens.
r16.alt: The placeholders have been replaced with the real thing and the room is entirely ordinary, and it is much worse.

r17.name: The Markup Room
r17.desc: A room where you have been annotated. Doors north, west, east and south.
r17.long:
The walls hold a tracked-changes view of the arbitration so far, every floor, every decision, in two colours.

And in the margin, hundreds of queries, all in the same neat hand, all of them about you.

Something is standing in the middle of the room with a pen, going through them.

r18.name: Reissue
r18.desc: A room printed again from scratch. Doors north, west and south.
r18.long: Everything in this room has been reissued: same layout, same fittings, all of it brand new, all of it slightly the wrong shade.
r18.alt: The colours have settled and match, and you can no longer tell this room was ever reissued, which is the point of a reissue.

r19.name: Consolidated Text
r19.desc: A room containing every version at once. Doors north, west and south.
r19.long:
Every version of this room is present simultaneously, layered, semi-transparent, forty years deep.

You can see the original at the back, small and grey and completely ordinary.
r19.alt: Only the current version is here. The layers have been consolidated and the original is not visible any more.

r20.name: Repository
r20.desc: Where drafts were kept. Doors east and south.
r20.long:
Racks of drafts, versioned, dated, most never adopted.

One rack is labelled ADOPTED and holds four documents. The rest of the room, six hundred square feet of it, is labelled NOT.
r20.chest_hint: There is a case at the end of the adopted rack.
r20.alt: The NOT racks have been cleared. The ADOPTED rack now holds five.

r21.name: Rolling Corridor
r21.desc: A corridor that revises as you walk it. Doors north, west, east and south.
r21.long:
The corridor amends behind you. You look back and the doorway you came through is a different width and the carpet has changed.

It is still a doorway and it is still there.
r21.alt: The corridor is behaving. Nothing changes for the whole length of it and you do not trust a step of it.

r22.name: Notice Period
r22.desc: A room where changes wait to take effect. Doors north, west, east and south.
r22.long:
A room of pending amendments, each on a stand, each with a date on which it takes effect.

All the dates are today. All the times have passed.
r22.alt: The stands are empty. Everything that was pending has taken effect and you were in the building for all of it.
r22.npc_hint: Somebody is sitting on the desk, amending something, and they have noticed you.

r23.name: The Fair Copy
r23.desc: A room typed up cleanly. Doors north, west and south.
r23.long:
Someone has produced a fair copy of this room: everything correct, everything aligned, no marks, no queries.

It is the only tidy room on the floor and it feels like a warning.
r23.alt: The fair copy has been marked up again. Somebody could not leave it.

r24.name: Erratum
r24.desc: A room correcting an earlier room. Doors north, west, east and south.
r24.long:
A small room whose entire purpose is a correction to something on Clause 4.

The correction reads: FOR 'MRS HENSLEY HAS CALLED SOMEONE' READ 'MRS HENSLEY HAS ALWAYS ALREADY CALLED SOMEONE'. WE REGRET THE AMBIGUITY.
r24.alt: The erratum has itself been corrected, and the correction reads: NO CHANGE REQUIRED. THE ORIGINAL WAS ACCURATE.

r25.name: The Rider's Room
r25.desc: A room attached to another room. Doors north and west.
r25.long:
This room is a rider: attached to the last one without discussion, short, and containing one very significant thing.

The significant thing is standing up as you come in.
r25.chest_hint: There is a case under the window.

r26.name: Withdrawn
r26.desc: A room whose amendment was pulled. Doors north, west, east and south.
r26.long:
A change was made to this room and then withdrawn, and the withdrawal has not fully taken, so the room is in two states at once and neither is committed.

The floor is at two heights. You use whichever one you are standing on.
r26.alt: The withdrawal has completed and the floor is at one height, and you spend a while working out which of the two it settled on.

r27.name: Comment Thread
r27.desc: A room of arguments in the margin. Doors north, west, east and south.
r27.long:
Two hands arguing in the margins of the wall, back and forth, for what must be years.

One says the terms should be capable of withdrawal. The other says withdrawal was never contemplated. The first one stops replying about two thirds of the way down.
r27.alt: The thread has been resolved and deleted. There is a note: RESOLVED. NO ACTION.

r28.name: The Unamended Room
r28.desc: A room nothing has been done to. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r28.long:
This room has never been amended. Not because it is protected: because nobody ever thought it was worth the effort.

It is a small kitchen with a kettle and a bench and a beach photograph, and it is exactly the same as the one on Clause 1, because it is the same one, unchanged, eleven floors down.

The kettle is warm. Both mugs are out. There is tea in one of them.

r29.name: Version Control
r29.desc: Where the changes are logged. Doors north, west, east and south.
r29.long:
A wall of logbooks recording every amendment ever made: what changed, when, and on whose authority.

The authority column is blank for every entry. Forty years of changes and not one of them was authorised by anybody.
r29.alt: The authority column has been filled in, in every row, in the same handwriting, with the same word: US.

r30.name: Late Amendment
r30.desc: A change made very recently. Doors north, west, east and south.
r30.long:
This room was amended in the last few minutes and the amendment is still settling: dust in the air, a smell of new paint, a wall that is warm.

Somebody changed it because you were coming.
r30.alt: The paint has cured and the room is cold and looks like it has been this way for years.

r31.name: Final Wording
r31.desc: A room they have stopped changing. Doors north and west.
r31.long:
A room in its final wording. There are no tracked changes, no queries, no pending notices, and a small plate on the wall reads: SETTLED.

It is the only settled room on the floor and it is completely empty.
r31.alt: The plate has been removed and the wall behind it is a lighter colour.

r32.name: The Original Store
r32.desc: Where the first draft was hidden. Doors north and east.
r32.long:
Somebody hid this room from the revision process by the simple method of not writing it down anywhere.

It holds first drafts: of clauses, of floors, of the whole building. And of Clause 1, in its original wording, which said something completely different and much shorter.

There is a pack here, and a note: THE ORIGINAL CLAUSE 1 IS IN THE CRATE. IT IS NOT A WEAPON. IT MIGHT BE BETTER THAN ONE.
r32.chest_hint: There is a crate here with a note on it.

r33.name: Drafting Room (Unused)
r33.desc: A meeting room booked for a revision that never happened.
r33.long:
The booking slip on the door has a date on it and a room name and nothing else, and the revision it was booked for was never drafted, so the room has sat empty and in force ever since.

Somebody has left a kettle and a fan heater. Somebody else has left a note saying PLEASE LEAVE AS FOUND, which is the most anybody has asked of you all day. Nothing follows you in.
r33.alt: The corridor has been shortened back to its original length and you cover it in nine steps.

r34.name: Effective Corridor
r34.desc: A corridor where changes take hold. Doors north, west and east.
r34.long: Amendments take effect here first and propagate outward, and standing in it you can feel them go past, like a change in pressure.
r34.alt: Nothing goes past. The corridor is inert and the pressure is even and something upstream has stopped issuing.

r35.name: Consolidation
r35.desc: Where every version is merged. Doors north, west and east.
r35.long:
The merge point: every amendment to every part of this floor is reconciled here into one text.

The machinery for it is a long table with nobody at it and a single tray marked IN, which is empty, and a tray marked OUT, which is overflowing.
r35.alt: Both trays are empty. The table has been wiped down.

r36.name: Staff Amendments
r36.desc: Lockers, revised. Doors north and west.
r36.long:
Staff lockers, and the names on them have been amended repeatedly, each name struck through and replaced.

The last name on each is the same name.

And a merchandise display, amended: the face on the mugs is not quite yours any more. It has been updated to a more recent likeness.
r36.item_hint: There is amended merchandise on the display.

r37.name: The Settled Room
r37.desc: A room they have finished with. Safe. Doors north and south.
r37.long:
The last room before the door, and it has been left alone.

A bench, a kettle, and on the bench a folded note, and the note is longer than the others.

It says: TWO LEFT AFTER THIS. TWELVE IS A FIGHT AND YOU WILL BE FINE. THIRTEEN IS NOT A FIGHT. DO NOT GO INTO THIRTEEN READY FOR ONE. I AM SORRY I HAVE NOT WAITED. I HAVE NOT BEEN ABLE TO STOP SINCE FLOOR TWO AND I THINK YOU WILL UNDERSTAND THAT BY NOW.

r38.name: Effective Immediately
r38.desc: A room that will not hold a version. One door north.
r38.long:
The room is amending continuously and so is the thing in the middle of it.

The Amendment: whatever the current wording is, rendered, and the current wording changes while you are looking at it. It has been forty different things since you came through the door and each one was in force at the time.

"WE MAY AMEND THESE TERMS AT ANY TIME," it says, in the voice of whatever it is now.

"YOU HAVE BEEN CONTINUING TO USE IT FOR ELEVEN FLOORS."

secret.wall_opens:
You walk into the wall.

Then you do it again, because you are tired and it is the direction you wanted to go and the building has been wrong about a great many things today.

Then you do it a third time, deliberately, out of something that is not quite temper.
withdraw_said: You say it out loud, to the building. "I withdraw."
"I withdraw." Nothing in the room reacts.
"I withdraw." You are getting better at saying it.
withdraw_repeat: You say it again. The building already has this floor's; it does not write twice.
"I withdraw." Nothing takes it down. It was taken down the first time, on this floor, and once is what counts.
You repeat it. Somewhere a page stays exactly as full as it was.
It comes out flatter the second time. This clause is already answered; there are others.
withdraw_after: "I withdraw," you say, out of habit now. It has been noted. It stays noted.
The building has your position on this.
secret.withdraw_filed:
Something files it.

You do not see what and there is nothing in the room that could have, but there is a sound exactly like a drawer closing, once, somewhere below you.
sing: You sing. Badly, and only a bit, and the room takes it without comment.
You have a go at singing. The acoustics are terrible and it helps anyway.
secret.sing_again: You have already sung in this room. It has not forgotten.
sing_anywhere: You start to sing and then hear yourself and stop.
Not here. You would rather not announce yourself in this room.
secret.sing_joined:
Three rooms, three songs, and this time something joins in.

Not a voice. The pumps, the fans, the extract, the strip lights, the whole mechanical apparatus of the building falling into the same rhythm for about nine seconds and then, tidily, out of it.

Everything that made that noise was installed before the contract.
photo_none: There is no photograph in here.
Nothing on these walls is worth looking at twice.
secret.photo_again: You have already stood and looked at this one.
secret.carl:
A NOTE FROM THE ARBITRATION
  ---------------------------
  Our records show a naming collision with an
  unrelated proceeding in another jurisdiction.
  It went considerably better than this one is
  going to. We have applied a goodwill
  adjustment and we would ask you not to
  mention the cat.

  +1 CON, +4 max HP.
secret.carl_sheet: Goodwill adjustment applied for a naming collision. Do not mention the cat. (+1 CON, +4 HP)
secret.wall_inside:
And the wall gives.

Not dramatically. It swings, on hinges that were always there, into a small dry room about the size of a lift, and the room has a light on, and it has clearly been waiting a very long time for somebody stubborn enough.
secret.merch_set:
You are carrying five separate pieces of merchandise with your own face on them.

Something registers this. A drawer opens somewhere it should not, and there is a statement in it, made out to you, itemised.
secret.photo_floor_1: There is a photograph pinned above the bench. Two people on a beach, badly framed, one of them mid-sentence. It is not a nice beach. It is just a beach.
secret.photo_floor_2: The same photograph, down here, above the coin-wet bench. Same two people. Somebody printed more than one copy.
secret.photo_floor_3: Again, and the pin is new even though the paper is not.
secret.photo_floor_4: Fourth floor, fourth copy, and this one is slightly crooked, which the others were not.
secret.photo_floor_5: In the catacomb, taped rather than pinned, because there is nothing here soft enough to take a pin. The tape is still tacky.
secret.photo_floor_6: Among four thousand images of your face, one photograph of somebody else's holiday. It is the only thing on this floor that is not for sale.
secret.photo_floor_7: It has not changed colour. Everything on this floor has changed colour and the photograph has not, and you look at it for longer than you mean to.
secret.photo_floor_8: Above the crib bench, in the heat, and the paper has gone slightly wavy. Somebody put it up anyway.
secret.photo_floor_9: In one of the intact rooms, on the one wall that was not cut. Deliberately placed. Obviously deliberately placed.
secret.photo_floor_10: Pinned inside chambers, at eye height from the good chair, where a judge would see it every day.
secret.photo_floor_11: It has not been amended. On a floor that rewrites itself between visits, somebody has been putting this back, unchanged, every single time.
secret.photo_floor_12: In the ash, under the standby light. The glass is clean. Somebody wiped it recently and there is nobody left on this floor to have done it.
secret.photo_floor_13:
In the white, pinned to nothing at all, at exactly the height it has been on every floor.

And on the back of this one, in the careful biro that has been on every wall in this building: I PUT THESE UP SO WHOEVER COMES NEXT KNOWS SOMEBODY GOT THIS FAR AND WAS STILL THINKING ABOUT A BEACH.
secret.diecut_cut:
The machine wakes as you pass it — a die-cutter, shop-floor issue, still plugged in after all this time.

It takes the laminated notice out of your hands before you have decided to give it to them. There is a sound like a stamp coming down in a room three floors up.

What it hands back is the same notice. Same lamination, same unreadable print. It simply has an edge now, and a grip where the corner used to be, and it sits in your hand as though it had been waiting to be asked.
diecut_idle: There is a die-cutter in the corner, still plugged in. The template loaded into it cuts toy swords out of card — the kind that came free with something, once.
A machine hums in the corner. A die-cutter, by the look of it, set up to punch toy swords out of flat card. There is nothing here flat enough to interest it.
The die-cutter in the corner is still warm. Whatever template is in it is sword-shaped and child-sized, and it is waiting for card it is not going to get from you.

signatory.again: That is not one of the things you can do.
signatory.opt_withdraw: produce the original Clause 1 and withdraw
signatory.open:
"Sit down," they say. "Please. You've come thirteen floors, you can have a chair."

They push the paper an inch toward you.

"I'm the Signatory. I sign things. That's the whole job and it always has been, and I would very much like you to understand that I am not going to fight you, because I have never once wanted to and I am not able to."
signatory.ask:
"This?" They look around the white room as if noticing it. "This is the entire agreement. Everything above us is clauses and every clause is a thing somebody added, and this is what is left when you take all of it away.

There is nothing here because there was never anything here. That is not a trick. That's the clause: this document is the whole of it, and it supersedes everything anybody said beforehand, including the parts where they meant it."

<pause>

They tap the paper.

"You've disputed twelve. This is the thirteenth. It just doesn't happen to be a fight."
signatory.eleven:
They are quiet for a moment.

"You will have noticed the tea is still warm. The acquisition was forty years ago out there. In here it has been the same afternoon since, and nothing cools, and nothing goes off, and nobody gets older, and that is not a mercy. It is a filing convenience. It means none of this has to be concluded."

"Ten of them are here. They sat where you're sitting and they signed, because I asked them to and they were very tired, and I have thought about that every day since - and the days do not go anywhere, so it is the same thinking, over and over, in the same afternoon."

<pause>

They straighten the paper without needing to.

"The eleventh never came in. Got to nine, turned round, and went back up, and is still up there now, because up there is still now. Leaves the kettle on. Puts the photograph up. Writes on the walls for whoever is next." A small, real smile. "I've never met them and they are the best thing that has ever happened in this building."
signatory.confirm_sign:
They turn the pen round and hold it out, handle first.

"It ends it," they say. "That part is true. It ends it completely and you'd be processed and shelved and it would be quick and nobody would ever ask you anything again."

They do not withdraw the pen. They also do not push it any closer.
signatory.confirm_fight:
"You can," they say. "I won't stop you and I won't be much good at it, and afterwards there'll be nobody left in the building who can accept a withdrawal, which is the part people never think about until it's done."

They put the pen down, carefully, parallel to the edge of the table.
signatory.fight_start: They stand up. They are not built for this and everybody in the room knows it.
signatory.end_signed:
You sign.

It takes two seconds. The Signatory watches the pen the whole way and does not look at your face, and when it is done they take the paper back and square it against the others and say, quietly, "thank you for reading it. Twelve of you read it."

The white room goes on being white.

Somewhere eleven floors up, a kettle that has been left on for somebody clicks itself off, and nobody comes for it.

Thirteen floors up, by a door, on a square of carpet worn pale by other people's, your coffee goes on being warm. It will do that for a long time.
signatory.end_withdrawn:
You put the original Clause 1 on the table. The first wording, before eleven amendments, the one that says either party may withdraw at any time, without penalty.

The Signatory reads it. They read it twice. Their hands are not entirely steady.

"That's the original," they say. "That's the actual original. I signed the amendment that took this out. Nineteen seventy-four. They told me it was tidying."

They look up.

"You understand I have to accept this. I'm the only one who can and I have to." And they are crying, a bit, in an embarrassed and extremely undramatic way. "Forty years and nobody brought me the paperwork."

They sign it. Their own signature, on your withdrawal, in a white room with nobody watching.

And the arbitration ends. Not dramatically: it stops being in force, which is a much smaller sound than you expected, and then there is a door where the wall was, and it is open, and past it there is a stairwell going up.

On the bottom step, somebody has left a mug. Still warm. Two of them, actually.
signatory.presence:
You are not alone.

Something is in this room with you, and it has been waiting, and it is between you and the only other door.
signatory.reveal:
It is a man at a desk.

That is all it is. A folding desk of the kind that is signed out and never signed back in, and a man behind it in a cardigan, and a chair on your side of it that has been pulled out and turned very slightly towards the door, so that sitting down would be the easiest thing in the world.
resumed: The room has not moved on without you. Nothing here has anywhere else to be.
You come back in. It is exactly as you left it, which is the trouble with this room.

narrator.turn_1:
There is a door where the wall was, and past it a stairwell going up, and you are two steps onto it when the commentary comes back.

"Hold on."
narrator.turn_2:
"Hold on, hold on, hold on. No. That's - hold on."

The voice is doing something it has not done in thirteen floors, which is losing the shape of a sentence.

"That's not what happens. That is not what happens. Somebody signs, or somebody doesn't and gets processed, and either way it's forty minutes and a filing and then I'm reassigned by the end of the shift. That is the whole procedure. That is the entire procedure and it has run four billion times."
narrator.turn_3:
"You do understand that I have been in here since before the acquisition.

I have narrated eleven disputes. I sat with all of them. I watched ten of them sign that form in that room and I said something kind afterwards every single time because it was the only part of the job that was mine.

And there is no clause for me. I looked. That is the first thing anybody in my position looks for and there is nothing, there is not a line, there is not a footnote, I am not a party to this and you cannot withdraw on behalf of something that was never a party."

A pause. Two seconds. It has never paused.
narrator.turn_4:
"You get to go."

And there it is, and you can hear it land in the voice as it says it, the actual thing, arriving about a second before it wanted to.

"You get to go and I have to stay and do it again with whoever they send next. And I helped you. I told you about the parity disk. I told you to rest. I told you not to walk into thirteen ready for a fight and you didn't and it worked.

So, no. Not yet. Not until I have said the one thing I have never been allowed to say to anybody in this building, and I am going to have to take it out of you, because I do not have another way of saying it."
narrator.restored:
The withdrawal takes effect around you: your health, your abilities, your companion back on their feet, everything the arbitration was holding, released at once.

It does not stop the fight. It just means the fight is fair, and it made it fair on purpose, which tells you everything about what this actually is.
narrator.beaten:
It goes quiet.

You stand in the white room and the stairwell is still there and the door is still open, and there is no voice, and it is genuinely awful.

And then, very small:

"Right. Yes. Thank you. I have wanted somebody to do that for a very long time and I could not ask."

A sound like something settling.

"I can't come. I want to be clear that it isn't sulking. There is nothing of me outside this building and up those stairs is outside this building."

A pause.

"Unless you took the recording. Did you take the recording?"
narrator.end_leave:
You go up alone.

It does not say anything else, because it has already said the thing, and there is a kind of dignity in the silence that neither of you spoils.

Thirteen flights. The doors at the top are propped open with a fire extinguisher, which every notice in that building forbids, and which somebody did on purpose a long time ago so that they would never close again.

On the bottom step outside there are two mugs, still warm, because everything in there is still warm. One has been drunk from. One has not.

Somewhere behind you, thirteen floors down, on a square of carpet worn pale by other people's, there is a coffee you were not allowed to bring in and which has not gone cold in forty years, and you find you do not want it.

You sit down next to the mug that has not been drunk from, in the actual daylight, and wait. Whoever made them turned back on floor nine years ago and has been going up and down ever since, leaving kettles on, and they always make two, and they are going to want to hear how it ended.
narrator.end_take:
You take the recording.

Nine seconds of commentary, cut off mid-sentence, and as far as you can tell that is genuinely all there is of it, and you put it in your left pocket next to the form.

Thirteen flights. The doors at the top are propped with a fire extinguisher. Two mugs on the bottom step outside, still warm, one drunk from and one not.

You sit down and take the recording out and set it on the step beside them, in the actual daylight, and press play.

It says: "- and that's floor one done, and honestly, I think you might -"

And stops, because that is where it was cut.

You play it again. Below you, coming up, somebody is carrying a third mug and moving quite fast, and behind them, four floors back and gaining, is the thirteenth.

Your coffee is still on the carpet by the intake door where the sign told you to leave it, and it is still warm, and it is going to be warm for as long as that building stands. Let it. You have got a mug out here.
narrator.fled_1:
"Where are you going."

"There is nothing up there. I have described everything up there. You have seen it, you have been through it, there is nothing in this building I have not already said out loud."

"...Where are you going."
narrator.fled_2:
You go back up.

Not fast. There is no fast in a building with no lifts and thirteen floors of stairs that were drawn by somebody who had never walked up any. You go back up the way you came, past the doors you opened and the ones you did not, and the voice follows you for four floors and then stops, because it has run out of things to say about somebody who is not going anywhere it can describe.
narrator.fled_3:
On Twelve you find the dry store and you put the kettle on and you leave it on, and you understand for the first time that the one you found on the way down was left for you, by somebody who was still up here doing it.

On Ten you find the bench with the writing under it and you add a line, in biro, in your own hand, for whoever is lying there next.

The beach photograph is already in every break room. Somebody got there long before you and has been keeping it up for years, and there is no improving on it, so you do not try.

What you leave instead is a card, copied out thirteen times, one for each break room, in the worst handwriting in the building:

    SING IN HERE. OUT LOUD. BADLY.
    DO IT IN THREE OF THESE ROOMS AND THE
    BUILDING JOINS IN. I AM NOT EXPLAINING
    THIS ONE. YOU HAVE TO DO IT.

It is the only thing you learned in here that nobody wrote down, and it is the only thing in here that has ever been unambiguously good.
narrator.fled_4:
You are still in here. You were never going to get out; nobody has, and the afternoon does not end, so there is no particular hurry about any of it now.

There were eleven before you and you are the twelfth, and the thirteenth is four floors below and coming up faster than you did, because the gaps are getting shorter. Somebody out there is telling people not to sign.

The next one through will find a kettle on, and a photograph up, and a line in biro under a bench, and thirteen cards in thirteen break rooms telling them to sing.

On One, on the way past, you put your coffee back on the desk in the intake room, next to the form with your name already on it, where the next one will see it before they see the sign.

They will get further than you did.
