That is the point. That was always the point.

r01.name: Ash Landing
r01.desc: A landing under a slow fall of grey. A door south.
r01.long:
The stairs come out into falling ash.

It is coming down steadily from somewhere above and it has been coming down long enough to have drifted against the walls, and when you look closely it is not ash. It is paper, burnt to nothing, still holding the shape of the type.

On the wall, a printed notice, curling: THIS FACILITY WILL CLOSE. The date has been crossed out and rewritten eleven times.

r02.name: Shutdown Junction
r02.desc: Four ways, all of them powering down. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
The lights here are on a sequence: they come up as you enter and go off behind you and stay off.

Something is turning this building off one room at a time and it is doing it in the order people leave.

r03.name: Cleared Desks
r03.desc: An office with everything taken. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
Forty desks, all cleared, all wiped, all with a cardboard box beside them that has not been collected.

Every box has a name on it. The boxes are full. Nobody came back for any of them.

r04.name: Server Ash
r04.desc: Where the racks were. Doors east.
r04.long:
The racks from Clause 5 ended up here after termination, stripped and stacked and burnt.

Something survived the burn in the bottom of the pile.

r05.name: Handover Room
r05.desc: A room set up for a handover that did not happen. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
Two chairs facing each other, a table, and a folder in the middle marked HANDOVER.

The folder is empty. Both chairs have been sat in, recently, at the same time. You cannot make that work with anything else you know.

r06.name: Emergency Lighting
r06.desc: A corridor lit only by the green boxes. Doors west, east and south.
r06.long:
Main power has gone here and the emergency lighting has taken over: green, low, and rated for three hours.

It has been running for eleven years.

r07.name: Exit Route
r07.desc: A corridor of green running men. Doors west and south.
r07.long:
Every few feet, a sign with a running figure and an arrow.

The arrows point in both directions along the corridor. You follow one set for a while and it turns you round and sends you back, politely, at a comfortable pace.

r08.name: Cold Plant
r08.desc: The heating, off. Doors east and south.
r08.long:
The plant room, and the boilers are cold for the first time since the building was built.

There is frost on the inside of the pipework, which should not be possible on this timescale, and the frost has been disturbed by a hand.

r09.name: Records Ash
r09.desc: Drifts of what the Reaper has been eating. Doors north, east and south.
r09.long:
Ash to your knees, and here it is thick enough to wade.

Every so often something in it is only half burnt and you can read a line: a name, a date, a decision. You stop reading them after the fourth.

r10.name: Standby Room
r10.desc: A room still on standby power, and warm. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r10.long:
A small room on the standby circuit: a light, a socket, a kettle, and a bench.

The standby circuit predates the contract, which is why it is still on and why nothing comes in here.

The kettle is warm. Of course it is warm.

r11.name: Terminal Corridor
r11.desc: A corridor with the terminals dark. Doors north, west, east and south.
r11.long:
Wall-mounted terminals every ten feet, all dark except one, which shows a login prompt and a cursor.

You type nothing. The cursor blinks for a while and then, very politely, the screen goes off.

r12.name: The Last Meeting
r12.desc: A room where a decision was taken. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
A meeting room with the chairs still pulled out and a whiteboard that has been wiped except for one word in the corner: PROCEED.

Under it, in a different hand, much smaller: under protest.

r13.name: Packing Up
r13.desc: A corner where somebody is packing. Doors north and south.
r13.long:
He is packing up.

Not hurriedly. The stock goes into the bag in an order that has clearly been worked out over decades, and the lamp goes on top, and the flask goes in the side pocket.

"Twelve floors," he says, without looking up. "You'll want to buy now. There's nothing left downstairs and I mean that in the specific rather than the commercial sense."

r14.name: Fire Door
r14.desc: A heavy door, propped. Doors east and south.
r14.long:
A fire door, propped open with an extinguisher, which every notice in this building forbids.

Somebody propped it and then somebody else did not close it, and it has been propped ever since, and the whole floor is warmer for it.

r15.name: Redundancy
r15.desc: Where the notices were served. Doors north, east and south.
r15.long:
A room with a desk, two chairs, and a box of tissues that is empty.

On the desk, a stack of identical letters, unsigned, waiting for a name to be typed in. Four hundred of them.

r16.name: Ash Hall
r16.desc: A wide room half full of drift. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
The largest room on the floor and the ash has drifted across it in dunes.

Something very large has been through here recently. The drift is pushed aside in a channel eight feet wide and the edges of the channel are scorched.

r17.name: The Noticeboard
r17.desc: A wall of final notices. Doors north, west, east and south.
r17.long:
A noticeboard sixty feet long, and every notice on it is final.

Final reminder. Final demand. Final notice. Final, final notice. They go back four decades and the last one is dated today, and it has your name on it, and it is the only one that has been delivered by hand.

r18.name: Stopped Clocks
r18.desc: A corridor of clocks. Doors north, west, east and south.
r18.long:
Every clock in this corridor has stopped, and they have all stopped at different times, and none of them is the time now.

The last one to stop is still warm at the movement.

r19.name: Last Post
r19.desc: A pigeonhole wall, mostly empty. Doors north, west and south.
r19.long:
Four hundred pigeonholes and eleven of them still have post in them.

You check. They are all addressed to disputants. Ten have been opened. One has not.

r20.name: Salvage Store
r20.desc: What somebody has been saving. Doors east and south.
r20.long:
Crates, packed and labelled, of things that will still work after the power goes: hand tools, a stove, a wind-up torch, water.

It is a going-away kit and it is not big enough for one person to be planning to stay.
r20.chest_hint: There is a crate here, packed and labelled.

r21.name: Wound-Down Plant
r21.desc: Machinery running on the last of it. Doors north, east and south.
r21.long:
Enormous machinery, unmaintained since the acquisition, still turning over on whatever momentum it has left.

It is going to stop. Not today. You can hear that it is going to stop.

r22.name: Ash Crossing
r22.desc: A narrow way through the drift. Doors north, west, east and south.
r22.long: Somebody has cut a path through the deepest drift with a shovel, and left the shovel at the far end, upright, handle out, for whoever needs it next.

r23.name: Terminated Accounts
r23.desc: Rows of closed files. Doors north, west, east and south.
r23.long:
Every account this building ever held, closed, filed, and stamped TERMINATED.

The stamp is enormous and it is on the desk and the pad is dry. Yours is in here somewhere and it is not stamped.

r24.name: Cold Aisle, Dead
r24.desc: The catacomb air-handling, off. Doors north, west, east and south.
r24.long: The plant that kept Clause 5 cold, shut down. The air is completely still, which after eleven floors of moving air is the loudest thing that has happened all day.

r25.name: Liquidation
r25.desc: Where the value was realised. Doors north and west.
r25.long:
Everything of value in the building, catalogued and lotted, with a number on a card beside each item.

The lots include desks, plant, fittings, and, at lot 909, an entry that reads DISPUTANTS (11), CONDITION VARIABLE.

Something is walking the rows with a clipboard, checking the numbers against the list.
r25.chest_hint: There is a strongbox in lot 400.

r26.name: Deep Ash
r26.desc: Ash to the waist. Doors east and south.
r26.long:
It is up to your waist here and moving through it is like wading in warm snow.

Under the surface your boot finds things that are not ash: a chair leg, a keyboard, once, briefly, something that grips back and then lets go.

r27.name: Powered Down
r27.desc: A room with nothing running at all. Doors north, east and south.
r27.long:
No lights, no plant, no standby, nothing. You are working by the green glow leaking in from the corridor.

This room is finished. It has been terminated and it is what the whole building is going to be.

r28.name: Second Standby
r28.desc: Another room on the old circuit. Warm, lit, safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r28.long:
The other standby room, and the kettle in this one has just boiled.

Just. The steam is still on the window.

You missed them by less than a minute and you go and stand in the doorway and look down the corridor for a while, and there is nothing but ash and green light and no footprints, because the ash has been falling the whole time.

r29.name: Ash Junction
r29.desc: Four ways, all grey. Doors north, west, east and south.
r29.long: A junction under the fall. All four corridors look identical, all four are ankle deep, and the ash has smoothed over every track anyone has made in the last hour.

r30.name: Shredding
r30.desc: Where the records went first. Doors north, west, east and south.
r30.long:
Industrial shredders, forty of them, hoppers empty, blades stopped.

They did the first pass. Then something decided shredding was too slow and began eating instead.

r31.name: Last Office
r31.desc: One office still occupied. Doors north, west and south.
r31.long:
One office on the whole floor still has a desk lamp on and a chair pushed in and a coat on the back of the door.

The coat is yours. Not like yours. Yours, the one from Intake, with the thing in the left pocket you have been carrying since the first floor.

You check your left pocket. It is still there.

r32.name: The Kit Room
r32.desc: Where somebody prepared. Doors east and south.
r32.long:
A small room, thoroughly organised, that somebody has been provisioning for a long time.

A route drawn on the wall in marker, floor by floor, thirteen down and thirteen back up. Ticks against one through twelve. Nothing against thirteen.

And a crate, packed for two people.
r32.chest_hint: There is a crate here, packed for two.

r33.name: Ash Gallery
r33.desc: A long room under the fall. Doors north, east and south.
r33.long:
The ceiling is gone in here and the ash comes down properly, thick, silent, endless.

It is, unexpectedly, beautiful. You stand in it longer than the situation warrants and nothing at all attacks you, and afterwards you cannot decide whether that was a mercy or an oversight.

r34.name: Dry Store
r34.desc: The one room on this floor where it is not raining.
r34.long:
The ceiling here was sealed properly, once, by somebody who cared, and it has held. It is the only dry room on the floor and you can hear the weather going on without you, three feet above your head.

There are towels. There is a heater. There is a hand-lettered sign reading TAKE YOUR TIME, THE STORM IS SALARIED. Whatever was behind you stops at the door.

r35.name: Approach, Grey
r35.desc: A wide way sloping down. Doors north, west, east and south.
r35.long:
The floor slopes and the ash slides with it, and everything on this floor has been slowly migrating toward the doors at the bottom for eleven years.

The drift against those doors is six feet deep and something has pushed through it from the inside.

r36.name: The Hoard Edge
r36.desc: Where the drift becomes something else. Doors north, west and east.
r36.long:
The ash stops being ash here and starts being pages: whole ones, unburnt, packed flat by weight into a floor you can walk on.

It is a hoard. You are already standing on the edge of it.

r37.name: Merchandise, Last
r37.desc: A display, still stocked. Doors west.
r37.long:
A merchandise display, upright, dusted, fully stocked, in a room where everything else has been burnt or taken.

Somebody has been dusting it. That is the detail that finishes you. Eleven years of termination and somebody has been coming in here and dusting the mugs with your face on them.
r37.item_hint: There is merchandise here, immaculately dusted.

r38.name: The Last Warm Room
r38.desc: A room on standby, and a bench. Safe. Doors north and south.
r38.long:
The last warm room in the building.

Bench, kettle, light. And on the bench, laid out deliberately: a full flask, a folded blanket, and a note.

It says: I CAN'T DO THIRTEEN. I GET TO THE DOOR AND I CAN'T. TWELVE TIMES NOW. TAKE THE FLASK. IF YOU GET THROUGH IT, COME BACK UP AND TELL ME WHAT'S IN THERE. I'LL BE ON NINE. I'M ALWAYS ON NINE.

r39.name: The Records Hoard
r39.desc: A vast room floored in paper, with a dragon on it. One door north.
r39.long:
The room is the size of the whole floor and it is floored, six feet deep, in records.

Every file this building ever kept, every form, every claim, every excluded box from Clause 10 and every rejected claim from Clause 3, packed flat under its own weight into a hoard, and lying on top of it with its head on its claws is the Reaper of Records.

It is an actual dragon. Grey, enormous, older than the acquisition, with wings that are pages and a body that is index cards, and it opens one eye as you come in and the eye is a very small, very neat rectangle of type.

"AH," it says, and ash comes off it in a wave. "THE ONE THAT READ IT."

r01.name: The White
r01.desc: A white space with a way on. A door south.
r01.long:
The stairs stop and there is no doorway at the bottom, only white.

The room is white. The floor is white and the walls are white and where the ceiling should be there is more white, further away than a ceiling has any business being.

There is no ash here, no signage, no fittings, no smell. After twelve floors of a building insisting on itself, the absence is almost rude.

Somewhere ahead, a very long way, there is a single dark shape that might be a door.

r02.name: White Junction
r02.desc: Four ways through nothing. Doors north, west, east and south.
r02.long:
A junction, in the sense that there are four ways to go. There is nothing marking it as a junction and nothing marking the ways.

You work out afterwards that you knew which way you had come from the whole time, and you cannot say how.

r03.name: Superseded
r03.desc: A room holding what does not count. Doors east, west and south.
r03.long:
The only thing in this white room is a low pile of documents in the middle of the floor.

Every one of them is a thing somebody was told before they signed. Promises, assurances, an actual handshake photographed. All of it superseded by the agreement and therefore, formally, not real.

You can pick them up. They feel like paper. They are not evidence of anything.

r04.name: Four Corners
r04.desc: A room that is only its own boundary. Doors east.
r04.long:
The room is defined by four corners and nothing else: no walls between them, no ceiling above them, just four right angles hanging in the white at the distance walls would be.

Nothing outside the four corners forms part of this agreement. You are inside them. That is the only thing that is currently true about you.

r05.name: Recitals
r05.desc: A room of things that were agreed beforehand. Doors west, east and south.
r05.long:
The recitals: WHEREAS the parties wish to, WHEREAS it is intended that, WHEREAS in consideration of.

They are printed on the white in white and you can only read them at an angle. They are all quite reasonable. None of them is operative.

r06.name: Definitions
r06.desc: A room where words mean what they are told to. Doors west, east and south.
r06.long:
A list, floor to nothing, of defined terms.

'Disputant' means you. 'Arbitration' means this. 'Reasonable' means whatever we say. 'Withdraw' has no entry at all; there is a gap in the alphabetical order where it should be, and the gap has been left deliberately and neatly.

r07.name: Severance, White
r07.desc: A corner where the floor stops. Doors west and south.
r07.long:
The floor ends in the clean plane you last saw on Clause 9, except here there is nothing on the other side of it to see.

You throw something in. It does not land.

r08.name: Boilerplate Row
r08.desc: Standard wording, at length. Doors east and south.
r08.long:
Paragraphs and paragraphs of it, in perfect type, saying nothing that could not be said in a sentence.

Somebody has been through with a pen and put a small tick beside about one line in forty. Those lines, read together, say something quite different.

r09.name: The Blank Room
r09.desc: A room with nothing in it at all. Doors north, east and south.
r09.long:
Nothing. Not white-with-features: nothing.

You stand in it for a while to be sure, and you are sure, and it is the first genuinely empty space in the building and you find you are grateful to it.

r10.name: White Bench
r10.desc: A bench in the white, and a kettle beside it. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r10.long:
There is a bench here.

No room around it, no walls: just a bench, in the white, with a kettle on the floor beside it plugged into nothing, and it is warm.

Above the bench, pinned to the air at exactly the height it has been pinned in every safe room in this building, is the photograph of the beach.

r11.name: Prior Understandings
r11.desc: A room full of what people thought. Doors north, west, east and south.
r11.long:
What everybody believed the deal was, exhibited: four billion versions, most of them broadly the same, all of them wrong in the same specific way.

Yours is here. It is very close to correct. It is not correct.

r12.name: No Amendments
r12.desc: A room that cannot change. Doors north, west, east and south.
r12.long:
After Clause 11 this room is unnerving in the other direction: it is exactly the same as it was when you walked in and it will be exactly the same when you leave.

You go back and check twice. It is fine. That is the problem.

r13.name: The Last Pitch
r13.desc: A table set up in nothing. Doors north and south.
r13.long:
He has set up in the white.

No overhang, no corner, no shelter, because there is nothing here to shelter from and nothing to set up against. Just the folding table, the lamp, the flask, and the stock, standing in an infinite white room with no customers.

"I know," he says. "I do know. But I've done every floor for forty years and I wasn't going to skip the last one."

r14.name: Entire
r14.desc: A room containing the whole document. Doors east and south.
r14.long:
The agreement, in full, at actual size: every clause, every schedule, every appendix, laid flat across the floor of a room with no visible end.

You walk on it for eleven minutes and reach Clause 4.

r15.name: White Corridor
r15.desc: A corridor by convention only. Doors north, east and south.
r15.long:
It is a corridor because it is longer than it is wide, and it is longer than it is wide because you are walking down it.

When you look back it is a different shape and you decide not to make an issue of it.

r16.name: Construction
r16.desc: A room about how to read it. Doors north, west, east and south.
r16.long:
The rules of construction: headings are for convenience only, the singular includes the plural, and any ambiguity shall be resolved against the party that drafted it.

That last one is written smaller than the others. It has been written smaller deliberately, and it is the single most useful sentence in the entire agreement, and it has been sitting on the last floor for forty years where nobody would reach it.

r17.name: The Reading
r17.desc: A room where the agreement is being read aloud. Doors north, west, east and south.
r17.long:
Somebody is reading the agreement out. All of it, from the beginning, at a measured pace, in a clear voice with no emotion in it whatsoever.

They are on page nine hundred and something. They began, by your reckoning, several years ago.

They do not stop when you come in. They do turn slightly toward you, which is worse.

r18.name: Counterparts
r18.desc: A room of identical copies. Doors north, west, east and south.
r18.long:
This agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original.

There are four billion counterparts in here and they are all originals and they are all identical and they are stacked in a column that goes up past where the ceiling isn't.

r19.name: Notices
r19.desc: How they were to reach you. Doors north, west and south.
r19.long:
The notices clause, rendered: a single letterbox mounted in the white, at head height, with nothing behind it.

All notices shall be deemed served when posted. Nothing was ever posted. Everything has been deemed served.

r20.name: Waiver
r20.desc: A room about what they let you get away with. Doors east and south.
r20.long:
No failure to enforce shall constitute a waiver.

Everything they let you do on the way down is in this room, filed, with a note beside each entry confirming it does not count as permission and can be enforced retrospectively at any time.

The list is very long. You had not realised how much you had got away with.
r20.chest_hint: There is a case at the end of the list.

r21.name: White Junction, Lower
r21.desc: Four more ways through nothing. Doors north, east and south.
r21.long:
Another junction. You have started leaving things on the floor to mark them, small things, a laminate, a screw.

They are still there when you come back. It is the only navigational aid on this floor and you invented it.

r22.name: Assignment
r22.desc: A room about who owns you now. Doors north, west, east and south.
r22.long:
We may assign our rights under this agreement without notice to you.

A chart on the white shows the chain: the original party, then an acquisition, then another, then a shell, then Vantablack Holdings LLC, then, at the bottom, an arrow pointing to a box that is empty.

The empty box is current. Whoever owns this now, there is nobody in it.
r22.chest_hint: There is a case beneath the chart.

r23.name: Force
r23.desc: A room about what still applies. Doors north, west, east and south.
r23.long:
Twelve clauses, listed, each with a status beside it.

Eleven say DISPUTED. One says DISPUTED, pending. The pending one is Clause 12, and while you watch it changes to DISPUTED and the whole list is complete.

Underneath, a thirteenth line, blank.

r24.name: Interpretation
r24.desc: A room where meaning is decided. Doors north, west, east and south.
r24.long:
A bench, a lectern, and a scale, and on the scale, two identical readings of the same sentence, balanced exactly.

One of them means you can leave. Nobody has ever been here to tip it.

r25.name: The Whole Thing
r25.desc: A room containing the agreement, animate. Doors north and west.
r25.long:
Everything you have fought is in this room at once, not as monsters but as clauses, layered, complete, in force.

And it stands up when you come in, all thirteen of it, and it is the last thing in this building that is going to try.
r25.chest_hint: There is a strongbox behind it.

r26.name: Nothing Follows
r26.desc: A room after the end of the text. Doors east and south.
r26.long:
This room is after the signature block.

There is nothing here because there is nothing after the signature block, and being in it feels like standing in a margin.

r27.name: White Approach
r27.desc: A long white way. Doors north, east and south.
r27.long: It goes on. You walk it. It stops going on when you have walked far enough, which is not the same as it having an end.

r28.name: Second Bench
r28.desc: Another bench, another kettle. Safe. Doors north, west, east and south.
r28.long:
The second bench.

The kettle is warm, the photograph is up, and there are two mugs, and both have been used, and there is a third one out and clean and waiting.

They have started setting a place for you.

r29.name: Consideration
r29.desc: A room about what you got. Doors north, west, east and south.
r29.long:
What was given in exchange, exhibited: a discount meal-kit subscription, twelve weeks, first box half price.

It is on a plinth, under a light, correctly labelled, and it is the entire consideration for everything that has happened to you.

In the case beside it, on smaller plinths, are the things that were asked for: an option on your immortal soul, exercisable within five working days; a thousand hours of community service, unclaimed; your first child, listed as an asset and marked JOKE - DO NOT REMOVE; and an undertaking not to operate nuclear facilities with a music player.

Every one of them is initialled. Every one of them is yours. You did tick the box.

r30.name: Termination, Aftermath
r30.desc: A room after the last floor. Doors north, west, east and south.
r30.long:
You can see Clause 12 from here, sort of: a grey smear at the edge of the white, several miles down and to the left, still falling.

It is finished. It finished while you were walking.

r31.name: Execution
r31.desc: Where it was signed. Doors north, west and south.
r31.long:
The signature block, at scale: two lines, one signed, one not.

The signed one is a small neat hand that you have seen at the bottom of every notice in this building. The unsigned one has four billion names on it, printed, in six point, going down past the floor.

Yours is on it. It is printed, not signed. Nobody ever signed it. It did not need signing; it was accepted.

r32.name: The Cupboard
r32.desc: A cupboard, in nothing, with a door. Doors east and south.
r32.long:
On a floor with no walls, somebody has built a cupboard.

Freestanding, plywood, badly made, with a door that shuts properly and a hook and eye on the inside. It is the only ugly object on Clause 13 and it is the only one anybody made with their hands.

Inside: a chair, a light, a flask, and a wall of tally marks that stops.
r32.chest_hint: There is a box under the chair.

r33.name: Governing, Absent
r33.desc: A room with nothing presiding. Doors north, east and south.
r33.long:
The court from Clause 10 should reach here and does not. There is no jurisdiction in this room, no forum, no venue, and nothing that could hear a matter.

It is the safest place in the building and it is completely useless.

r34.name: Recess
r34.desc: White, quiet, and with two chairs facing each other.
r34.long:
The room is white like the rest of this floor, but somebody has put two chairs in it facing each other, and a low table between them, and on the table a pot of tea that is still warm.

Nobody is here. Nobody has been for some time. The arrangement has been kept up anyway, which on this floor amounts to a kindness. Nothing follows you in.

r35.name: Miscellaneous
r35.desc: The clauses nobody negotiates. Doors north, west, east and south.
r35.long:
Headings, counterparts, severability, notices, waiver, assignment, entire agreement.

The boring end of every contract ever written, and between them they have done more damage to more people than any of the clauses upstairs, and none of them was ever read by anybody.

r36.name: The Long White
r36.desc: A room that is only distance. Doors north, west and east.
r36.long:
There is nothing in this room but the far side of it, and the far side is a long way, and getting there takes the amount of time it takes.

You spend it thinking about the beach in the photograph, which you have never been to.

r37.name: Merchandise, White
r37.desc: One display, in nothing. Doors west.
r37.long:
A merchandise display stand, freestanding, in the white, fully stocked, lit from nowhere.

It is the last one. There is a small card on it, handwritten, not printed: LAST ONE. TAKE IT IF YOU WANT IT. IT'S YOUR FACE.
r37.item_hint: There is one last piece of merchandise here.

r38.name: The Eleven Benches
r38.desc: A row of benches in the white. Doors north and east.
r38.long:
Eleven benches, in a row, facing a door.

Ten of them have been sat on: the white is worn where people sat, and beside each worn patch there is a small pile of belongings, folded, tidy, left.

The eleventh bench is not worn. There is nothing beside it. It has been waiting a very long time and nobody has ever sat on it, and you understand, with complete clarity, that it is for the one who gets to nine and turns round and goes back up, and that they are never going to use it.

There is no twelfth bench. Nobody ordered a twelfth bench. Whatever the building expected, it did not expect you, and it has not expected anybody since nineteen seventy-four.

r39.name: Outside The Door
r39.desc: A bench, a kettle, and a door. Safe. Doors north and south.
r39.long:
The last safe room, and it is a bench in front of a door.

Kettle warm, photograph up, three mugs out. And a flask, full, with a note under it:

I'M NOT COMING IN. I'VE TRIED. WHATEVER THEY SAY IN THERE, THE ANSWER IS IN YOUR LEFT POCKET AND IT HAS BEEN SINCE INTAKE.

You check your left pocket. The form from the desk on Clause 1 is still in it, folded, with DISPUTE ticked in your own handwriting, which you never did.

r40.name: Entire Agreement
r40.desc: A white room with a table, two chairs, and one person. One door north.
r40.long:
A table. Two chairs. One of them occupied.

That is all there is on Clause 13, and it is all there has ever been, and everything above it was built to stop anybody arriving here.

standing.2: Something in the building notices that you are still going. It is only a flicker of attention. It is the first you have had.
standing.3: You have stopped flinching at the signage. That is not nothing; most people never get that far.
standing.4: Your file has been moved to a different shelf. You have no way of knowing this and it is true.
standing.5: Somebody upstairs has started using your name instead of your case number.
standing.6: The Enforcement Entities have begun to be briefed about you specifically, rather than about disputants in general.
standing.7: You are no longer an irregularity. You are a matter. Matters get resourced.
standing.8: Two floors below, something has been told to expect you and has asked, apparently, what you are like.
standing.9: The stream has picked you up properly. There is an audience now, in three galaxies, and none of them are on your side and all of them are watching.
standing.10: Merchandise bearing your face has entered a second print run. You will find some of it. You will not be paid for it.
standing.11: You have outlasted the point where anyone below you was told to plan for. Everything from here is being improvised, including you.
standing.12: There is a version of this building's procedure that has your name written into it as a defined term. It is very recent.
standing.13: Ten disputants signed. One turned back. You are the twelfth and the only one still moving.
standing.14: Something has begun to remove obstacles from your path in order to see what you do next. This is not help.
standing.15: The clauses beneath you have started to reinforce each other, which they are not supposed to need to do.
standing.16: You are being cited. Not in the record: by the things down here, to each other, as a warning.
standing.17: The arbitration has stopped treating you as a party to it and started treating you as a fault in it.
standing.18: Whatever is left below knows exactly what you are and has decided, on balance, to be somewhere else.
standing.19: There is nothing in the building that has not now heard of you. It is a quieter feeling than you expected.
standing.20: Your grade no longer appears on the printed scale. Someone has written it in the margin, in pen, and initialled it.
standing.21: A subcommittee has been convened to determine what you are. It has met twice. It has not agreed.
standing.22: The building has started rounding you up. Doors that used to want a reason now simply open and hope for the best.
standing.23: You have been issued a lanyard nobody can account for. It opens everything. It appears on no inventory.
standing.24: The floors below have begun describing you to one another in the past tense, which is either respect or wishful thinking.
standing.25: There is no rank above this. The document does not contemplate anyone reaching it, which means, technically, that you are now unaccounted for.

notes.f5_n1:
Biro, on the wall beside a niche:

"IF YOU ARE READING THIS ON YOUR BREAK, THE BREAK ENDED IN 1987. NOBODY TOLD ME EITHER."
notes.f5_n2:
A laminated card, screwed to the stone:

COLD STORE - OCCUPANTS ARE NOT DECEASED FOR THE PURPOSES OF SCHEDULE 4 AND SHOULD NOT BE ADDRESSED AS SUCH.
notes.f5_n3:
Pencil, very small, at ankle height:

"they can hear you. they are just extremely polite.

the one with the cup counts his own five and guesses yours high, every time, and he would rather raise than call. let him climb. when the number he is claiming is more than there are dice on the table, call him."
notes.f6_n1:
A memo, pinned through the plaster with a compass point:

"Reminder that the lift is not out of order. The lift is out of scope. These are different and only one of them is being fixed."
notes.f6_n2:
Marker pen, above a door:

"SEVENTEEN OF US WENT IN. THAT IS NOT A WARNING, IT IS AN ATTENDANCE FIGURE. IT WAS A GOOD DAY."
notes.f6_n3:
A payslip, folded into eighths, damp, with writing on the back:

Gross: 1 paperclip. Deductions: 0. Net: 1 paperclip.

"spent it at the card table. she draws to sixteen and stops on seventeen, always, she told me so herself and she was not lying, she just did not think it would help me. it did not."
notes.f7_n1:
Four colours of chalk, which on this floor is a statement:

"IT CAME BACK ON A TUESDAY AND NOBODY HAS EXPLAINED IT. I DO NOT WANT IT EXPLAINED. I WANT IT TO STAY."
notes.f7_n2:
A postcard, taped up, the picture faded to nothing:

"Wish you were here. There is no here. Still wish it."
notes.f7_n3:
Biro on a fire door:

"if you can see this in colour you have got further than maintenance and maintenance had a van"
notes.f8_n1:
Scratched into a cooling plate with something harder than it:

"THE FOUNDRY DOES NOT MAKE ANYTHING. ASK WHAT IT IS FOR. GO ON. ASK."
notes.f8_n2:
A safety notice, half burned, the surviving half legible:

...AND IN THE EVENT OF FIRE, CONTINUE. THE BUILDING HAS ASSESSED THE RISK AND FOUND IT ACCEPTABLE. TO THE BUILDING.
notes.f8_n3:
Biro, shaky, on the inside of a locker door, under four hundred tally marks:

"day 400. still hot. still here. still ours. foreman still cannot be beaten at the grid and i have stopped trying to be clever about it. one, eight, seven, nine. in that order, every time. she has never once played it differently and i do not think she can."
notes.f9_n1:
Chalk, on one side of a break that goes down further than light:

"THE OTHER HALF OF THIS SENTENCE IS ON THE OTHER HALF OF THIS FLOOR AND I CANNOT GET TO IT ANY MOR"
notes.f9_n2:
A compliment slip, from an office that no longer joins this one:

"With the compliments of Floor 9 (East). Please return to Floor 9 (East). We would like it back."

Underneath, in biro: "there is a way over. it is not a bridge and you do not walk across it. the small room at the top of the west run has a floor that is not a floor. mind the drop, it is shorter than it looks."
notes.f9_n3:
Pencil, on a wall that used to be a floor:

"severance was a verb here first. remember that when they put it on your letter."
notes.f10_n1:
A hearing notice, pinned at head height, the date left blank:

YOUR MATTER WILL BE CALLED. PLEASE REMAIN AVAILABLE. Under it, in biro: "eleven years. still available."
notes.f10_n2:
Biro on the underside of a bench, only readable lying down:

"they list everything. that is the whole trick. make them list something they do not want written down.

the things they hand you at the end of a hearing do not go in your bag and they cannot be taken off you. that is the only property in this building that works like that."
notes.f10_n3:
A docket, stamped ADJOURNED nine times, the tenth stamp half struck:

Handwritten in the margin: "nearly. nearly. nearly."
notes.f11_n1:
A style guide, page torn out and taped to the wall:

"Do not use 'shall'. Do not use 'will'. Do not use 'may'. Rule 4 has been amended and is now Rule 4."
notes.f11_n2:
Blue pencil, corrected twice, each correction corrected:

"the draft is not the agreement" "the draft is the agreement" "the draft is not the agreement"
notes.f11_n3:
A note in an even hand, taped over another note:

"Whoever keeps amending my sign: I admire it, I recognise it, and I am going to keep putting it back."
notes.f12_n1:
A weather log, pulped, one legible column:

MON - indoors, raining. TUE - indoors, raining. WED - indoors, raining. THU - dry. INVESTIGATE. FRI - indoors, raining.
notes.f12_n2:
Marker, running in the wet, on a stairwell wall:

"IT IS NOT A LEAK. WE CHECKED. THERE IS NOTHING ABOVE US TO LEAK. IT IS JUST WEATHER AND IT IS INSIDE."
notes.f12_n3:
A laminated sheet, the only dry thing on the floor:

UMBRELLAS ARE NOT PROVIDED. UMBRELLAS ARE NOT PERMITTED. THE POSITION ON UMBRELLAS IS UNDER REVIEW.

Taped below it, handwritten: "the break rooms still work down here and nothing follows you into one. use them. i did not, for a long time, out of pride."
notes.f13_n1:
Pencil on white wall, the only mark in the room:

"i typed for a year onto nothing and i can still recite it. that is what they could not take. try it."
notes.f13_n2:
A single sheet, blank, with one line at the very bottom:

"Everything above this line has been agreed."
notes.f13_n3:
Scratched, small, beside a door that goes further down:

"THIRTEEN IS NOT THE LAST ONE. THIRTEEN IS THE LAST ONE THEY WROTE DOWN."
notes.f1_n1:
Biro on the back of an induction leaflet, left on a chair:

"nobody who works here has ever had a locker, a drawer or a payslip they trusted, so everything gets hidden and then everybody leaves.

i have stopped walking through empty rooms. i stop and have a proper look round instead. i am up about four hundred clips on it and i have been here eleven weeks."
notes.f1_n2:
Marker pen at knee height, beside a doorway, with a boot mark under it:

"THE WALLS ARE NOT ALL WALLS. THE BUILDING PUT THEM UP IN A HURRY AND IT DID NOT FINISH.

if you think one is wrong, do not stand there thinking about it. walk into it. walk into it again. THREE TIMES and it gives, and it only does it once so pick your wall."
notes.f2_n1:
A shift handover sheet, the last entry in a different hand:

"Do not worry about talking to yourself down here. Everyone does it.

Worry about the fourth or fifth time, in a room with nobody in it, when something answers. It is polite. It does not stop. You can talk back and I would, because the ones who ignored it got nothing out of it at all."
notes.f2_n2:
A price list, crossed out and rewritten so many times it has gone through:

"the man with the folding table is on every floor from here down and it is the same man. he does not move and he does not mind being come back to. sell him the armour you are not wearing, he does not care that it is yours."
notes.f3_n1:
Pencil on the inside of a break room door, in a careful hand:

"Rule for the break rooms, and I am serious about this one.

Sing in them. Out loud, badly, it does not matter. Do it in three different ones and the building works out what you are doing and joins in, and I have never seen it do anything else that was kind."
notes.f3_n2:
A note taped to a first aid box, no signature:

"You cannot drink a thing twice and you cannot top up what is already full. It will stop you rather than waste it, which is more courtesy than anything else here manages."
notes.f4_n1:
A postcard-sized print, pinned in a break room, one of many:

"Somebody puts a photograph of a beach in every break room in this building and has done for years. Nobody knows who.

Look at it properly. Not a glance - stand and look. I have done it on four floors now and I am fairly sure that on the fifth one I find out who has been putting them up."
notes.f4_n2:
Biro on a doorframe, at the height of somebody sitting on the floor:

"the break rooms are the only rooms where nothing follows you in. whatever is behind you loses you at the door. it is not a trick and they have not closed it, and i think that is because they cannot."
notes.f11_n4:
A withdrawal form, filled in, never submitted, softened with handling:

"Clause 1 says you may withdraw at any time. It does not say how, and there is no office, and there never was.

So say it. Out loud, wherever you are. Once for every clause they have put you under - thirteen of them, thirteen times - and somebody somewhere in this building is obliged to file it. I got to nine."
notes.f13_n4:
Pencil on white wall, low down, in a hand that was in no hurry:

"if you get out and they put you back in, and they will, give them a different name at the desk.

give them Carl. i do not know why it works. the building reacts to it like it has met him and it did not go well for the building."
notes.f1_w:
A laminated card by the door, the first thing anybody sees:

CLAUSE 1: EITHER PARTY MAY WITHDRAW AT ANY TIME.

Under it, in biro, in a hand that pressed hard: "read that again. read it again on every floor. it is the only sentence in here they cannot get at."
notes.f2_w:
A complaints procedure, screwed to the wall, four steps long:

1. RAISE THE MATTER. 2. RAISE IT IN WRITING. 3. RAISE IT IN WRITING AGAIN. 4. THE MATTER IS CLOSED.

Somebody has scratched out all four and written: "or just say I WITHDRAW. out loud. nobody has tried the obvious one."
notes.f3_w:
Biro on the wall beside a kettle:

"there is no form. i looked for the form for two years. there is no office either and there is no desk and there is nobody to hand it to.

so it is not written, is it. it is said. I WITHDRAW. out loud. like that."
notes.f4_w:
A postcard, pinned up, blank on the picture side:

"Dear whoever. I said I WITHDRAW once, on my own, in a corridor, feeling like an idiot. Nothing happened. I said it again the next day.

Keep count. That is all I will say. Keep count."
notes.f5_w:
Chalk on a niche, low down, where somebody sat a long time:

"the occupants down here never said I WITHDRAW. not once, not one of them, and that is the difference between them and you and it is the only difference there is."
notes.f6_w:
A memo, pinned through the plaster:

"Reminder that verbal notification remains valid notification under Clause 1, and that this department has no mechanism whatsoever to receive it.

Please do not test this by saying I WITHDRAW out loud on every floor."

Under it, in biro: "test it."
notes.f7_w:
Four colours of chalk, on a wall that has them now:

"SAY I WITHDRAW. I KNOW. I FELT STUPID TOO. SAY IT ON EVERY FLOOR. IT ADDS UP, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE TRICK, AND NOBODY HAS THE PATIENCE FOR IT."
notes.f8_w:
Scratched into a cooling plate:

"the crews say I WITHDRAW at the end of every shift, all together, as a joke. thirteen years of it.

i do not think it is a joke any more and i do not think they do either."
notes.f9_w:
Chalk, on one side of a break in the floor:

"i said I WITHDRAW eleven times and then the floor came apart and i lost count and i have never been able to make myself start again.

do not lose count. it is thirteen. one for each of them."
notes.f10_w:
A hearing notice, the box for ORAL SUBMISSIONS ticked, then unticked, then ticked again:

"They will not take it in writing. They have never taken anything in writing. Stand up and say I WITHDRAW, thirteen times, one per clause, and there is a man downstairs who is obliged to hear you."
notes.f12_w:
A weather log, pulped, one line still legible in the margin:

"shouted I WITHDRAW into the storm on the ninth day. felt better. said it properly after, on my own, quietly, and that is the one that counted.

thirteen. do not stop at nine like the last one did."
notes.f13_w:
Pencil on white wall, at the height of somebody kneeling:

"if you have been saying I WITHDRAW all the way down, you will know by now.

if you have not: go back up and start. thirteen times, one for each clause. it is not too late and it is never going to be, and that is the one thing they got wrong."
notes.f2_t:
A clocking-in card, still in the rack, punched once:

IN 14:52. OUT ______.

Under it, in biro: "that was forty years ago. it is still that afternoon in here. i have checked against the outside twice and i wish i had not."
notes.f6_t:
A food safety notice, laminated, above a sink:

PERISHABLES MUST BE CONSUMED BY THE DATE SHOWN.

Under it: "nothing perishes in here. the milk has been fine since the acquisition. the tea stays hot. i stopped finding that comforting somewhere around year six."
notes.f10_t:
A docket in a different hand to the rest:

"they say ten of them signed over forty years and you will do the arithmetic and it will not work, because the gaps are not in here. in here it is one afternoon and we are all in it together, the ten of them and me and whoever you are.

the only thing that moves is us."
notes.f3_tos:
A photocopied page from the agreement, Schedule 2, pinned up by somebody who wanted it witnessed:

2.4 The customer grants a non-transferable option to claim, now and forever, their immortal soul.

2.4.1 Should we wish to exercise this option, you agree to surrender your soul, and any claim to it, within 5 (five) working days.

Under it, in biro: "seven and a half thousand people accepted this in one afternoon. it was a games shop. it was april. nobody read it and it went through anyway and that is how we all ended up down here."
notes.f5_tos:
A clause, cut out and taped to a niche:

You may not use this product in the operation of nuclear facilities, aircraft navigation or communication systems, air traffic control, life support machines, or weapons systems.

Under it: "that is a real line out of a real agreement for a music player. somebody sat down and wrote it. somebody else approved it. i think about them constantly and it is the only thing keeping me company."
notes.f8_tos:
Scratched into a plate, in the shaky capitals of somebody on a break:

"CLAUSE 57.10. THE RESTRICTIONS ON USE IN LIFE-CRITICAL SYSTEMS DO NOT APPLY IN THE EVENT OF A WIDESPREAD VIRAL INFECTION CAUSING HUMAN CORPSES TO REANIMATE AND SEEK TO CONSUME LIVING HUMAN FLESH."

"THIS IS ALSO REAL. SOMEBODY DRAFTED IT. WE ARE HOLDING THEM TO IT DOWN HERE AND IT HAS BEEN VERY USEFUL."
notes.f11_tos:
A drafting note, blue pencil, in the margin of a clause about free wireless access:

In exchange for use of the network the customer agrees to 1,000 hours of community service, including but not limited to: cleaning portable lavatories at festivals, scraping chewing gum from public paths, and manually relieving sewer blockages.

"Twenty-two people accepted this in a fortnight," says the note. "Nobody has ever been asked to do the hours. The hours are still owed. I have them on a spreadsheet and I do not know what to do with it."
notes.f12_tos:
A page of the agreement, pulped but legible:

The customer agrees that the first child born to them following acceptance shall be considered an asset of the arbitration and may be called upon.

In the margin, in a hand that pressed very hard: "THIS ONE IS A JOKE. THEY PUT IT IN AS A JOKE, TO PROVE NOBODY READS THESE, AND FOUR BILLION PEOPLE PROVED THEM RIGHT, AND THEN NOBODY TOOK IT BACK OUT.

it is still in. it is clause six. i have checked eleven times."
